However, when I received the order, one pack had a hole and its content had spilled.  1 out 12, still not a bad deal as far as its per-pkg price was concerned.  I threw away 1 package and cleaned 11 others.  By the time I finished all 11 packages in November 2011, I found 2 had already gone bad even though expiration was some time in 2012.  I thought my experience was an isolated case as well, but being apprehensive about my own, I just peeked into this website to see if anyone else had encountered something similar, bingo!  The Subscribe & Save reordering date is approaching, but I just now canceled the subscription.  It's unfortunate that the bulk-buying doesn't seem to work for this item and I need to start buying it from a local grocery store.

My wife bought this because she likes drinking Hemp Milk, but this purchase was bad.  I'm not sure if this is an isolated incident or not, but this experience was not good.  First, when the box arrived, at least one of the containers was broken as there was milk all throughout the box.  We did not report it to Amazon thinking it's just one and we could live with it.  But after a week or so, my wife noticed that at least a couple of the containers were bad already.  The expiration date on the containers say April 2012, but when she opened them to drink them, they were bad.  No where does it say to refrigerate before opening and even when we could find these in the stores, they were not always refrigerated.  We're not sure if we're going to order these again and I'd hope this is an isolated incident.
Used this flavoring with pre-made lip balm base, with no seperation. Flavor held up, no graininess or clouding, not sticky, didn't burn off, and smelled great too.

Maruchan's Akai Kitsune Udon is a nice treat. Easy to make, but containing a lot of flavor. It's the perfect thing when you're stuck outside Japan, but want Kitsune Udon, or if you are just seeking a great snack to warm you through.

After living in Japan for three years, it is quite difficult to live without noodles in the US. These hit the spot every time and I look forward to my shipments when they arrive. If you want authentic Japanese Ramen, Yakisoba and Udon, give these a try. You won't be disappointed.

I've really enjoyed these noodles and used to get them at my local Asian supermarket. However, they don't carry these noodles anymore so I am extremely happy to know that I can get them here. Delicious as usual!  I just wished shipping was not so ridiculously high!

This is one of the best tasting instant udon I've had!!

I love the flavor and the texture of the noodles!!

It's a great buy!

I was addicted to this kind of instant noodle when I was in Japan 2 years ago and since then I have been looking everywhere to find an instant kitsune udon. Needless to say, I was very happy to find this on Amazon. The noodles reheat to be perfectly soft, the fried tofu square is heavenly, and the soup base is also amazing - just as I remember it in Japan. It certainly isn't healthy (97% of your daily sodium in one of these bowls), but it's perfect as a treat. Even though I am giving this product 5 stars (because the instant noodles themselves deserve it), I will say that this product took nearly 2 weeks to get to me and they are kind of expensive with the shipping costs added on, so this was a bit annoying. But next time I will just buy these in bulk.

For anyone who hasn't had this type of instant noodle, buy it! Seriously, it will take you to a whole new level of deliciousness.

I have never had 'real' ramen before so I cant say how close this is to that. But I have eaten a lot of different types of instant ramen. Most are too spicy (no flavor, just spicy) or lack a certain something. THIS stuff right here is just freaking pure win. I found this brand from the ramen eater website, though it was a different flavor he recomended(soba). I went to my local koreon/asian supermarket and found only this flavor. I grabbed just one bowl which I am now eating ... Im really glad I did. For something instant its really good.

If youre curious what it tastes like, its a miso soup kinda taste.

A few years ago, my cats and I relocated to Germany. And while my four-pawed trio generally took the move in stride and quickly adapted to their new home in a manner that filled me with new love and admiration for them, there is one item now, several years later, still sorely lacking in their lives: Pounce Tuna Treats! For as long as we've been together (and in the case of the two females, that means their entire life), there has never been a better way to reward them or just show them my affection than by giving them some of these - my cats loved them, and I knew that due to the treats' many healthy ingredients I was actually doing something good for my kitties in addition to making them happy. But Pounce is nowhere to be found on the shelves of German stores! My cats are not overly picky in their food choices; they willingly accept almost everything appearing in their food bowls. But they have made it quite clear to me that a decent substitute for Pounce is yet to be discovered. In the meantime, what's a poor cat owner to do???

The only good comment I can give on these treats is that my cat loves this stuff, and its really cheap! I can usually find these treats for under two dollars at the store and lasts a long time because I won't give my cats very many at a time. I only give them no more than 1-2 a day as apposed to the recommended 6-8, which is just crazy. It would be nice if pounce treats had healthier ingredients, maybe some vitamins or a dental cleanser, but no, its just junk food. They smell really gross to me but my cat loves it. My biggest reason for not liking this treat, aside from the terrible ingredients and smell, is the fact that it is soft and chewy and not crunchy. Soft treats reek havoc on pet teeth as the sticky particles just sit on their teeth and gums and just rot there. Crunchy treats at least crunch off and don't stick to their teeth. For a really good dental product, I recommend Crunch N' Clean brand with DentaShield. Greenies brand doesn't have a beneficial dental ingredient either, but they are crunchy and they do have vitamins in them, so they are much better than these.

Pros: taste and price
Cons: smell, nutrition, and texture
I always bought these at Food Lion and they stopped selling them.  My cat loves these treat and I get them in Tuna, Caribbean Catch and Seafood.
I purchased this decaf espresso so I could enjoy a cup in the evening with my new espresso maker. I love it, great flavor.
We have used several brands of coffee, many flavored in different ways but feel this coffee has been an excellent addition to those that tempt our taste buds.

I am very picky with coffee.  I had been trying to find maple coffee forever.  I found this company and just gave them a try.  So glad I did.  Now I have bought more bags like this one in different flavors.  I have found when I want to buy flavored decaf that it is practically impossible to find good flavors that actually taste good.  They have so many to choose from I have trouble deciding.  They have awesome customer service.  This is were I am buying my coffee now!  Highly Recommend!!!

Don't buy this in hot weather or it will arrive a liquified gooey mess. No packaging provisions were made for the fact that this is a meltable product.Ridiculous to sell this online is such provision is not made.

We have had these wonderful caramels from other sources and they were great.
These came smelling old-putred....we think from the butter turning old. There was a grease or something all over the packaging. So bad we had to throw away...not even usable in a sauce.
Save your money!!!!!!!
We buy LOTS of things from Amazon. Almost everything is great. But shame on them for selling this garbage. Hope they post this so we can help fellow users avoid rancid product.

Summary: a lot of $ for a delicious product!
Text: I received this as a gift, and did not realize how expensive this little package of caramels was, but they were DELICIOUS! I did not cook with them or bake with them so I cannot say what they would be like in that scenario. I can say they were very delicious just by themselves. In response to the reviews that the caramels were putrid or greasy, I must admit they were greasy and this is probably due to the butter used as a main ingredient. Overall, despite the fact that the grease from the caramels permeated the package, these things are quite tasty. I have not decided if this makes them worth the price, but the caramels are of the highest quality. So you decide! (Four stars for the price!)

When I received the news that I had to put one of my dogs on this special low fat diet my heart sunk. I envisioned more money down the drain for a specialty food that my pets wouldn't touch.  To my surprise they LOVE this food, even more then their usual Science Diet.  Also the dry variety of this low fat dog food makes a great treats that my dogs don't turn their noses up to making it handy for doling out very controlled amount of small sized treats.

I have tried many different rubs in competition for my BBQ and there is no match to Rods Rub.  I put a very generous rub on before I cook it and then I sprinkle the rub on the pork right after it has been pulled.  By the way.  It is also great on Popcorn.

Summary: Quality ingredients - good brand, and she LIKES it!
Text: Our little 15 pounder, AbiGirl the wonder BOM (beagle/pomeranian), is a VERY picky eater, and we search the world over for quality ingredients that have added nutritional value. While they might seem pricey, you get what you pay for- We feel the value is fair for the quality of the product. We'd rather feed quality raw foods to keep her healthy- because health is priceless... Stella and Chewy's understands the importance of a raw diet that is easy to handle and dispense... these little freeze dried steaks make AWESOME treats if broken into pieces, as well as a nice easy dinner if served whole. Terrific for traveling, convenient, really nutritious, and - most importantly- Abi loves them... no turned up nose EVER when we hand her a Stella and Chewy's steak!

Great food for the Master's best friend it's all natural and my dog love's it. Before we tried these she had trouble keeping other dog food digested and she would leave accidents on the floor. Now she's trouble free and gets the vitamins and required nourishment she needs.

My 9 month old Yorkie puppy is a finicky eater.  When he is in the mood, he gobbles down Stella & Chewy's dreeze dried patties.  He likes the beef the best, but will occasionally eat the duck-duck and chicken.  I have a friend who has larger dogs and they are on a raw food diet and love these patties.  Their coats are so shiny and I have found that my Yorkie's coat is beginning to also shine.

Summary: Finicky senior kitty loves Stella and Chewy's products
Text:
Stella & Chewy's Freeze Dried Dog Food for Adult Dogs, Lamb Patties, 32 Count, 16 Ounce Bag

First time reviewing on Amazon so not sure on inserting links, but Stella and Chewy's is a terrific product. I was always curious about "raw foods" but was also very leery. For those in the fence who are interested for their cats or dogs, this product removes all the guess work. I am down to one cat now, a 17year basically healthy kitty, known by her finicky nature as she's had some health issues. I had tried another product which she sniffed at and walked away from, this stuff she LOVES even pulling the bag out from the cabinet. I give her about 1/4 a patty, with a traditional canned food, and she generally inhales it. If I put her bowl down without it, she sits and looks at me, plainly demanding "where's my Stella's" and does not eat until it's added.
4 stars as I have only been using it for about a month, but her coat and behavior is great, she's back watching out the window in the morning, she has tried the chicken and lamb so far and loves both. Patties are easily broken up and can be fed as treats or as a meal.
So far purchased locally but anticipate purchasing here, I got samples from a local pet shop initially.

My dog LOVES this stuff. He wasn't eating his regular food and I got this and crumbled one burger on top and he attacked it! Also he is a nervous stomach kind of dog but there was barely any upset when I introduced this food. Really amazing.

After feeding frozen raw for years, i got tired of preplanning every meal (and sometimes forgetting...) so i switched to dehydrated raw--much easier! Just add water!
So I researched a lot of dehydrated raw dog foods and this one gets dogfoodadviser-dot-com five star rating. Really an excellent product.

BUT--my small (20lb), moderately active, adult dog would eat 6 burgers per day. 12 burgers sells for $12+ per bag! (This item I'm reviewing is the double bag--a teeny bit less $) So I'd be paying around $40+ per week to feed him. It's pretty excessive. I'm not sure how they stay in business with these prices. Do they only sell to people with tea cup sized dogs? Not sure. But I know I wouldn't feed a Large or Giant dog this stuff. OMG it'd cost a fortune.

Anyway, if you have the money, it's a really great product. If they ever lower the price, I'll give it 5 stars.

I order one bag of the freeze dried beef patties to try.  I found these better than other freeze dried raw food products and my dogs loved them.  They come in a form I can store on the shelf and are easy to break up and mix with a little warm water to re-hydrate.  My only "beef" is the cost.  I would like to have some of this on hand for emergencies or travel but it is way to costly to feed on a daily basis.

Summary: my finicky eaters LOVE this product
Text: sooooo healthy AND my mamas who refuse almost all food for the first few days after whelping will eat this...also the first solid food I feed my puppies.

I'd been searching for a while for a food my picky little maltipoo would eat. Someone suggested a raw diet. I'd been trying the frozen Primal Raw food (also very good but requires enough forethought to defrost each day's portion overnight in the fridge) for a while and got a sample of this stuff. Not only did my dog eat it, he snatched right out of my hand and devoured it! He absolutely loves these. After just a week on this food, I can already tell he's feeling better. The sales clerk at the local doggie boutique said to start with these dry and work up to re-hydrating the patties.

Summary: Toy Poodle ATE IT!  Couldn't believe my eyes
Text:
I received a sample here in Los Angeles, and I couldn't BELIEVE that my toy poodle actually ate this! She is the PICKIEST, worst eater, ever! I've tried every dried and wet food imaginable, but the only thing she'll eat is real chicken or the occasional filet mignon piece. I've talked to a few poodle owners who have the same (exact) feeding problem, but I can't keep giving her chicken because I know she's not getting the proper vitamins/nutritional value.

The food looks a little gross, but hey, if she eats, I'm thrilled.

I actually run the pieces under warm water in my hand, then break it up with a fork, add a tiny bit more water, place in the micro for 10 seconds (only) and it's good to go.

I say give it a try!

My dog loves this stuff and I quite like it myself. I always try any food I'm going to give to my dog first. If its horrid I won't feed it to him. The difficulty is that I don't find most dog food that tasty and in consequence he mainly eats what we do. We eat lots of fish and he loves it. Turbot is his favorite but it's very expensive and sometimes it's not available at my store. Trout is also hard to find and getting all the bones out Is a pain. He's not a great fan of Talapia, or most farmed fish now I come to think of it. As for meat, he just loves a nice bit of steak. He prefers New York over Fillet which is strange, but there's no accounting for taste, right? Anyway back to this dried food. Dried is right! You really have to moisten this stuff. For a hurried snack rushing to work, I usually just pour some cold milk over it and scarf it down, but it's best if you save a little gravy from your Sunday roast.

Summary: My Dog Is Addicted To These
Text: I'm always on the hunt for a dog treat that my picky manchester will eat.  Most everything he will just turn his nose up and walk away.  One day I explained my dilemma to a sales lady at a dog product sales website and she sent me a free sample of Stella and Chewy's Beef Cookies.  Well, she knew what she was doing because my dog went crazy for these treats.  She made us a customer for life.  He is literally hooked on these!  I crumble one up in this dog food at every meal.  In fact, he will not touch his dog food if I don't put one of these cookies in it.  They are so expensive, and I've tried to break him away from them.  I've tried other treats.  I've tried looking for treats with similar ingredients.  He won't accept anything else.  So, now I am forced to keep him stocked in Stella and Chewy's Beef Cookies.  If you have a picky eater and you don't mind the extra cost, try these.

Summary: Our Long Haired Doxies love em'
Text: We have two long haired miniture Doxies, one year old.  They have been raised on Natures Select and Stella & Chewy's since they were 3 months.  They both are healthy, lean and have really smooth and silky feeling hair.  Don't know how much can be credited to their diet, but I'm sure it helps.  Only con is these are a bit costly, but worth it.

It's nice to have a quality freeze dried raw product to feed my raw food eating dog when on the road.  Break it up, add some water, wait a bit, feed the dog.  Couldn't be any easier.  The price is great too compared to others.

I have fed Stella and Chewy's to my six year old 14 pound Pekingese (his normal weight - a muscular, active dog) over the past year and he loves it. His coat is glossy, he is full of energy and has no health problems. In general, he is very picky when offered dog food and I have offered him many, many kibbles and moist dog foods (almost all were rejected). His appetite is excellent for roast chicken, grilled salmon, salads, etc. He also eats a semi-moist dog kibble daily (small dish). Very pleased.

I have two cavalier king charles spaniels who are pretty picky eaters.  The only way to get them to eat is to mix this freeze dried in with it.  Personally I take the time to mix in a little hot water to reconstitute it and then mix it with kibble.  My wife just sprinkles some on dried.  Either way they love it.  It's a little pricey, but we only use half a disk at a time to mix in with kibble.  So it lasts.

I was looking for a different S & C product and couldn't find it so ordered this. The dogs love the patties so I'm quite happy with the product. Still, I wish I could find the other product that my dogs were absolutely crazy for - it'd be nice to see a photo of the product itself rather than just the bag.

The patties get mushy if any water is introduced (humidity) so keep that bag closed tight.

Great dog food!! keeps well and my dog loves it! He likes some flavors better than others but then changes his mind and eats the one he didn't like before with gusto. And it is good for him.  Great to take when you travel

I have an extremely picky 20 lbs French Bulldog/Boston, it took a year to find a food that she would actually eat on a regular basis...that is up until 2 weeks ago, when she just refused to eat. I went to a wonderful natural dog food place and they gave me samples of this along with others. To my shock she gobbled it ALL up and then proceeded to look for more! It is very pricey, but is worth it! It recommends feeding a 20 lbs about 5 pattys/day. To cut that down, I have been feeding her 1-2 pattys soaked in water (then mushed up) and mixed into her dry food. I highly recommend this product (and Dr. Becker Bites - treats) for any picky eaters and caring owners!

My Boston Terrier LOVES Stella and Chewy's.  We do feed her the frozen raw patties, but use these as a treat or for fast or on the go feeding.  She gobbles them up like they are a treat and begs for more!  It is hard not to feed her more than the recommended amount because she would eat more if given to her.  I love how they are so easy to take with us and no need for dishes or cleanup!  I also love that I save a couple bucks getting them here rather than at my local pet food shop.

Summary: The Only Thing My Chihuahua Will Eat
Text: This was a pricey gamble because my 4lb chihuahua is a very PICKY eater. She now gets excited at meal times & wont eat anything but this food. Yes its expensive but its cheaper then having to throw out food cause she wont eat it & shes not that big so she eats only 2 patties a day max. If you have a small picky eater this is GREAT & seems to be very healthy. If you have a large dog this might be a healthy thing to add to their dryfood (not to mention a nice way to spice up their food). I highly suggest the freeze dried Duck, Duck, Goose Stella & Chewy's version. I tried the frozen version & my dog wasnt as interested.

This stuff is way too expensive for what it is. I mean, seriously, how do people actually eat this. I had it this morning with some poached eggs and even a healthy amount of hollandaise couldn't make it taste good.
Very tasty item, although I enjoy it more with some veggies, but overall great sauce, and quality product.

Annie Chun's Peanut Sesame Chow Mein Noodles makes an excellent lunch or dinner. The noodles cook quickly, and the peanut sauce is perfectly savory and sweet. It's rich enough to be a meal. I add tofu and frozen veggies to make it more into a meal.

Unlike Simply Asia,Annie Chun's Chinese meals are made here in the US. The sauces are of higher quality,as well. Annie Chun's is based in the Bay Area (Novato or San Rafael) The organic Peanut Sesame Chow Mein tastes as good as her other excellent meals. One can enjoy chop suey in the comfort of one's own home!

I previously read submitted reviews, and I should have listened. Especially to the one that stated he didn't get the organic product shown in the picture. I too did not get the organic product. I have seen it in the stores, and it has a much lower sodium content per serving. I haven't been able to find it in a while so I thought I would buy it through Amazon.

The product was the old stuff with an expiration date of 6 months from now. Usually the product in the store carries and expiration date of a year, so that tells you something right away.

The noodles are okay. My family is not that particular, so it's a good side dish on ocassion. If you are an expert on peanut noodles, this dish is not for you. It's slightly gummy and thick.

Summary: Not as heathful of a snack as you might think
Text:
The good news is that the peanut butter flavor of these granola bars is really good. When I first bit into one, I immediately thought I was eating a peanut butter cookie. They're very reminiscent of a Girl Scout peanut butter cookie, minus the cream filling of course.

That brings me to the bad news. While a serving of these granola bars has a tad less fat and sugar than a cookie, the difference isn't great. If you don't believe me, just look at the nutritional information for a Nutter Butter cookie here. That doesn't mean that this isn't a good snack to have on occasion. These are a healthier alternative than a candy bar, for example, but they're really not much different than a cookie. In other words, even though most people would equate granola bars with health food, one must be careful not to overindulge in these.

These granola bars are twin-wrapped and contain 90 calories per bar.  They're very crunchy, but the peanut butter flavor is intense and fresh, not overly sweet like a cookie tends to be...perfect for curbing a craving for real peanut butter.  These are so good that you'll likely to be disappointed at not eating the crumbs from each bite.

I have been eating these for years and still love them.  This is my favorite variety and if you love peanut butter, you'll love it also.  Very crunchy and a good mid-day snack, certainly better an a candy bar or the other stuff available in most office vending machines.  Great for road trips.  Is there anything these bars can't do? ;)

These are a great mid day snack. Love that there are two bars in each packet--pair these with a glass of milk and you have a wonderful, healthy mid day treat. In both bars, there are 190 calories and 7 grams of fat, plus 2 grams of fiber. They are the perfect solution to satisfying a sweet tooth!! The subscribe and save price makes the 6 packages a great deal, especially when it is on sale (frequently).
I must not have noticed the "crunchy" part in the title, cause they are very hard.  I mean they are still good, but I just wasn't expecting them to be that hard.

Summary: The brightest star in the Heaven of Nature Valley Granola Bars - which are the best in the Universe!!!
Text:
For an earlier reviewer, I don't see anywhere on the package where it is claimed that this is a "health food". However, whole grains should be an important part of our diets, and I'll bet your Girl Scout cookies and the Nutter Butters are not made with whole grains. I love peanut butter and I really appreciate how much peanut butter flavor there in these granola bars, but the calories per serving are only 180. For anyone who has never had a Nature Valley granola bar, they come 2 in a pouch and 2 are considered one serving. In size I would say the pouch would equal 4 small/medium cookies. A tip on the crunchiness: These almost crumble when you bite into them, and depending on where you are eating, that can be inconvenient. Here is what I do with ALL of the NV granola bars, whether I'm at a table, in a recliner, or driving down the road. First, I break both the bars into 3 crosswise. I then break each of those thirds once, crosswise. Then I open the pouch along the lengthwise seam. There are far fewer "crumbs" left in the pouch then you would have created preparing to and eating them any other way I can think of.
Thank you AMAZON, and thanks for the new subscription service. I live in a very remote area and it is a real crap shoot what flavors will be in the stores any given week.

Summary: TASTES GREAT AND LASTS WAY BEYOND NOON
Text:
I am not a good label reader nor a health nut person but I do know what I like. These are great!

I started buying a case of these - looked ok and they had peanut butter on granola bars. What is not to like? I am 78 and we all need a little roughage. So I ordered them. Now I have reordered and the thing I like best is they are filling. I have a cup of hot chocolate with a little coffee in it - at my desk - with a Peanut Butter Nature Valley Bar. It works for me. (You can dunk them when no one is watching)

Thinking of trying the other ones but these seem to be a winner. They are messy so you need a napkin to clean up - but try them.

Let me know if you have tried the others!
I LOVE these bars because they are dairy, rice AND gluten free (I am allergic to all of those. They fill me up and keep me going longer than most other granola bars do, and they also taste delicious.

As someone else mentioned, the taste is somewhat reminiscent of the peanut butter Girl Scout sandwich cookies.  As a college student, I just throw some of these in my backpack and when hunger strikes these are ready at hand.  I like them because they don't make me feel sick after eating a bunch of them like potato chips do.  Also, because they are whole grain, they supply good, long-lasting energy.  I ordered the variety pack first, but found myself wishing the cinnamon and honey ones were peanut butter.  Needless to say, I was very happy when this peanut butter only pack went on sale.  You can have your variety- I'll take my peanut butter!

Summary: delicious product at a great price!
Text: Always love to keep these on hand to grab on the go. The price kept going up at my local grocery and at the supermarket, so I figured I'll try amazon to see if it's cheaper here. MUCH cheaper here, and if you choose "subscribe and save" you save even more! Had to buy 6 boxes at once, but that's only 36 packs of bars (boxes say 12 bars, but they're packed 2 bars per pack, with a whole pack usually eaten at once). Would definitely check prices here again before I purchase it next.
Not chewy at all which I would like for a granola bar.  The name does say they are crunchy which they are.

The bars are hardened, clearly stale and taste almost chemically (likely from the staleness). The worst part is there is so much to throw out. This is gross. Must be a bad batch or the way they're stored that made them this way. Beware of buying in such quantities if you haven't purchased a particular food product from Amazon before.

What a perfect extra for the lunchbox. Arrived fresh
and tasted very good. None were broken. Granola cravings
solved. I will order again. (Have ordered before)

Summary: I love these - but the ones from Amazon were stale tasting
Text: I get these from the grocery store all the time, so getting them in bulk made sense. The first one I ate tasted stale - it was super hard to bite into and had that stale texture, like moisture got into it. I thought "oh no!" my bars had been compromised! The next one I ate was totally normal - crunchy and fresh. ??? I would say about half of the shipment was stale (although the expiration date was for next year) When I open a stale one, I give it to my husband who doesnt seem to care as much, but he definately notices the weird texture also.

Summary: Thrilled that these are gluten free!
Text: These aren't the healthiest of snacks, but they are conveniently portable and tasty--and gluten free. They're one of the few easily-available granola bars out there that have no gluten OR whole nuts/seeds (thank you, gluten intolerance and diverticulosis). I kind of wish they would package the individual bars separately for when it's just me, but they're a perfect quick snack for two people.

ProfileName: G. Proulx "Up to my Neck in Tech"
Summary: Great for lunch packers, a little hard
Text:
I have these on subscribe and save since we go through so many. They are a great, easy, snack to either pack in lunches, or to grab when you are on the go. Sure, they may not be a health food, but at least they are a filling snack that can tide you over to the next meal.

They are quite hard so it'd be nice if they were a little softer, but nonetheless I still enjoy them. I enjoy how they have real peanut butter slathered around the outside of them. Overall, a tasty snack for a good price, especially when you use subscribe and save.

Summary: I crave these more than candy bars
Text:
They are THAT good. They are a mouthful of crunchy, peanutty, deliciousness! In fact, I went through an entire box in less than one week. If you really want to be bad, smear some peanut butter on these, and you'll be hooked for life.

I actually ordered a case of the same type of bars, but the Barbara's Bakery brand because I like eating organic. They're really good, too, but I must say that they're not as scrumptious as these.
Many of our troops try to eat healthy and would rather have granola bars than candy and this was a great item to buy in bulk from Amazon to send to them.

I can barely eat one of these without risk of breaking a tooth.
I think they have been sitting around too long.
I was expecting crunchy. I received rocks.

These Nature Valley "Crunch Granola Bars, Peanut Butter" are a tasty mid-afternoon snack and are filling enough to hold me over until dinner. These are, as the name suggests, very crunchy and can be a little messy (crumbs) when eating. Since these are somewhat dry, they also travel well in the heat or in a pocket.

My kids will eat these in place of candy, which is another plus, but these are too hard for my wife who has sensitive teeth.

Highly Recommended!

CFH

I absolutely love these bars. Like the other review said it is gluten and dairy free which is hard to find these types of food that actually taste good! They may be a little high in fat and calories but they fill me up most days. They are a bit hard to bite into at times, but great on the go bar for breakfast. They do make quite the mess when eating in the car but that is easy to get over! Great for the price too.

I tried these based on other reviews and am glad I did. However, I am a little disappointed in that the peanut butter flavor isn't stronger. But otherwise, they taste great and are a great alternative to snacks at work or on the road. I like these a lot but would love them if the flavor were stronger.

Text:
I am a nurse that works night shift and travels frequently. Between the two, I have a funky sleep schedule and sometimes go through periods of extreme insomnia.

I haven't had any side effects, but better safe than sorry.

Summary: adds flavor and nutrition to any breakfast dish, so far
Text:
I purchased this whole grain teff on a special deal here on Amazon, without having tried it previously or having any idea if I'd like it, but so far I'm loving it.

I haven't tried the recipes on the back of the package yet for teff porridge or teff pudding (they look very tasty, but require longer stove-top cooking and more attention than I usually want to invest unless I've already tried the result and know for a fact that it's worth the time and trouble).

However, when I added a generous sprinkling of teff to a bowl of McCann's Quick & Easy steel-cut Irish oats before adding the boiling water and following the microwave directions on that package, the result was spectacularly good (much better than the oats alone, even when cooked with my usual cinnamon, dried fruits, and nuts).

And then I tried 'blooming' a half-cup of teff in about a cup of boiling water (I ended up simmering it in the microwave for a few minutes, since I was impatient) and stirring that into a standard pancake recipe (using a generic reduced-fat baking mix). The pancake batter looked thin and a little gloppy, but they cooked up beautifully and had a wonderful, nutty (but not heavy) taste. After I made the first few pancakes, I didn't even bother dropping frozen wild blueberries onto the pancake batter anymore, since the teff made the pancakes tasty all alone. The texture of the pancakes was light, but spongy, and they're just as good warmed up in the microwave a few days later.

One of these days I'll work up the nerve to try cooking the teff all alone, but in the meantime I'm adding it to other cooked or baked products at every opportunity, and I haven't been disappointed in the result yet.

Try the pudding, or add the grain to a mix for breakfast or as a side dish - it's healthy and it tastes good.

I heard about this product, but I couldn't find it anywhere in my local store. I was glad to find it at the Amazon. It came quickly. It is so fine, I don't know wether I need to rinse it or not. Teff is a small grain, smaller even than quinoa, rich in fiber as well as flavor. It's the basic grain of Ethiopian cooking. Teff flour is used to make the sour sponge bread served in all Ethiopian restaurants. Teff whole grain can be cooked as a breakfast porridge or as a dinner course rather like polenta, either soft or solid.

I picked up "Bob's Red Mill Teff" at my local grocery, in response to my teenage son's interest in cooking grains from around the world. There are two adequate recipes on the package, but we didn't follow either exactly. In the dinner recipe, we used cardamon in place of cloves and dried apricots in place of dates. If you've ever cooked grits or polenta, you won't find teff difficult at all. Check the other brands of teff here on amazon if you decide to order some; "Bob's" appears to be the most expensive.

Summary: Teff is a new staple in my household

I prefer berries of some sort. At this point, my consumption of both granola and milk have markedly decreased. I do not water down the cereals with milk and fine the flavor greatly enhanced.

I had no idea what Teff was before I spotted a single bag in the grains section of Whole Foods a year or two ago.

I had no idea what to do with it, and I didn't know how it was supposed to taste. I was intrigued. The whole grain looks like tiny poppyseeds, but brown.

I decided to cook it in my ricemaker, using the package directions to estimate how much Teff, and how much water. While it was cooking, it smelled great--the problem with the ricemaker was that it overflowed and stuck all over the lid parts of the ricemaker.

When it was finished cooing, I opened it, and the teff looked slightly puffier than the uncooked teff. I put some into a bowl, put some yogurt on it, and ate it (just like a cooked hot-grain cereal). It was great!

My lesson--cook a whole bag of the raw Teff over low heat in a large pot on top of the stove, instead of in the ricemaker, stir frequently, and when it's done, let it cool a bit, and then, spoon 3/4 to 1 cup portions into sandwich baggies (Put the baggies into a measuring cup while you spoon the warm/hot teff into the baggie). Get as much air out of the bag as you can before sealing it closed, and then freeze the bags.

In order to use the frozen Teff (as a breakfast meal), take the frozen bag of teff, unseal it, put it into a bowl (while still in the baggie), and microwave it for about 1.5 minutes. Empty the bag into the bowl, add milk, yogurt, or whatever you like, and enjoy!

Mushy and very strong flavored, Teff is not a grain most people would like simply boiled. On the other hand, it is so nutritious (see below), that I tried to work it into my diet. Boil 6 cups water; add 2 cups quinoa, 2/3 cup Teff, 3 tbsp fenugreek seeds. Simmer 20 minutes. Serve with poppy seed dressing and sprinkle of Chia seeds. I highly recommend Bob's Red Mill Teff (which I purchased on sale at my local grocery).

First of all, there's no "chicken" in the ingredients at all. The closest we have to anything animal is "CSC shortening" -- I don't know what that particular product is but much of the time shortenings are trans-fats which are extremely unhealthy for you. The last ingredient listed is "Other Spices" which is often a codeword for MSG.

Basically, as far as I can tell from the product list and taste of the final product this is a jar full of tumeric and celery and onion powder. When you use it to make broth you end up with a substance that's the same color, opacity, and viscosity as orange juice and that tastes not at all of chicken broth. It also has a film of semisolid granules floating at the top that have the consistency of those little orange fish eggs you sometimes find on sushi (my guess is that it's either the shortening or poorly dissolved celery powder) that would have to be skimmed off of any soup you made if you wanted people to actually eat it.

The next two products I will try in my search for a low/no sodium chicken base is Herb Ox's Sodium Free Chicken Bullion (which potassium cholride as a substitute for salt and monoammonium glutamate as a sub for MSG, an imperfect solution to just leaving them out) and if that doesn't taste good then I'll probably end up with the "low" sodium Better Than Bullion chicken stock paste product, which I know at least tastes right even though it still has an awful lot of salt in there and is much more expensive than regular bullion.

This is a great gum as far as the natural ingredients. It does not contain any aspartame or manitol, but unfortunately the flavor does not last. Within about 5 minutes of putting in your mouth, it loses flavor. I would not repurchase.

Xylitol is fantastic for dental health.

This gum is great because it doesn't contain any of the less-than-ideal additives (like aspartame-nutrasweet, saccharin, sorbitol, mannitol, artificial flavors, artificial colors, etc.) that make most other gums and mints, even those with xylitol as an ingredient, problematic.

The flavor is nice, the texture is fine, and it lasts for at least 15 minutes (which is all I want it to do).

Note that this gum is manufactured in Finland and the xylitol is sourced from birch wood [also, it's non-GMO (not genetically modified)], which is not the case with some other brands of xylitol products, which source their xylitol from China and/or from corn.

I wish that this gum could be purchased in smaller amounts, because the price for this company's giant containers/packs is quite a lot of money to spend on something you've never tried before. I'm sure more people would give them a try if they packaged this in one 30-piece, portable little cardboard box, and sold it as an "add-on" product at Amazon for 2 dollars or something, just so folks could try it out.

Summary: Great flavor for being sugar free
Text: Although these are sugar free, they don't taste it and they don't leave a weird aftertaste in your mouth when you're done with them. The taste lasts longer then the Glee Gum I purchased, which has sugar in it. Great for diabetics and anyone else who doesn't want to chew on sugar!!
Better value, softer, and longer lasting flavor than Spry. Container is easier to use than Spry. I have subscribed to it.

Summary: no sugar, no aspertame, long flavor
Text: We wanted to find a gum that did not contain aspertame and Xylichew fits the bill.  The flavor lasts for a long time too.  We have tried a few flavors and the Spearmint is our favorite.
Excellent gum, but flavor does not last as long as some gums that I have bought in local stores. I will continue to buy Xylichew, however, because it does not contain aspartame.

The flavor of these is great, but it doesn't last as long as the leading sugar-free gum and it isn't as "juicy."  If you've ever tried the small square-shaped gum in the small candy machines then you will know what kind of fleeting flavor to expect from this.  I have also noticed its effect when you chew more than 2 or 3 pieces within a few hours...it can cause some serious bloating! If you want something to chew on for 10 to 30 minutes after a meal then try this.  If you are looking for a substitute for candy or something to keep you awake in the afternoon, you may want to proceed with extreme caution or get something else.  I wouldn't recommend these as something you can indulge in constantly throughout the day like tic-Tacs or Junior Mints.  However, as something to chew 1 or 2 pieces of after a meal for 10 minutes, I have no problems with them.

xylichew is the best natural gum on the market . the xylitol that is in this gum for sweetening comes from the birch tree bark . beware of what i call imitation xylitol that is made from gmo corn stalks , it's very unhealthy .

bp

Summary: Great flavor but does not last long
Text: I buy this gum at my local heath food store for $15.00 a bottle. It tastes great but does not last 15 minutes. I eat 3 pieces at one time. It still only lasts about 20 minutes. When you keep it in your mouth for more than 1 hour it starts to fall apart. I would recommend buying it if you like xylitol gum. If not try Spry gum. It last a little longer and has lots of flavors.

I like Xylichew because I can defend it as a health food. The xylitol supposedly reduces cavities, and the gum does not contain anything harmful unlike Xyloburst and Spry, which have a carcinogen, titanium dioxide, that is thought to cause cancer in human beings. Those products made in China for Americans should not be purchased by intelligent Americans. Titanium Dioxide is nothing more than a food coloring. So Xylichew will not be perfectly white. If this causes your brain to explode, then you had better buy Spry instead and subject your body to the ravages of cancer.

The flavor does not last forever, because it's natural, but so what? One way to counter that would be to pop a mint in your mouth while chewing and let the gum absorb the mint flavor.

Summary: Tea was very good taste & aroma.
Text:
The tea was excellent. And easy openning. This tea's aroma and taste was excellent.
Only disadvantage is that the packaging is long ago.
This tea has been packed the last in Aug.2009, tea was best before Aug. 2012. I received 21. May. I had just left for a period of three months only.

The operative thought is bitter. Nuance? There is a salty background.

This was a one time purchase. Folger's is even better.

Brazilian Santos Whole Bean Coffe.not good.
You recive what you pay. My Solois 500
coffee machine normaly produce delishes coffeee..
I try to change grinder set up, still do not have any good coffe
