Text: It's the curcumin plant pigment which gives this spice its characteristic golden yellow/orange color. I've tried several different varieties of turmeric, and Frontier Organic comes out on top in terms of quality, appearance, and taste. What you're getting here is the Alleppey variety, which recorded maximum color in chemical analyses of turmeric rhizomes (not to get too science-y...basically, this is "the good stuff"). A simple google search will yield a wealth of info explaining the numerous health benefits of this powerful golden powder. For those not familiar or who have never tasted it before, turmeric has a deep, earthy flavor that is somewhat pungent/bitter. It's somewhat of an acquired taste, depending on who you ask--some say they can barely taste it, that it mostly just stains everything they eat (along with their tupperware!) with its trademark bright golden tinge. I feel good about cooking with it because of the anti-inflammatory effects. Also, on the beauty front, I often use it topically (as a homemade facial mask, mixed together with a bit of chickpea flour and almond oil) to maintain glowing skin. You are paying more for organic, yes, but if you use a lot of turmeric (i.e. in your everyday meals), then I happen to think it's worth it because you're consuming the spice at a much higher volume than if you were to only use it sparingly. I believe you can get 3 bags (so that's 3 lbs.) of the non-organic turmeric from Frontier for about $20, which is clearly a sizable price difference. It's a personal choice, obviously. I opt for organic with several spices, only because I do consume certain ones regularly. (Keep in mind that organic doesn't really mean "better" so much as it simply ensures that the food is grown without the use of pesticides, synthetic fertilizers, sewage sludge, genetically modified organisms, or ionizing radiation.)  I've repurchased the 1-lb. bag at least a half dozen times already--I'm replenishing my supply today in fact; just ordered a fresh bag--and I will continue buying Frontier Organic because I find the quality and flavor to be superior. I would absolutely recommend incorporating this spice into your life if you haven't done so already; try it!

Text:
CLAXTON FRUIT CAKE (3lb.) AMAZON REVIEW

Credit cards are weird. I mean, you wann 'em, and if you play your cards right over time, you gott 'em. But ahh, the catch. If you don't use 'em, you might just lose 'em. What's all of this have to do with fruitcake? Well, sans any fruitcake jokes, please stand by...

Recently, I've lost a couple of hard-earned credit cards, due to "lack of use." Really? I mean, really?!! Is this what America has come down to? I do all I can to establish or re-establish my basic U.S. dollar, human worthiness for unsolicited credit card offers, only to get a few, only to lose out when I don't use them for awhile? Without warning. ZAP! They're gone. Seems "they" want you to have the cards, but if you go overboard with them, they hound you to no end, but then, if you don't use them, or even forget you had one, they cut you off and cancel your card. Fruitcake, I say! Fruitcake!

So it was, after I learned these things and more, that I told myself, with one card, hey, I better USE this or LOSE it. Having nothing really I wanted or needed at the time (all you NEED is love...), I ordered this product from Amazon. Through one of those cards I feared losing soon, unless I used it. But after ordering, receiving, and trying this particular product (some supposed "gourmet" fruitcake), I can only report that this was/isss overall, much less than I expected. In other words, this is pretty bad fruitcake, in my opinion, and for the price, really bad. If you are at all in my situation, I strongly suggest that you use any under-used credit card funds or other "disposable income" on something else. Cause this is pretty bad fruitcake.

Now, before you cut me to the quick, and question either/or my knowledge and experience of/with said fruitcake product, let me just say that I've been getting fruitcakes as gifts (usually around Christmas), for a long, long, long, long time. Ever since I care to remember actually. I think I remember that once upon a time, I casually mentioned to family, friends, or others, that I liked fruitcake. I actually, generally LIKED fruitcake. Well, soon the word spread, and I've been given them by family, friends, or other over the ages. Not that I'm complaining, because I DO LIKE FRUITCAKE! There, I said it all. But...this particular fruitcake brand? Fairly average at best, but compared to the cost, pretty awful.

Oh, believe me dear readers and followers, I WANTED to like this. I really did. An impulse buy at the time, all I wanted really was some half-decent fruitcake and an inexpensive means to keeping a credit card alive and kicking. Well, big, impulsive mistake, because, according to my taste, and my own decades-long relationship with fruitcakes in general, this is not very good. And it is only my history of loving almost EVERY fruitcake I've ever had, which guides to you, my fellow fruitcake lover, away from buying anything more than a sample of this product. And please don't make the mistake I made when I ordered taste-unseen, three single fruitcakes, when the purchase of even one would've told me the story here.

I realize with this review that I may go against the grain (though not fiber-wise) in dissing this, but I'm just coming from a long history of fruitcake enjoyment and this doesn't even come close in quality, taste, and otherwise, to fruitcakes enjoyed past, present, and future. Heck, this isn't even "cake" at all. It's like this big, thick, DOUGH, with TOO many TOO sweet "fruits," and the nuts were pretty dry and unmemorable. Heck, I don't even LIKE sweets generally. I'd much rather have a bowl of cheese crackers or chips than a bowl full of M&M's or Reese's peanut butter cups or chunkey monkey or any other such sickenly sweet thing. But heck, just about the ONLY sweet I've ever really loved, was/is fruitcake. So, why was/is this so disappointing, and so overpriced?

I think this is the fruitcake equivalent of fruitcake DOUGH. Like cookie-dough ice-cream, which I've always thought too weird and not really concentrating on the essentials. This is like eating fruitcake DOUGH, before any baking. And that, ain't good. Fruitcake should be CAKE, not uncooked DOUGH. And that's what this is really. In the end, wholly unacceptable, and to go technical on you'all, pretty darn yucky, you betcha! Only my opinion...try a sample before ordering anything more than that.

Judging by the generally favorable opinions about this specific fruitcake I've found here on Amazon, I may never know if this is just me, or what. This has generally high reviews, but I only managed to finish ONE of the THREE individual pounds I ordered and was sent (and btw, Amazon delivered nice and fast and easy as usual), and was just gonna GIVE the rest away, but I think I would've felt guilty about subjecting anyone else to this, so I just threw the other two pound "cakes" away. Maybe the rats or worms will like it, I don't know.

Basically, to make a long, boring, but hopefully humorous story short, I suggest buyer beware on this, and buy/try the smallest portion/size you can. If you like this thick, tasteless in many ways, un-fruitcake, by all means, purchase away. But I can't give this any kind of enthusiastic thumbs up, as far as fruitcakes go. And wouldn't ya know it, the instructions for use are virtually non-existent, with no manual, no software, and little documentation as to why and how I'm supposed to actually enjoy this doughy mess. And no real warranty! Fruitcake lover/buyer beware...

To all fellow outcast, strange dog, hopelessly romantic, secret fruitcake lovers, my small minority brothers and sisters who KNOW good fruitcake from bad, let me just say that this is nowhere near worth the asking price. To those of you who've tried this and actually liked it, I can only suggest you expand your fruitcake worldview and experience to other brands because this just ain't that good. A cheap dollar store variety is better than this, IMHO. One thing for sure though, next hardly used credit card purchase goes to another gift card for someone else, for something other than such a bad product as bad as this...

These berries are thought to be one of the one of the healthiest natural foods. There are many "stories" about the amazing benefits of these berries, many of which may be true, but a few verifiable facts about them (in dried form) follow:

1) High protein (about 12%), and are a complete protein. This is good for anybody, but particularly noteworthy to vegans, who choose not to get their protein from meats.

2) Decent fiber content (about 10%)

3) 18 (!!) amino acids

4) Like most sweet fruits, high in carbs and calories. 100 grams give you about 350-380 calories; roughly 3/4 from carbs and 1/4 from fat.

5) 6 vitamins, 8 amino acids, 11+ minerals (more in trace amounts)

6) Carotenoids, unsaturated fatty acids (this is a good thing), phytosterols (help lower cholesterol), and other healthy (or theoretically healthy but not particularly well researched) phytochemicals.

Enough with the technical jargon. These berries are great in cereal, smoothies (once hydrated), and tea. For tea, try this:

Put water, a small number of berries (6-15ish) and a teabag in your cup, microwave for about a minute per teacup (time varies), drop a small amount in your favorite tea along with the teabag and let the berries and tea steep for about 3 minutes.

This adds a subtle character to green tea (plus an unusual, tasty snack to do with a few of the sips). The flavor seems to blend well with chai and jasmine too. This may work differently for those who use creamer.

Of note:

- If you let them soak for too long (more than about 5-10 minutes) they get mushy and lose their texture and flavor.

- If you do not soak them long enough, they can feel a little bit gritty. I think this is due to the seeds. I don't mind it myself, but some might.

I recommend that you try a bag, keeping in mind that you may need to soak the berries in water/tea/whatever in order to make them soft, and see what you think. I have found they make a great addition to my usual cereal-only breakfast because they give me a much-needed protein boost.

If you like them quite a lot, you may want to take the time to look for a supply in a nearby Asian foods store. I have heard they can be purchased at a lower cost in bulk.

The reviewer that reported these are "gross" may have received something from a bad batch. I think they have a nice cranberry/raisin-ish flavor and have almost no noticeable odor (and the odor isn't an unpleasant one to me).

Summary: Buyer Beware:  HOW DO YOU KNOW THIS IS GENUINELY "ORGANIC"????
Text:
Go to [...]. Search for the video entitled: WHOLE FOODS MARKET "ORGANIC" FOOD MADE IN CHINA!!!!

According to my research, China is the major supplier of Goji berries. There's been an unresolved growing concern about food, any food produced in China, even though it is labeled "organic" with the USDA and AIC labels.

If you want to know about specific products, you can go to the WJLA website for a "do not purchase" list.

Because I learned that China produces the vast majority of the world's supply of goji berries, I sent an inquiry to a US distributor-retailer of "certified organic" goji berries to ask them how they knew for sure that their "certified organic" goji berries were truly organic. I never got a response.

I have learned that the Chinese government does not allow non-Chinese, independent individuals or agencies to inspect the organic farms in China. I do not know whether the Chinese government has changed that policy or if any progress is being made as of this writing.

Until I can be sure the higher prices for "organic" labeled foods are justified, I am going to avoid any food products that are "Made In China" from Whole Foods Market or from any other distributor.

If you don't see the country of origin on the label, my feeling is....why? And I don't buy it.

Of course, even if the label says "Made In USA", that is no guarantee that some ingredients in the product do not originate in China. E.G., Trader Joe's does not sell products "Made In China" but that does not mean that products put together and "Made In USA" do not use ingredients imported from China. Which is worrisome.

The consumer is king. If you weigh in with your buying habits (your almighty wallet), the producers will listen. Your health is the most important asset you own. Become a fierce creature and protect your health.

Summary: all 8 essential amino acids in a berry!
Text: need i say more.  practically a miracle food.  doesn't really taste bad or good.  eat straight up as a snack, part of smoothies, in cereal.

I like goji berries and have purchased other products from Navitas Naturals of good quality, so when I received these I immediately opened them and tried them. They smelled and tasted off...slightly moldy...but I didn't see any mold. I opened the second package (8oz 2 pack) and they tasted the same. I put them away and disregarded the taste until I started to feel a little sick. I went back to the packages and cut some of the perfectly fine looking berries open...and about 1 in 10 was filled with mold.

I will definitely not be purchasing this product again, no matter how packed with nutrients it is. It has made me temporarily paranoid about all of the dried stuff I eat...it all looks fine on the outside.
It is a shame there are no returns with this item as I am noticing from reviews that the mold problem is fairly common.

I know these berries are the ultimate food for your health. I am just a little disappointed that they don't taste so good by themselves,  like a little snack by themselves. You have to eat them with something, yoghurt, nuts, chocolate - then they are ok. I will keep eating them because they are a powerhouse for health.

Summary: goji berry- superfood vs tasty snack
Text:
I have been eating goji berries since a friend gave some to my brother when he was undergoing chemotherapy. They are less sweet and smaller than raisins and I find them quite tasty. At first, the taste was unfamiliar, so it took a little getting used to. They can also be a bit drier than other dried fruit. One of the best things about them is how they affect my energy level. I have a friend who uses a supplement made up mostly of ground up goji berries (also known as wolfberries) He lost a lot of weight, his skin got really healthy and started to glow and his energy was notably clearer. His improved health was so obvious, I noticed it before he even said that he was doing anything different and had to ask him what had changed.
These goji berries are well packaged and this is a better price than I was able to find elsewhere.
These were here in record time!  And my boys LOVE them! ;)  I'm sure we will be ordering again soon since they are being inhaled by my 3 and 2 year olds! ;)

I ordered these because I don't like sulfur dioxide, which most of the commonly-available goji are heavily treated with. These were definitely priced right, and they are sulfer free, fresh-looking, with great color, and certified organic. I will definitely be ordering again.

I've gotten two shipments of these Goji's already and I have to say that Navitas Naturals is a great company. Their products are very high quality, and they have trade agreements with locals overseas that grow their different products for them. Goji berries are very healthy for you, and I'm in the process of growing them in my house too. But until I have enough to make buckets full of them I'm going to continue to buy them here on Amazon.com , The best place to buy these.

I eat a handful or more a day and it's a very tasty snack, although these are a tad drier than others I have tried; but the dryness seems to be just on the outside of the berry because the inner part has a moist chewiness. We really enjoy them.

Summary: Fresh light scent, works well & no stinging sensation as with Nizoral
Text:
My husband and I both occasionally use the new Clear Haircare products but for different reasons. He wanted to try this since he now wears suits much more often to work and wanted to make sure he had no stray flakes visible. Skin flakes build up for a variety of reasons and many people run straight to the anti-fungal shampoos such as Nizoral Anti-Dandruff Shampoo, 4 oz. which is formulated to deal with only dandruff caused by a common fungal infection of the scalp. It is appropriate if that's the case but expensive and stings both your scalp and burns your eyes which can be inconvenient. My husband merely has dry scalp since we live in Los Angeles under very dry conditions. He found this new Clear Men Scalp Therapy shampoo to be gentle enough for every day use and that a very little amount will clean his just below the ears, curly but conservative hairstyle. In fact, he says it rinses cleaner than many other shampoos we have product tested that claim to moisturize the scalp in order to prevent flakes.

My husband liked the refreshingly light Mint scent that didn't overpower his other toiletry products and has found that using this as his new daily shampoo is saving us money. It doesn't seem to strip his hair of its own natural oils so he doesn't need to use heavy duty conditioners. We're more than pleased with the new formulation. The flake-zapping ingredient is the Pyrithione Zinc but the addition of traditional used Tea Tree Oil as a natural anti-fungal and anti-bacterial is safer than the ingredients in Coal Tar Shampoos or Shampoos such as Nizoral. The latter product relies on formerly prescription strength antifungal Ketoconazole. If you do not in fact have the Fungal infection that Ketoconazole is intended to combat, you could actually be ruining your chances of that solution working should you become infected with the highly common fungus that lives on our bodies naturtally and sometimes grows out of control due to health issues or too-frequent shampooing with harsh detergent type shampoos.

Clear Men Scalp is a terrific down the middle choice at a good price point! Highly recommended! However, if you truly do suffer from the common fungal cause of serious flakes, you will need to eradicate the cause with a product like Nizoral and perhaps discuss it with your Primary Care Physician as well. If your scalp is merely dried out from too frequent washing, this is a nice mild shampoo when used in moderation. It works well and you may find that soon you can even skip shampooing to every other day and merely rinsing your hair clean of common pollutants, dirt and sweat that build up during the day and saving a good washing for the second day. When my husband first noticed his scalp was overly dry, limiting his shampooing to every other day was the recommendation he got from his doctor. However, he finds this shampoo, used in small amounts, gets the job done without stripping his hair. he also now uses their conditioner.

I used the shampoo on my own long hair "Ethnic hair" but found I was better off sticking to the same company's new Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty line of nourishing products for Women of Color or even fair skinned women who simply have textured, dry hair and dry scalp in need of proper nourishment and moisture protection such as CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY Ultra Shea Smooth & Nourish Conditioner, 12.7 Fluid Ounce and the shampoo and nourishing hair Oil that goes with it. Clear and all its products are passing muster in our household! Rack up another win for them with their new line for men! For more information on their line Google their website using the terms: Clear Haircare and their wbsite will show up under that name smooshed together. We can't list outside websites in reiviews anymore. They have several other lines for all types of women too so give them a look!

ProfileName: James Beswick "In my day, we had 9 planets."
Text: I've used Head & Shoulders and the Walgreens white-label anti-dandruff shampoo products for a long time and not really been enamored with either, mainly due to the scent and variable success at eliminating dandruff. I've tried this over the last week and think it's an improvement on what I had been using. The lid is well designed, making it easy to open in the shower, and the scent is much more pleasant too. Best of all it does seem quite successful in eliminating dandruff so I think I'm going to convert to this brand. As another reviewer commented, it's pricey but these products usually are.

This shampoo is marketed for men, which basically means it has more of a masculine scent and is designed for men's hair. This shampoo by Clear has a very pleasant smell. The shampoo is made with a combination of tea tree, natural mint, ginseng and a very subtle hint of coconut. Theses fragrances combined really promote an appealing aroma, without being too over bearing. It is also designed as an anti-dandruff product, I don't have dandruff, didn't have it before this product and don't have it as I type this. I guess it works.

The shampoo itself looks like glue but works in very well into hair and suds up wonderfully. It should be respected that with this product, a little goes a long way. My hair felt very clean and refreshed after using this shampoo, I attribute that to the mint. Oh and never fear, this product will not leave your scalp feeling like you rubbed Vicks vapor rub on your head. I have used a hair product that had mint in it and that was the result. This is not the case here. Overall a great product that I could see myself using again.

Five dollars for 12.9 ounces of shampoo struck me as being an awfully good deal.  I do have dandruff, so I had nothing to lose.  As far as the ginseng, mint and other natural items, there is a fresh smell but nothing seems truly pungent.  It is a subtle smell with no lingering smell after rinse.  I was also surprised at how little it takes to use.  It is very concentrated and instead of a foamy lather, you obtain a creamy lather.  After one week and wearing the same dark or darker shirts I normally wear, I saw little evidence of dandruff on my clothes.  I even wash my goatee with it now and when I rub it, there are no more tiny flakes.  I'd say this company and product will go far.  This is a very good bargain.

Summary: Good, gentle shampoo that smells a little too much like bubble gum
Text: I used to have serious dandruff problems.  Fortunately, those have passed for the most part.  Now my issues are only minor, but the Clear Men shampoo resolved the little I had left.  It's kind of weird to describe a shampoo as soft, seeing as it's a liquid and therefore would be regardless, but it just feels very very soft.  It doesn't make your hair any softer, but it's pleasant to use.  It also cleans very well and is gentle so it won't damage your hair.  (At least, that's been my experience.)  The only downside is the smell.  It's not bad by any means, but the scent is reminiscent of bubble gum.  If you like that, you're good to go.  I'd prefer something a little more subtle.  That said, everything is else great.  It's a very reasonably-priced, functional, good shampoo.

I highly recommend this for men whether or not you have dandruff or not as they seem to use ingredients in this that are more appropriate and effective for men. I was using a different product and my scalp was irritated, red, and flaky. This felt like a milder, calming version that cut back on those symptoms. There is a slight tingle, but it is less irritating. The smell is also nice which is a huge plus. If you have an irritated scalp I would highly recommend this product.

Let's cut to the chase: The active ingredient in this shampoo is Pyrithione Zinc (1.0%). It is the same active ingredient and concentration as another popular anti-dandruff shampoo, Head & Shoulders Classic Clean Dandruff Shampoo with Pump 33.8 Fluid ounce. If Head & Shoulders works for you, so will CLEAR.

Why, then, buy CLEAR? It's got a whole host of botanical additives including ginseng (who knew your hair could be more ALERT?), tea tree, natural mint (more on this one below), vitamins B5 and E, sunflower, soybean, almond and coconut oils. Sound delish, but don't mistake this for an ice cream topping. How much of these additives actually make some sort of positive difference for your hair, well, who knows? One thing I have found, though, is the addition of natural mint may make your scalp tingle. If you leave this shampoo in for a few minutes, you may notice a tingly sensation eminating from your scalp. It's pretty cool and quite invigorating first thing in the morning. Does it actually make one's hair more lively? Unlikely, but it feels GREAT. If you want to spend a little more and get a super shot of tingly scalp check out American Crew Daily Stimulating Conditioner, 33.8 Ounce or American Crew Citrus Mint Cooling Conditioner 33.8oz. (Now there's a dramatic jump start for your scalp.)

Overall, I've been very happy with the aroma, feel, and dandruff-control effectiveness of this shampoo.

I have used many types of Dandruff shampoos - mostly Head & Shoulders brands or pharmacy store equivalent generics. This product works just as well, if not better than those shampoos at eliminating dandruff, plus is smells a whole lot nicer and left my hair feeling a bit lighter. I've been using this product (and others of the same variety but with different fragrances) for two months, now, and can honestly say that it is the best anti-dandruff shampoo I have ever used.

Summary: makes my hair really soft and manageable
Text: I didn't notice at first. It made my hair really soft and manageable. My hair used to stand up. Now my hair is softer to touch and manageable and does not stand up too much after using it for a few times.

Summary: Lathers well, cleans nicely, smells good
Text:
I've been using this new "Clear" product each day for about two weeks. Before using this product, I used one very similar to it for about 3 weeks: CLEAR MEN SCALP THERAPY 2 in 1 Anti-Dandruff Shampoo and Conditioner, Clean & Refresh, 12.9 Fluid Ounce. Honestly, I can't really tell the difference. I guess the other one was formulated to fight dandruff more, which I used to have, but that has not been an issue for me for some time now. Before using the "Clear" products, I used to use Head & Shoulders.

Pros:
- Nice design for the bottle; dispenses cleanly without leaving a mess on the bottle (H&S can clump up over time, and their caps are not as easy to use as the Clear product)
- Smells clean, not too strong (H&S has an OK smell to it too in my opinion)
- cleans well (I have oily hair, and Clear cleans it well, and does so quickly)
- lathers up nicely! (I'd say it lathers up better than H&S)

Cons:
- the only issue with this product is that a small amount of it leaked out in shipping. That was not the product's fault, but be aware that buying a liquid anything, and having it shipped to you, might leak. In all fairness, I don't blame Amazon or the product's packaging for the leak, and for the small mess that I had to clean up, things just sometimes happen during shipping, it's a risk we all face when we purchase this way

Interesting:
- I will say that this shampoo feels and looks a bit like Elmer's(r) glue when you put a little in your hand; sort of fun!

I have problem dandruff that is too much for Denorex and, until now, has required a coal tar-based shampoo to subdue. I've been using Clear Men Scalp Therapy for about a month now and my scalp is healthier and more dandruff free than anytime I can remember. It has a pleasant scent and leaves my hair and scalp feeling great.

ProfileName: A Research It Maven "Just the facts please"
Text: This Head & shoulders shampoo really controls my dry itchy scalp! It does have a heavy scent tho. I'd buy it again because my hair stays clean a lot longer, too. I recommend that you buy it!

While I'm not usually one to put a lot of stock in differences in shampoos, I have to give this one credit. It cleans very well, and actually smells pretty good. It's not some crazy fruit smell of strawberries or the like, but a nice mint. While that's not terribly manly itself, it's better than most. It's a lighter feeling shampoo that doesn't seem to weigh hair down and rinses away well.

My husband has a dandruff problem and uses Head and Shoulders so when amazon offered this product I said why not give it a try. It might actually work. And guess what? It actually does. It's much cheaper than Head and Shoulders and smells great as well. I very rarely give 5 stars on Vine products but this one does deserve its 5 stars. We've mostly grown up with the impression that cheap stuff rarely works but in this case this isn't true. After using it for close to 2 weeks (not on a daily basis) his dandruff is not as prominent as it once was. He's decided to scrap H&S and stick with this for now.

Summary: Clear Men Scalp Therapy does it again!
Text:
After using H&S for many years I thought it was high time to try something else and see if I couldn't improve my current shampoo situation. Clear Men Scalp Therapy sounded interesting so I figured "what the heck" ! You get almost 11 ounces in this bottle which is a bit less than my current brand.

The bottle is easy to grasp and manage in the shower without becoming slippery from the water and opening is a breeze thanks to the push down lid. I found that while the consistency of this shampoo seemed a bit thin to me, very little was actually needed to achieve a full head of suds and to clean my overly oily hair and scalp.

After using Clear Men Scalp Therapy for 45 days I can happily report at least the same dandruff reducing results as I got my my mainstay Head and Shoulders. But since the shampoo is apparently more concentrated, I used less and it actually rinsed out faster.

I wanted to try the Clean & Refresh variety and it feels both great to use and leaves a nice subtle scent. As with all my other Clear shampoo products this will leave your hair thoroughly cleaned but not oily feeling. Plenty of lather and an easy rinse off are what I have found to be the case with all the Clear shampoos I have tried so far. (I have tried AND used 3 varieties) They all smell good and not overpowering and they ALL get my hair very clean.

Basically all the varieties of Clear I have used employ a varying special formulation that includes tea tree among other ingredients. Some with conditioner, some without. Now I am no expert but honestly my hair is much more manageable after a weeks use of Clear brand shampoo as opposed to H&S and the anti dandruff ingredients do the trick 100%! Give it a try! I like it, maybe you will too.

Clean smell, slightly citrus, shampoo. After switching from another brand, the Clear Men Scalp Therapy seems to work well at keeping away the dandruff. Keeps hair feeling soft and smooth. Only a small amount and you get loads of lather.  Good size bottle, should last a while.

Very nice light scent, doesn't over power you. Gets your hair very clean with only a little bit, I mean like only a few drops.  Takes care of your dandruff, and can be used everyday.  In my experience you probably won't need to use a conditioner also.

The Clear Men Scalp Therapy Anti-Dandruff Shampoon Clean & Refresh works as advertised. The fragrance is pleasant but not overly deafening like many of the new shampoos that have come out in recent years. I've used Head & Shoulders for years and this one works just as well, perhaps a little better, no flakes so far.

What I really like about it is that with a small amount one can generate a great deal of lather, which makes washing one's hair far easier, and this also makes the bottle last much longer than the competition.

As far as the refreshing feeling it's supposed to generate, it is indeed invigorating, unlike other anti-dandruff brands that claim the same but actually produce a burning sensation instead. This one is clearly designed for those of us who have more chemically sensitive scalps.

Design wise the bottle's quite utilitarian, easy to open, store and it doesn't wobble over easily, which isn't a major concern but nonetheless it's an added bonus.

I'm usually reticent when it comes to trying new products in this genre, but I've definitely found a worthy alternate to my usual shampoo. Highly recommended.

Shampoo is shampoo, right? Wrong, this product has a luxurious thick texture. Since it is made for dandruff or other issues with your scalp, it provides an agent which leaves you with a fresh feel.

Because of the thickness, you don't need as much to provide a typical cleaning. The container is ideal for the shower as it can stand up or fit inside your accessory tray. If you are seeking to an alternative for hair/scalp treatment this product is worth trying.

Summary: works on dandruff and smells good
Text:
I normally used head and shoulders dandruff shampoo, which prevents dandruff and also smells nice. This shampoo also worked to prevent dandruff on my hair. In fact its smell is somewhat similar to head and shoulders as well.
The shampoo itself is creamy white with the smell being a nice clean scent. The smell starts fading after half a day but its still there by the end of the day, just faintly. The bottle is easy to open, you just press one end and the other end pop ups. Which is great because the H&S bottles are a pain to open; you know what i mean if you use H&S. It also works up a lathe quickly.
Overall i can heartily recommend this product to others to purchase; i dont believe you will be disappointed.

Don't have a great deal of hair to wash but I have been using the "Clear Men Scalp Therapy" daily and works as promised. I even use it on my beard and mustache and it makes taking my shower that much more invigorating, With the scent and tingling feeling on your scalp and face makes you feel that much more clean. My scalp is flake free and not itchy at all.

ProfileName: Michael A. Saxton "Dark Lord of the Sith"
Text: I received a recommendation awhile back that you shouldn't use the same shampoo every single day because of buildup on your scalp. I use anti-dandruff shampoos because I don't want build-up and flaking so I took that to heart. I typically use head and shoulders but I wanted an alternative for the days I switch off. This one has done well. It keeps up with the anti-dandruff job it has. When I use it, I don't need conditioner (I have long hair). And best of all, it doesn't smell fruity. It's another reasonable shampoo for guys.

Many men my age have a retreating hairline. Mine didn't just retreat, it unconditionally surrendered!..many years ago...and left only a few lonely sentinels on the great plain of my balding pate. What hair I have left is a semi-circular rear-guard on the back of my head and above my ears. And it's sensitive. After a defeat like that, who wouldn't be?

In fact it's so sensitive that the usual dandruff-removing shampoos (the kind that's supposed to make your scalp "tingle" when it's working) irritate my skin so badly that it turns red...or maybe it's just blushing after its former defeat. So I quit using dandruff shampoos...and quit wearing dark shirts and coats as a result.

Along comes CLEAR MEN SCALP THERAPY. I thought: what the heck, why not try it. The worse that can happen is nothing...or my skin turns the color of fall leaves in the mountains again.

It's been less than 2 weeks since I started using CLEAR MEN SCALP THERAPY and already I've noticed a tremendous difference. It works. Not only does it work, it does so without irritating my skin. Two weeks and no rash or itching...and NO dandruff. YUP...this stuff works. It REALLY works. I like it.

This dandruff shampoo isn't harsh on my hair or hair color. (I'm female) It leaves my hair squeaky clean without drying it out) Also the smell isn't "manly" smelling. I thought it might smell like men's products but it doesn't. I actually prefer using this to my everyday shampoo because it cleans gently and removes all the residue from my hair products.  I also feel like it keeps dandruff at bay. I don't have terrible dandruff but if you do and your products dry your scalp, it can make it worse.

I don't have dandruff to I gave this to my husband to try out. He's impressed with it.
It works well for him, smells good and costs much less than many other dandruff shampoos.
Grateful for the opportunity to try it. What more could you ask of a dandruff shampoo?

The shampoo has a good scent designed for men.

Clear Men Scalp Therapy is excellent it leaves your hair feeling clean and fresh.

I don't have bad dandruff but my boyfriend does.  He's tried Selsun Blue and Head & Shoulders, neither of which worked.  He finally found a solution in Sulfur 8, a shampoo that's sold in Walmart's "ethnic hair" section.  I let him try this and it was funny -- I heard "wow..." "wow!" coming from the shower. When he came out he was so happy and darn if his hair didn't look glossier.  There is not a speck of dandruff in his hair since he's been using it. He said it was very tingly and refreshing and now this is the only shampoo he'll use. Highly recommended!

This is a fine shampoo for clearing up flaking or dry skin however it does leave my scalp and the roots of my hair slightly oily.  This would be a huge problem if I had very long hair or possibly a problem for men with longer hair.  It definitely works nicely, but would be best suited for women with a short/cropped haircut or men with very short hair.

I've been using Neutrogena T-Gel Terapeuthic Shampoo, Original, 4.4 Fluid Ounce for years and have had mixed results. At times it would seem to work, but other times I would still have an itchy scalp and dandruff -- anyone with dandruff knows how embarrassing it can be. I've also used Head & Shoulders, but it didn't seem to work well for me either.

I've been using this Clear Men Scalp Therapy shampoo for the past 2-3 weeks and have been pleased with how well it has worked. My scalp has felt less itchy, dandruff hasn't been noticeable, and my hair feels almost as silky smooth as if I used Pantene.

My complaint with this product has do with the packaging. The item came in a padded envelope. When shipped, as much as 1/4 of the shampoo had leaked all over. The cap just isn't secure enough. Even after washing the bottle off, turning it upside down would result in leakage. Despite the flaw in the packaging, I would still recommend this product -- but consider purchasing this at your local store instead.

This is a great anti-dandruff shampoo.  It does the just as well as other leading shampoo, but it does so without that medicine-like smell that follow other similar products.  It also cools the scalp really well as it has mint and other herbs.  For those individuals with longer hair: You will probably need to use conditioner after this, which is not a big deal if you are already doing so anyway.

ProfileName: James C. Ward "horror and sci-fi fan.."
Text: really enjoyed this shampoo.  Only a small amount is needed to later your entire scalp.  Fresh clean scent that helps to control dandruff.  Will buy this product again.  Highly recommended.

Summary: I have like all of these products so far.
Text: I have reviewed a few of these shampoos and they are all very good products.  They clean your hair and it stays clean feeling all day.  It does not make your hair feel like it has something on it and it does have a good smell.  The price is very competitive with Target and Walmart and this is something that you can get here for just as cheap as the box stores.  This shampoo also got to me without flexing and losing a little product as well so they have improved the shipping method for this as well, all in all a very good item.

This shampoo is good for those who struggle with a flaky scalp. We found it to be effective. It has a light scent and doesn't leave a buildup on the hair, it doesn't weigh it down. We'll purchase this again.

My husband has psoriasis and I have to keep T-gel on hand for him to keep the itching down, but it stinks.  This works just as well and has a light, pleasant fragrance that he remarked about right away.  I love the consistency, which is like a lotion and it lathers well.

Summary: Works well, even on ladies' hair.
Text: I have somewhat short, fine hair, (but a lot of it) and my husband has fine thinning hair.  We both occasionally experience issues with dandruff and dry scalp, so I wanted to try this shampoo as an alternative to our usual brand.  While billed as "shampoo for men," I found the scent of this shampoo to be pleasant and mild, and not at all "medicine-y."  The shampoo itself was rather thin, like my regular shampoo, rather than the toothpaste like consistancy of our usual brand of dandruff shampoo.  I was very pleased with the results on my hair, it washed away any dandruff I had, and my scalp was totally itch free.  This is not a "2-n-1" shampoo, so those with very dry hair may want to follow up with a conditioner; although the formula is not drying, and I don't think conditioner would be needed unless your hair is very dry.  Overall, this shampoo does what is advertises, which is get rid of dandruff, and it leaves a clean, fresh scent behind.  I think this is a very good product.

Summary: Effective anti-dandruff.  Great scent and lather.  Leaves hair a bit dry.
Text:
My review title pretty much sums up my experience.

I found this Clear Men Scalp Therapy to succeed in combating dandruff as well as the dominant marketed product (I'll say it . . . Head and Shoulders).

I really like the application experience. A nice rich lather (more creamy than foamy, but rinses clean easily). The label boasts of gensing, tea, and mint ingredients. I love the scent and I'll just say that it is quite herbal-like and really reminded me of apples more than anything else. Nice bottle by the way, which sits up securely and easily on either end.

Now, to my only negative on this shampoo, for which I deducted a star -- It seems to leave my hair more dry and straw-like than the other shampoos I use. I've tried Clear with and without conditioner. The conditioner helps of course, but all else being equal, it seems to leave my hair feeling dry.

In all, for anti-dandruff shampoo needs I like the Clear scent and lather. I think I prefer my old standby (Head and Shoulders) for final results with hair feel. Both are effective against dandruff.

Summary: Very mild scent (a positive for me), but a bit thin
Text: I like this shampoo.  It works well, just like other anti-dandruff shampoos that contain zinc.  It is also very mildly scented, something that I appreciate.  (I cannot stand bath products that have too strong of a scent.)  I am deducting one star from my rating because I think the product is a little thin/watery.  It does lather fine, though, even when using a small amount.

The product is a light lotion shampoo that has a subtle fragrance, and imparts a slightly cooling effect when used. I've used it for about a month, and don't think my hair feels any cleaner than before. I don't have a bad dandruff problem, so maybe I'm not the best person to test this product. I do need to use a conditioner after using it, since it does seem to dry out my hair.... or maybe it's just the hot, dry summer weather doing its thing. I probably won't be looking for this product on the shelf in the future, but if I find it on sale, maybe it is worth another try.

Summary: Works as well as more famous brand but with a more pleasing odor
Text:
Great shampoo! Seems to work as well as "brand x", but smells much nicer and less chemical/medicine-y. I have been using this on a daily basis for the last week and a half and have not been tempted to use my old shampoo once.

Recommended!

Though it has been years since anyone in our family has had dandruff, we do have a couple with other scalp issues and this shampoo did help with them. It does a great job of getting hair squeaky clean and looking great. I also believe it may help prevent future outbreaks of dandruff and other scalp problems. Whether you have a normal scalp or need therapy for your hair issues, it is a great product to have on your shelf as a 'just in case' treatment or preventative. Also, it says 'men' but I used it as well and liked how my hair looked and felt afterwards. I don't know how it would work on someone who has greasy hair issues, this type might cause more problems in those cases.

Summary: A Product That Gets It Right at a Fair Price
Text:
What should a dandruff shampoo do?

First (& probably 2nd, 3rd, and so-on and so-on)...it should control dandruff. Clear is, foremost, an effective treatment for mild fo medium dandruff (I don't know if its efficacy is actually higher, but it simply works well).

Second, it helps if the fragrance is decent, Clear goes beyond decent and is noticeably aromatic, yet understated, . Simply put: This stuff smells very good in a "natural" way that is never too heavy.

Finally, the strenght of this shampoo speaks for itself, but you will not have a pile of dry straw as it seems to leave hair soft and pliable.

So, Clear gets a definite recomendation as it is a product that does what is purports to at a reasonable cost. No reservations...Highly recommended.

I found this shampoo felt good on my head and my hair. It also has a pleasnt scent, and the bottle is a pleasure to use. As for the shampoo it seems to work well and it says it is made for everyday use. I don't feel worried about using it, my scalp should benefit from using it; although I don't think I have a problem with dandruff.
So while I do not need this shampoo, I feel comfortable using it.

Clear Men Scalp Therapy is described as an anti-dandruff shampoo that is "clinically proven to help eliminate dandruff symptoms at the source with pyrithione zinc." Okay. After approximately a week of use, I cannot say with any certainty whether that product description is true, but my hair sure feels clean after using it. It also seems to be less dry after shampooing although that could also be the result of my tendency to use only a little dab, having found that with shampoo, like Brylcreem, that'll do ya. I can't say that I agree with the claim that the natural mint ingredient will leave "an extra cooling sensation." My head did feel cooler but I attribute that to the ice cold showers I have a habit of taking when the temperature is in the 90s, as it's been too often of late.

There are a lot of ingredients that sound impressively healthy, including ginseng, tea tree, vitamins B5 and E, sunflower, soybean, etc, but, not surprisingly, when you squeeze it into the palm of your hand, all you see is a white cream. Nonetheless, I assume this is all good for the scalp.

This seems to be a quality shampoo. I recommend it.

Summary: Nice alternative to Head and Shoulders
Text: I have been a longtime user of Head and Shoulders shampoo to control my dandruff problems. Clear Men's Scalp Therapy shampoo is a fresh, pleasant alternative. It comes in an elegant and functional bottle, easy to open and shut, even with wet or soapy fingers! It has a nice texture - thick and creamy, and a subtly pleasant aroma that increases as you use it. It does an excellent job cleansing the hair and scalp, leaves no appreciable residue, rinses completely. The dandruff control is effective 24 hours after showering, which puts this treatment head and shoulders over Head and Shoulders. Good product! CLEAR MEN SCALP THERAPY 2 in 1 Anti-Dandruff Shampoo and Conditioner, Dry Scalp Hydration, 12.9oz

Used daily, this shampoo is very effective in eliminating dandruff. It has a great consistency, no separation in the ingredients.

The shampoo has a fresh, lemony and pleasant fragrance that is subtle and lingering and not over-powering at all.

It leaves my hair very soft and conditioned, much more so than the other dandruff shampoos. I love the luster in my hair after using this and the invigorating refreshed and really, really clean feeling.

If you have dandruff and still want soft, lustrous hair then I really recommend your trying this. Best dandruff shampoo I've tried so far!

The Clear Men Scalp Therapy is a good shampoo for hair and beard. The Bio 10 Nutrium formula with ginseng, mint, and tea tree leaves the scalp and face skin somewhat moist without the tight dry feeling that I get after using other shampoos. It produces a mild tingling sensation probably related to the mint ingredient. The shampoo has a very subtle flowery fragrance, not overpowering as in other products. I have only minor flaking in scalp and face skin and this shampoo effectively ended that minor problem. The product is white and milky prior to use and does not produce much in the way of suds. The consistency is like a mild skin cream/moisturizer and can be used every day. I think this feature helps to end flaking at the scalp and skin sources rather than just washing away flakes that have been produced already like other anti-dandruff shampoos. I would highly recommend this "scalp therapy" as a mild and effective anti-dandruff product.

This shampoo met my expectations. I have very thick hair, and this shampoo leaves your hair fairly soft and smooth. It also smells very pleasant.

I use Head & Shoulders regularly, but I tried this product as an alternative. So far, it is very good - I still notice very minor flakes, but overall it has done a good job of keeping dandruff to a minimum.

I would consider purchasing this product again, I really like it.

My husband has bad psoriasis on his scalp. Nothing made the flaking go away until this shampoo. He only has to wash his hair every other day and no more snow storm on his shirt. I am not a fan of all the ingredients. Sodium lauryl sulfate is bad. It has a lot of chemicals in it. We try to do no chemicals in anything. Since this works so well, he will continue to use it but less frequently. It tingles the scalp for a refreshing wash.

Dandruff does not hang around when this shampoo comes acallin'. It was fun watching the Olympics today and leaving the scalp scratching to someone else. This product has a mild but very pleasant odor. A small amout of this creamy substance will suffice for a thorough cleaning. The lid is designed to easily open for extracting the shampoo and just as easily closes back down. No shampoo that I have used in the last few years has been as satisfactory as this Clear.

I received this shampoo from the Amazon Vine program. Some of the contents spilled out all over the shampoo bottle, the packing slip and both the inside and outside of the shipping carton. I would guess that approximately 1/3 of the contents were spilled out. The lid was closed so the spillage was not from the normal opening but seems to have been from the sides of the lid. I still have a lot of shampoo to use and appreciate the opportunity to use this fine product. I mention the leakage only as an alert that it could happen to someone who purchases this product in which case it would need to be returned. Do not let my experience deter you from buying this product. It is a winner.

Summary: I'm quite pleased with the results
Text:
When given the opportunity to try this shampoo I was low on my anti-dandruff shampoo anyway so thought why the heck not. I don't have a real big issue with dandruff so typically use an anti-dandruff shampoo only once or twice a week although I typically wash my hair daily or near daily.

Upon the product's arrival I immediately liked the pop open and snap closed top, one of the better designs in my opinion. When smelling the shampoo for the first time I very much liked the light and clean scent.

The first thing I noticed when using Clear Men Scalp Thereapy anti-Dandruff shampoo is that a little goes a long way. I live in an area of the country where the water hardness is among the worst in the nation. Even when softened with a salt-based softening system many shampoos or soaps do not produce a nice lather. Each time I've used the Clear Men Scalp Therapy shampoo I've reduced the amount I use and am now down to a pea size amount which produces great lather on my medium length hair.

So, how are the anti-dandruff results. I've not seen any flakes since I started using this shampoo so that to me says it's working. But, I've also been flake-free when using Head and Shoulders and only notice flakes when I go 7 to 10 days without an anti-dandruff shampoo. However, I do like the clean scent and clean feel better than I do when using Head and Shoulders. My hair is very fine and I normally use a moisturizing rinse after shampooing. I've tried comparing this to Head and Shoulders without a rinse and with a rinse. Either way, the Clear Men Scalp Thereapy Anti-Dandruff shampoo is my choice. My hair is clean and less dry than when using Head and Shoulders. I can finally kick the "Head and Shoulders habit". Go ahead and try some, I think you'll like it.

Summary: Review for Clear men's anti-dandruff shampoo, clean & refresh version
Text: I found this to be similar to head & shoulders shampoo, which I use regularly. However, I did find that head & shoulders performed a bit better in preventing my scalp from itching for a longer period. In terms of being anti-dandruff, both shampoos worked about the same. I thought this shampoo would feel minty/cooling from the name and because mint and tea tree are written on the bottle, but it actually wasn't. The first time I used this shampoo, the fragrance was stronger than usual and lingered for several hours, making me worried that other people would notice the smell and get annoyed. The smell was not bad. I'm just not a fragrance person. However, this only happened the first time I opened the shampoo bottle and the fragrance was at normal levels the other times I used it. The fragrance was unisex and neither super manly or girly.

Summary: Works for the men in my family
Text: Requested this item for my son & husband. It worked like a charm. They had been using Head & Shoulders prior to testing Clear Men Scalp Therepy Anti-Dandruff Shampoo. While Head & Should worked for my husband it did not work for my son. He still would have dandruff. After using Clear for 3 weeks now, my son has no dandruff. It doesn't have an overpowering scent. It's smells clean and refreshing. I plan to switch from H&S to Clear. I highly recommend trying this product for men who suffer from dandruff. It may work for you.

I have been using the CLEAR MEN SCALP THERAPY Anti-Dandruff Shampoo, Clean and Regresh, for about a week. It comes in a 12.9 ounce bottle with convenient flat ends on both top and bottom, which means that when the bottle starts to empty, it can be stored on its top in order to get the remaining contents out easily. The ingredients include: ginseng, mint, and tea tree.

The shampoo itself is a milky cream which emerges readily from the container. The shampoo is not oily or greasy and appears not to leave residues. Any odor is not apparent to me. After one week of use, my scalp feels clean. My hair tends to curl, especially in the rain-forest environment where I live. However, this shampoo seems to flatten my curls. You may or may not like that effect. On the negative side, the shampoo is irritating if you get it in your eyes. Maybe this is caused by the mint. Altogether, I like this shampoo and plan to continue to use it.

Finally a dandruff shampoo that doesn't have a weird, medicated smell. The lid has a pop up part so you don't have to unscrew the top to get to the shampoo. It's not a deal breaker, but it is a nice feature. This shampoo doesn't make a lot of suds, but just a little shampoo seems to go a long way (the shampoo is rather thick). It does help with dandruff. I don't have this problem, but my daughter does. After using this product for a week I have to say it works as well as Head and Shoulders without the stinky smell.

Summary: 4 1/2 Stars - Handles Dandruff with a Subtle Scent
Text:
Clear Men Scalp Therapy Anti-Dandruff Shampoo Clean & Fresh comes in an easy to handle bottle with a modern pop-up cap. The Clean and Fresh scent can be spotted on the shelf because the cube on the front is surrounded by blue (as opposed to green for the Cool Fresh Mint scent).

Pros: The product does make a difference in dandruff. Having used the product several times, I see a difference. The Clean & Fresh scent has a more subtle smell than the Cool Fresh Mint even though they are both made with ginseng and tea. While the traditional whitish color of dandruff shampoo, it feels lighter and more like regular shampoos than a medicated dandruff shampoo and it leaves your hair feeling soft. Note, a very small amount works up a large lather, so the bottle lasts a long time.

Small issue:
The tilt cap can build up a slight crust that is a bit hard to wipe off because only a small space tilts up, putting it in running water cleans it up easily.

I recommend the product for clearing up dandruff with a subtle or no scent left behind. If you like to have a stronger scent of "clean" after shampooing you might try the Clean Fresh Mint scent too.

This shampoo has almost no scent, perhaps because it is intended for men.  It also seems to have low suds, at least less than some I have tried. It appears to work as anti-dandruff also, at least as well as the coal based shampoo that I have been using that my wife dislikes. While I have only used it twice so far, I like the way my hair feels after I use it. I have never before heard of this brand, but I will have to insure I can find where I can get it. (Probably order from Amazon).

Summary: Smells good. Feels good. Works good.
Text:
Let's dig right in...

++ THE PROS ++
+[APPLE SCENTED]
This has a nice, pleasing scent of apples. It's also very light scented and not at all overpowering
+[COLOR AND TEXTURE]
It's milky white and about the consistency of coconut milk
+[LIGHT LATHER]
This is meant to be a daily shampoo, so you're not going to get as thick a lather as a conventional shampoo.
+[WASHES OUT CLEAN]
It washes out easily and thoroughly, no feeling of leftover residue at all
+[FLAKES ARE UNDER CONTROL]
They're not completely gone, but so far this shampoo is doing a good job of managing and controlling it and keeping it to a minimum.
+[ITCHING IS UNDER CONTROL]
The Tea Tree and Mint are certainly doing their job here. I find I'm scratching much less with this shampoo.

-- THE CONS --
-[PRICEY]
Sadly though, this is usually the case with any anti-dandruff shampoo you buy. So I can't fault this product too much on that.

As far as scalps go, mine is very itchy and flaky. I have black shirts, but I'll only ever wear them at home as they serve to only remind me of just how bad my flaking can be.

I won't be so bold as to claim that I've tried "every" anti-dandruff shampoo out there, but I will say I've certainly played the field in search of the holy grail. Head-n-Shoulders, Selsun Blue, Denorex, Neutrogena and quite a few others I can't recall at the moment. I don't know what the heck is going on up on my scalp, even when I do seem to find something that works it doesn't take long before my scalp seems to develop an immunity to it.

I finally did find that holy grail of anti-dandruff product that works EVERY time, the VERY FIRST time but unfortunately it's completely unconventional and to put it mildly it STINKS!...And that product is Apple Cider Vinegar. That's right, that yellowy-orange cousin to White Vinegar. It's usually recommended to use a mixture of 50/50 ACV with water to dilute the smell...But sometimes the itch and flakiness on my head gets so bad I don't care and just douse at 100% ACV. Basically my head ends up smelling like Salt-n-vinegar chips and the BURN is intense and washing it out is a hassle and leaves your hair feeling like dried out branches...But man it WORKS!

So far I'm having good luck with this product, so I haven't had to go the route of the Apple Cider Vinegar, and that's a blessing! Well recommended.

I have now tried two Clear Scalp Therapy shampoos and am pleased with both of them.  Both are a creamy and white in texture and leave the hair feeling fresh and clean.  Clear Scalp Therapy are the shampoos for me.

Summary: CLEAR Are a Great Product Line

Summary: I'm rotating this in with my go-to shampoo
Text:
I've been using Pantene Sheer Volume for years and I really haven't strayed from it. But I heard it's good for your hair to switch it up and use different shampoos so the hair doesn't become accustomed to one thing. And then Clear caught my eye.

I feel like I have itchy scalp sometimes, so I've given Clear a shot because of the scalp therapy. I've been using it for a few weeks now and I like it. I think it's too early to tell if the shampoo is truly helping my scalp, but it's not hurting. The scent is pleasant and I was initially concerned since a lot of shampoos "for men" have strong scents. I don't care for that.

My hair feels good, I'm hoping my scalp feels even better, and it should be interesting how my hair reacts as it grows.

This men's 2-in-1 dandruff shampoo and conditioner smells good, lathers well, rinses clean, and leaves hair looking good. It contains the same active ingredient as Garnier Fructis, but with some herbal additives and a different scent.

So far, so good. Will update later in regard to dandruff treatment.

What I noticed when I first opened the shampoo is the smell. I can't really explain what it is, but it smells great. Nothing fruity or flowery, or over the top. It lathers nicely, if you like that, and rinses clean. You don't need much to do the job.

As far as the dandruff control, I've been using it a week and it seems to be working just fine. It's not overly harsh, and doesn't irritate my skin. Overall I'm very impressed with the Clear line of products, especially for the price.

My only complaint is the pop top on the shampoo bottle. While I like the ease of use in the shower, when I got my shampoo shipped to me I lost about 1/4 of the bottle because the pop top had been pressed inside of the bubble wrap envelope at some point and some of it leaked out and made a big mess. Maybe it was the way it was shipped (in an envelope instead of a box), but on the other hand I could easily see this happening if I bought it at the store and it was in a bag with other things that were on top that could do the same thing. Just a word of caution.
Well, this shampoo works fine with me. It smells nice and leaves the hair smooth and clean. As for the anti-dandruff claim, it seems true.

I'll have to say, I'm not disappointed. This shampoo has a pleasant "clean" fresh scent that I find agreeable. It lathers up well with just a small amount of shampoo.

As far as controlling my flakey, dry scalp - it has been almost 2 weeks and I've seen a noticeable improvement in my scalp. I think the Tea Tree ingredient makes this shampoo so gentle, but I can't be sure.

Overall, for the effectiveness and reasonable price, I give this product 5 Stars. I hope it works as well for you!

Summary: WOW!  This is a very good product...
Text:
I love white mochas, but at 4 bucks a pop at the cafe and goodness knows how many calories -- its an occational treat. Enter this very creamy and delicious mix from Ghirardelli. This mix is WONDERFUL! It contains no trans fats, no high-fructose corn syrup, and each serving of powder has only 90 calories AND NO FAT!!! In the world of canned soup products, I find Wolf Gang Puck's line to be a much needed respite from the testosterone-fueled, protein-worshiping Chunkys of the world that are a constant reminder we are still living in a warrior society dominated by an evolutionarily justified masculine self-view of physical gender hegemony. So you can imagine how thrilled I was to see Mr. Puck has delved into the realm of American home cookin'.

However, upon opening the can I was greeted with the unfriendly face of disappointment. The dumplings, uninspired cubes of flavorless dough, embodied the confinement felt by many of us who yearn for liberation from mass-produced culinary conformity. The broth's thickness belied its lack of substance--a trope of uncondensed soups better fitted for a Progresso "Italian" "Wedding" or Campbell's "Selects" (I suspect they are selecting from the bottom of the proverbial, and sometimes literal, in the case of food, barrel) "Cream" of "Chicken."

Ultimately, the can, with its prevailing superimposed bust of the supposed head chef, says it all. The superego, dazzled by the lustrous allure of capitalism, has superseded the ego, and the id is left wanting.

But add a little Tabasco and it's pretty good for a quick lunch.

First of all, I normally go out of my way to write positive reviews and avoid negative ones, but this was SO bad I just had to check in. Summary: Wolfgang Puck Organic Soup - Chicken & Duplings
Text:
I purchased this very very pricy soup on sale at my local Publix in their Greenwise section. It's typically $3.99 per can, but I caught a sale. I bought just one can to give it a try.

I agree with many of the other reviewers' comments, but I have a different take...He should be ashamed to put his name on this can.

I found 4 bits of what was passing as dumplings, 4 bits of celery, 3 chunks of what looked like processed canned chicken cubes, bits of carrots, lots of white potato, water, water, water, and more water.

I didn't need to eat it with a spoon because I could have poured it into a glass and drank it--very watery. The soup is not at all similair to the label which has hearty chunky ingredients like a stew.

The flavor was mild and not half bad, but the quality control for such a pricy soup should be better. I expected more gourmet for my money than I would have with most commercial brands that you can buy at the dollar store.

Pros:

Nice packaging
Packing made from recycled materials
Organic
Minimal preparation--heat and eat quickly

Cons:

Lacks flavor
Poor ingredients
High sodium content 680 mg.
7 g of fat
280 cal per can
Not a 16 oz can, rather a 14.5 oz. can

I give this soup a 5/5 for packaging, 0/5 for ingredients, and 2/5 for flavor. I like mild soups, but the lack of quality ingredients at this price really makes me pause. I do not recommend.

I'm a big fan of the Wolfgang Puck Chicken and Egg Noodle soup so I decided to try this. There were about 7 tiny pieces of dumpling, 2 tiny pieces of chicken, and maybe 12 tiny pieces of carrots. Expect to be very hungry after eating a can of this.

Wolfgang Puck should take his tiny dumplings back to Germany. This is AMERICA, baby... we gotta have flavor sensations.

Summary: I love the taste, and it is my "emergency" food
Text:
I love Near East Couscous. I always have a few boxes of couscous on hand for "emergencies" when I had no time to cook and I am in a hurry. Not only do I like the taste it is the easiest and fastest thing to prepare that I know.

Couscous is a coarsely ground pasta made from semolina, a type of wheat. When cooked it is light and fluffy, not gummy or gritty. Instant couscous already has been steamed and then dried again before it is packaged. To prepare it it only needs be soaked in boiling water until it swells, a process that takes only a few minutes. You don't even need the stove.

To start, measure out your couscous.
Pour it into a heatproof bowl.
Add hot water - the general proportion is 2 parts couscous to 3 parts water. So for 1 cup of couscous you'll need 1 1/2 cups water.
Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let sit for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork before serving.

Couscous doesn't have a lot of flavor on its own, but it works well as a base for vegetable or meat dishes. I have not found anything does NOT go with it. I like it with chicken, fish, lamb, and beef. I especially like it with the dishes have sauce as couscous absorbs the sauce so well. It also mixes well into salads and can be flavored with herbs like coriander, basil. It's a great base for all sorts of dishes.

I recommend it. It is a must have in my pantry!

Summary: Unfortunately, Acesulfame Potassium (Acesulfame K) is a main ingredient
Text:
I would love these suckers if they didn't use acesulfame potassium, or Acesulfame K, as a main ingredient. In various rat studies, Acesulfame K produced lung tumors, mammary tumors, and rare types of tumors in other organs (such as the thymus gland), several forms of leukemia and chronic respiratory disease, even when less than maximum doses were given. I first acquired a taste for cardamom when I lived in the Middle East. Both Arabic coffee and Turkish coffee are made with cardamon. The Arabic coffee is difficult to brew because it is made from green coffee beans and green cardamom pods ground together. I have not found a source for green coffee beans where I live. However, Turkish coffee with cardamom is both easy to brew and delicious to my taste.

For regular coffee beans I grind a few pods when I am grinding the beans (a little of this goes a long way), and the brewed coffee has a wonderful flavor (not to mention a wonderful aroma while brewing.) Friends find the taste ineffable. I find it familiar and delicious.

Another way I use cardamom is to make spiced chai (masala chai). I grind a pod with a part of a stick of cinnamon, clove and a single black peppercorn. I mix it in a half and half water and milk mixture that I bring to a boil, add black tea and grate a piece of ginger (or, when I am lazy, use powdered ginger.) For the chai, a nice touch is to sweeten it with Goya Panela Brown Sugar Cane 1 Lb - Redonda, known as "jaggery" in India. Or, for convenience, Turbinado Sugar - 1 box, 1 lb.

To be honest, I sometimes substitute powdered cardamom for pods, such as when I am making a quick Turkish coffee or chai, but when I want to treat myself, I use the pods. Frankly, there is not a ground cardamom I've tried that comes close to grinding the pods right before using them. And for company I never cut corners - these are an essential ingredient that is sure to impress and delight.

I loved the price. You can find it for $2 at most stores. Which is a really solid price for a yeast made by a reputable company. It seems like a very plain, average yeast without any significant character except breadiness and yeastiness.

Other than the price, I don't like this yeast. I tried it in a cider and a brown ale. It ferments fast and furious and when its done, that's it. This is a work hard play hard yeast. Mega krausen for maybe 36 hours and then that's it. The cider went from 1.056 to 1.008 in about 36 hours. The brown ale on the other hand started at about 1.060 and stuck at 1.030. I tried the usual stuff, swirling the tank, warm temp, nothing.

It finishes at a pretty high OG. It left very little apple character in the cider. Easy drinking but not anything special. I've heard people get good results with this. But I think it's a bit tempermental and in all honest not worth the price. When I have to spend $3.50 to pitch a pack of Nottingham to finish was the $2 pack of S-33 didn't, my yeast cost went to a price where I could have just gotten liquid.

Not a great combination -- yeasty, bready, poorly flocculating, inconsistent, tempermental.

This is my first experience with antioxidant-rich white tea. Also, I like the fair trade and organic labels. White Rose Velvet Garden White Tea is an exciting and unusual premium Numi tea. It is a white tea, more rare than other types of teas and less processed as well, having been only plucked and dried (not oxidized). Some people find white tea a subtler and more enjoyable type of tea experience (I know I do). White Rose Velvet Garden White Tea is certified organic, and is both fair trade and kosher.

It is made from hand-wrapped white tea leaves and rosebuds! Rosebuds---can you imagine?!?! Those are the only two ingredients, and they are delicate and delicious, different from anything else I've ever tried. This Amazon page erroneously lists some other ingredients but these are absolutely NOT in this tea---it is made from only white tea and roses.

This tea, like all Numi teas, is packaged with 100% post-consumer waste, and the tea bags are made from biodegradable filter paper. Numi does not believe in the practice of adding oils or flavorings to bolster flavors, and I love this and can tell the difference; for this and many other reasons, Numi is one of my favorite tea manufacturers.

On the box, Numi writes: "Roses have been a symbol of love and beauty since the dawn of romance. Numi's enchanting Velvet Garden(tm) releases a provocative sweet rosy taste as it blushes a soft pink. With every sip this liaison of organic rose petals and delicate Spring White tea imparts a silken smoothness. White Tea is the tender bud of the tea plant making it exquisitely subtle and supremely healthy. High in antioxidants and vitamin C, this uplifting Fair Trade Certified white tea blend will be the beginning of a long lasting love affair." I have to agree. This is truly an amazing tea.

If you like Numi teas, get it---you won't be sorry. If you are new to Numi but love white tea, or are curious to try it from the description, I do not think you could find a better source than Numi. If you are looking for a romantic tea, White Rose Velvet Garden White Tea fits the bill perfectly.

Highly recommended.

I tore the plastic open, put the frozen potato on a baking sheet in the oven and put it on 350. 45 minutes later it was done and turned out being delicious. The cheese filling was crispy on-top and the potato itself underneath was nice and soft. No way would they come out as good if put in the microwave, so I'd say oven cooking these is definitely the way to go. Now, you can obviously make your own stuffed baked potatoes for far cheaper then what Omaha charges for these alone, but as long as you get a good deal on the Omaha website, these simply make a great addition to any Omaha steaks order. As delicious are they are though, I wouldn't order a box of JUST these off the site due to the added shipping costs. But like I said, as long as they're part of a nicely priced packaged deal, I'll definitely take them. Actually, I probably wouldn't order any packaged deal in the future from Omaha that didn't include these. A big plus, at least for me, is if you check the ingredients list on these, there's no partially hydrogenated oils, so there's no traces of trans fats, which is very rare with stuffed baked potatoes. Also no high fructose corn syrup, which is another rarity on a food product like this and is always a plus. If you make your own or buy them frozen from your grocery store for example, chances are, the butter used, sour cream, etc. will be full of chemicals, trans fats & high fructose corn syrup. These, not so much. So there is a definite degree of quality with Omahas stuffed baked potatoes. Each potato does have 8 grams of saturated fat, which is 42% the DRV, but that's obviously to be expected with anything that contains bacon, cheese and sour cream. I was also expecting there to be no fiber, but it turns out there's 3grams of fiber per baked potato half. Another plus. Overall, the stuffed baked potato was very tasty and actually relatively healthy, being made with quality ingredients.

Summary: Excllent Product - Price of $50.00 for six 10-ounce boxes is overpriced
Text: Excellent product - My son loves this cereal.  Price at the Whole Food Store is $4.40 per 10 ounce box that equates to $25.00 for six boxes.  Charging $50.00 for 6 boxes seems to be grossly overpriced.
We love this cereal. I keep buying it for myself and my GFCF son, but my older son, who is not GFCF, keeps eating it up. We like the plain version, too, but the berries are extra nice.

I made "rice krispy treats" with them & they were good.  The berries added a little something extra to it.  Even people who don't need to eat gluten-free said they were good.

My daughter and I both have celiac.  This is her favorite cereal even over cocoa pebbles.  She loves the fruit in it.  I love that it is better for her than some of the other gluten-free options.  It is great that I can buy one kind of cereal that my whole family will enjoy, even those without celiac.
I have been gluten-free for a year now, and this is hands-down my favorite cereal - just the right amount of sweetness and crunch. And I love that it's made with brown rice. Awesome stuff!

Summary: Excellent food for those with food allergies
Text: This cereal tastes amazing! My son has severe food allergies which limits his diet. Often he's constrained to eating bad tasting foods so we were pleased to find a tastey alternative to what you find on the shelves of the local grocery store. You'll like this cereal!

Summary: The best gluten free cereal hands down!
Text: It's awesome tasting just like any mainstream kind with the taste of berries to boot. A real gem!

My sons and DH love this cereal. Not many of the gluten free cereals actually earn the title "delicious," but this one does. I like buying it here because it is generally cheaper than the local stores.

I love this cereal! Like others, I've also tried just about every gluten-free cereal out there, and this is quite possibly my favorite. I love Gorilla Munch but often find it too sweet and coarse, so this is a wonderful counterbalance to that. The berries add a nice touch, though I do love the plain Crispy Brown Rice as well.

My only issue is that, like many gluten-free cereals, Erewhon doesn't seem to have given much thought to fortifying their cereal with the extra nutrients that those of us with celiac disease so desperately need. However, I admit that I'll gladly take supplements if it means having food that doesn't taste like cardboard, so Erewhon Crispy Brown Rice with Mixed Berries will continue to be a morning staple in my home.

Also, as a side note for fellow dairy-intolerant celiac patients, this cereal does very well with soy milk. It doesn't get soggy and it retains its pleasant crispy crackling sound even as you eat.

This rice cereal is a real treat for me each morning.  It has a combination of dried fruit that enhances the flavor when milk is added. As a Celiac sufferer, this is my breakfast food that is tasty and gluten free.
If you like rice cereal and need gluten free, all the Erewhon brown rice cereals are really tasty!

Summary: Tasty but lacking in nutrional value

The other problem I had was that the cereal tends to stick together in clumps in the box so you have to break it up first.

If you examine the label you will see that it is mostly empty carbs. If you require a gluten free diet, I suggest Quinoa flakes with fresh berries on top instead. It has better nutritional value.
