Swirl some into yogurt, top with sliced bananas, sit back and imagine you are in The Olde Soda Shoppe, with a freshly made ice cream treat. You won't miss the calories, or the chemicals. Delicious.

Summary: Best caramel syrup I have had!
Text: I have tried Torani, Starbucks, and Amoretti. By far, Amoretti is the best. Its a little pricier than Torani, but well worth the extra cost. The quality is soooo much better. The syrup is thick in consistency. It is not like the 90% water stuff that you get from Torani. It also doesn't have the chemical after taste that Torani always leaves in my mouth. Plus, it has a rich deep caramel flavor. I do not write many Amazon reviews, but after tasting this syrup I felt compelled to do so! I love this with 4 shots espresso and some steamed half and half. It is the highlight of my morning. Can't wait to try the other flavors! Thinking a Holiday 3-Pack may be in my near future! Great job Amoretti!

I have purchased various flavors of syrups from Amoretti (within day intervals) and they have been fabulous.  When first opening this bottle, the scent actually blew me away.  I did not get an overwhelming smell of sugar, but that of what the flavor should taste like!  It had the caramel scent, but with a hint of butterscotch.  And to me, that is a VERY good thing.  The bottles are truly visually pleasing.  Most bottles that I come across just have the company name and flavor title; not very good.  But Amoretti has graced us with not only the flavor name, but a picture to go with.  These are definitely high quality coffee/etc syrups!  So, if you think that the cost is too much, just keep in mind that in most cases "you get what you pay for."  And in this case, that was a good thing.
Love this caramel syrup!  Amoretti is my new favorite brand of syrups.  The flavor is very rich, the syrup is thick, the bottle and pump look very nice on my countertop.

This is obviously one of those products where it's all about personal tastes. I was getting caramel lattes/fraps at Starbucks and Dunkin Donuts and was tired of paying for the high price. So I wanted to start making it for myself and on Amazon it was either this product or the other one where they used high fructose corn syrup. I obviously went for Amoretti because they don't use corn syrup. Once I got it and started to make my iced lattes, it tasted just fine. I haven't experienced anything wrong with this.

This syrup was not sweet enough for my taste. Obviously that is my problem, as the other reviewers liked the product very much. Talked to Customer service....they where great! The representative I talked to made everything clear.  While the taste was an issue for me personally, do not take that as a negative.  In fact I plan on ordering other products from this company in the near future, now that I better understand which items would be more to my liking. What a great company to deal with.....worthy of 5 stars for customer service alone.

I have purchased several different flavors of the Amoretti syrup and they are always of the highest quality. I used them to make my own latte's at home with a Tassimo machine and could not be happier with the end result. Plus being an Amazon Prime member my order is always here in two days at no charge.

Summary: Delicious healthy beverage, makes for great coffee substitute
Text:
There are other, bigger bags of this product available here on Amazon, and many reviews have been written under the 2lb size.
The price fluctuates, so it makes sense to do a bit of comparison shopping. I bought this packaging when it was about $10, which made it worth it. If you want to save some $$, you can buy bigger package and share with a friend, or just store it in the freezer - it will last quite a long time.

I have been drinking this for years, and as just about everyone else, really love it and recommend it. It has a very pleasant taste, dandelion is 'good for you' and you can use it as a delicious beverage or as an coffee substitute, if you wish. I usually add some stevia to mine, sometimes a little bit of half and half, could use rice or almond milk, some raw cacao powder, cinnamon, whatever sweeteners, "whiteners" or other enhancements you would put in the coffee and your imagination comes up with.
The amount to use will depend on your preferences. Some people like theirs little less concentrated, I prefer mine strong, so I use quite a bit. You can just play with it until you find your optimal powder-to-water ratio.

Also, from my experience, it is a good idea to keep your supply in the fridge or the freezer, as it does absorb moisture and if kept at room temperature, it very quickly hardens into a block and you have to chisel it if you want it to dissolve. Plus it loses the flavor, so it pretty much gets ruined.
I had to throw away sizable amount before I learned this, so what I started doing was putting whatever amount fits in a small glass mason jar with a plastic lid and keeping that in the fridge. Whatever is left, stays in the original bag, gets put into a Ziploc bag and goes into freezer.

Hope that helps and if you are sitting on the fence and want to just give it a try, definitely go with this size, I am sure you won't regret it!!

We love it. We are cutting back on coffee, have started making iced coffee with this product, and mixing it 50/50 with our morning coffee to reduce intake. It is an exceptional replacement. Use a small amount, as a concentrate.

I really, really wanted to like this. Really. I followed the directions on the package to make a "bold" cup of "coffee" drink and was put off by the taste. I tried it hot, cold and room temp. I LOVE a robust and bold cup of joe and this struck me as bland. It was pretty expensive so I'm pretty bummed about it. It's not a good sub for me. I don't have any experience with Postum like others so no comparison there.

This Dandy Blend is a wonderful alternative for coffee, just add any milk and sugar as you normally would.  I was cutting out coffee and having a hard time with it.  This was a health alternative to get me through.
I thought it tasted like coffee without the getters of caffine. would buy it again but would like to find it a little cheaper.

Summary: Delicious (and good for you) coffee alternative
Text: I tried dandy blend when I needed to stop drinking caffeine. I don't like decaf coffee because it gives me a headache. I was surprised by how good this drink tastes. It's instant so I add it to a mixture of hot milk and hot water. It's not sweetened but it has a sweet flavor so you don't need any sugar either. A very pleasant drink and worth trying whether or not you're off the coffee. I also learned that dandelion is high on the list of Chinese remedies for stomach and liver complaints. So it makes me feel good to know this is not some chemically concocted caffeine alternative, it's a wholesome beverage made from good-for-you ingredients.

I've tried two other coffee substitutes and this one is the most like real coffee of those I've tried.  It has the consistency of fine powder.  The package has several recipe suggestions.  One is a cafe-au-lait drink.  Another is a flavored ice cream made by simply stirring the Dandy Blend powder into some ice cream.  (It was a nice treat.)  A very good coffee substitute with hearty flavor.
Lots of decent flavors here and the folks at work like them well enough. If strong coffee is not your thing - this is great. Mostly medium roasts, it is just not strong enough for me.

I've ordered this variety pack from Green Mountain several times. I prefer strong coffee, and I've never been disappointed with the flavoring of this pack. They do have a "fresh by" date on the box, so maybe the other reviewer's experience could have been skewed by a less-than-fresh box (in which I'm sure Amazon would exchange for a new one). Enjoy!
Having a variety right at your finger tips is a pleasure.

Summary: All flavored coffees are not the same
Text: I ordered these 50! K-cups of flavored coffee because I liked some of the other flavored coffees that arrived in my starter kit when I got my B60.  Apparently, the brand does matter.  I like a stronger coffee and these are quite mild towards weak and thats on the small cup setting.  I recommend doing some taste testing before committing to a 50 pack!  [...]

Summary: Flavors in product description are inaccurate
Text:
According to the product description, I was supposed to received 2 sampler boxes that contained 22 k-cups with the following flavors: Hazelnut Cream, French Vanilla, and Rain Forest Nut.

The boxes that I received had French Vanilla, Caramel Vanilla Cream, Hazelnut, and Wild Mountain Blueberry. I was disappointed because I really wanted the Rain Forest Nut (but didn't get it) and I really don't like the blueberry flavor (already had a box of it).

The coffee is good, but don't be surprised if you get different flavors than what you were expecting.

No flavor here!

The main reason why I bought this system was for the Green Mountain flavored coffee. I happen to favor it over all brands at coffee stand. To my big disappointment the flavor is so subdued that you can't even guess which one from the variety pack you are drinking. A big disappointment.

Assumed it would be a mi of flavors and regular coffee. All fruity flavored coffee. Not good. And they would not allow me to exchange it. So now I'm stuck with $40 worth of coffee that I'm not going to drink.

Good price for a pack of two. However after sampling lots of different brands, my two preferred are Starbucks and Caribou. It all depends on your personal taste preference. I suggest a variety pack if you're not sure.
nice to have a veriety for your morning cup! Just love it.  Not a fan of French Vanilla but all the rest wee great!
I have tried many different K Cups and I always go back ro the Variety Pack, not only for me but I have something different for friends, love it.

Summary: If the name says "variety" -- shouldn't there be some variety?
Text:
My real complaint is not with the coffee that's in the box, as much as with the coffee that isn't in the box. Time to break out the dictionary and look up "variety."

This is Green Mountain -- who make how many different varieties of flavored coffees in k-cups? 12? 16 during the winter months? How about a box with 2 of every favor? Or even 1 of every flavor available, including the regionals? That's variety. This is just too few of too few choices.

The best in the box is the hazelnut.  After that is the French Vanilla.  Both have a very fine flavor and brew well. The Rainforest Nut tends towards a bitter edge that makes it come across as a sub-par coffee.

Overall, Amazon's prices on K-Cups are very good compared to retail stores.  This coffee variety pack is very good, but Green Mountain coffee overall is not that strong compare to Gloria Jean K-Cups and bold types.  If you like a stronger, bolder coffee, these are not for you.  Try Extra Bold Dark Magic by Green Mountain if you want to go that route.

This variety pack contains an assortment of popular flavored coffees (Hazelnut Cream, French Vanilla and Rain Forest Nut).  Flavors are good and do not overwhelm the coffee flavor.  This is the second time I've ordered the variety pack.  I enjoy the different flavors and my guests like having a selection from which to choose.
Purchased this coffee for my Keurig machine, great coffee and was cheaper than any other website I could find

Variety is the name of the game for me. That is why I like the Keurig system so much--I don't have bags of coffee going stale. This Green Mountain Flavor variety offers three of my favorites in one collection: French Vanilla, Hazelnut, and Rain Forest Nut--yummy. For a real treat, in your travel mug try blending a couple flavors.

GM is always an eye opener coffee for me-robust, but mellow. The flavors don't take away from their coffee's like they do for some.

The value of this particular deal was awesome too--all K-Cuppers are always looking for deals. You don't get one box, you get TWO.

Gosh, all this writing about the coffee has made want another cup! Enjoy.

Folks in the office, including yours truly, found these to be cloying and artificial tasting. Regardless of which flavor you select, they all have the same underlying maple flavor. Some people love flavored coffees, and maybe, with a lot of sugar, these would float your boat. True coffee afficionados will pass on these.
The coffee cups I received were not what I wanted and produced dissapointing coffee - flavor-wise.

Summary: GMCR - Best Coffee East of Seattle
Text: "Have you tried this coffee?  Have you tried that coffee?"  Yes... I have.  And Green Mountain Coffee is still the best.  These variety packs to use with the Keurig offer great variety and great flavors.

I like this variety pack better than Gloria Jeans.  It is a bit stronger than GJ's.  But still not as strong as I like my coffee.  I still enjoy it anyway.  The others in my office like it fine but they are not fans of strong coffee like I am.

Summary: Lion Coffee is the world's best
Text:
If you are a coffee Connoisseur, then you should be drinking Lion 100% Kona. My wife is from O'ahu, and if anyone asked her what the best Hawaiian coffee company is, she would not have to even think-LION KONA.

It has a flavor like no other coffee on the planet. Bold, but not bitter. It has a mellow after-taste, and a hint of sweetness. I swear to you it tastes like someone bottled up a Kailua Beach sunrise so you can sip it up on the mainland.

Onolicious for your opu!

I really wanted to like this stuff... I am a huge broccoli cheese fan and even once I added additional frozen broccoli it couldn't make up for the sins of the soup base.  Dixie Carb Counters - please reformulate this and i'll be happy to buy it and write a better review :)
this item was a real disappointment, it smells bad, tastes bad, looks bad, after preparing it looks very watery, portions are quite small, i threw the while thing out!

I first received this cheese from a cheese club. Tasted so good I actually went hunting for it online because it's not available locally. The price threw me a bit but decided I was well worth it. The cheese has the perfect amount of saltiness to suit my taste. I use it grated on everything that I would normally grate cheese on - and some things that don't normally get cheese. Shreds of it in a salad give the dish a boost. I've added it to macaroni and cheese, grilled cheese sandwiches, and cheese grits! Have not found anything yet that it's not good with. It's great just to nibble on also.
I used this rice for a paella dish and it was delicious... it was a real crowd pleaser :o)
It is what it is. Does what it should. Could be better but it also could be more expensive. All in all, I'm happy.

Summary: best organic soba noodles I've yet found
Text: I still am looking for the fabled organic 100% buckwheat soba noodles. But until then, these are what I'll be eating. The ten pound box is great - small, no extra packaging, but it will keep you in soba for a good long time even if you're a complete fiend. (This is not speculation, I tested it.)

Who knew dog food could be this delicious, this nutritious, this fun to serve? How can you go wrong with a product named "Stella & Chewy's" -- the name alone makes you want to hug the package.

But dogs can't read. So the real test came when I opened the package and popped out the dry, puck-sized wafer and put it in front of Madeleine, our 4.5 lb Papillon. Madeleine gobbled it down like she hadn't had a thing to eat in months. Sold.

What's in the wafers? Freeze-dried, RAW farm raised chicken with no imitation anything. It's also CERTIFIED safe raw and pathogen free food.

Do I trust those words? In today's FDA-scammed market, they aren't what they used to be. And yet, the whole package just seems to ooze with clues this company is ethical, responsible, progressive, and aware of the potential damage "ordinary" dog food brings to the table. I just have a feeling this company knows more about perfecting the domestic dog diet than I do.

This stuff is "Made in Wisconsin" according to the emblem on the front, but there's French writing all over the place. That's because Stella & Chewys' LLC is exporting their gourmet dog food to France, complying with French law by pointing out that it is indeed "Fabrique aux Etats-Unis" and it is "Nourriture pour chiens".

Given the exchange rate and the shipping costs, by the time it reaches the Left Bank, it must cost a bundle. And worth every Franc.

Botttom line: I think these people at Stella & Chewy's care about the same things I care about. That may be irrelevant in the business world. Profits are hard enough to come by these days.

But they aren't cutting any corners in Chewy's Chicken Dinner. Because it's a healthy blend of this, that and the other thing, it's even healthier than, say, pure Chicken or Steak right off the dinner table. This has fruits and vegetables mixed in (organic blueberries, apples, carrots, squash, beets, broccoli, cranberries and pumpkin seeds). That's important for a happy, healthy dog. No wonder Madeleine is hooked.

My dog is on a raw diet, which is impractical when traveling. I feed Stella & Chewy's freeze-dried food during trips and it works out beautifully. The patties may be re-hydrated or fed dry - my dog loves them either way.

IMO the true measure of dog food's quality is the dog's "output." I'm happy to report that whenever my dog eats this food for a few days his stools are *normal* without any dietary upset whatsoever, despite the fact there's often stress involved in travel.

Some people feed this food as a main diet, but it can get expensive depending on the size of your dog.

If you're dabbling in raw feeding or need a practical alternative for traveling, buy Stella & Chewy's without hesitation. It's a great product and all of the flavors are delicious according to my dog. :-)

Mostly I use this broken up into small pieces for training treats.  However, this also makes a great addition to my dog regular food.  Either way, my normally very picky eater really loves this stuff.
My dog Timmy likes it, and that's a pretty strong endorsement.  I like it because it is good for him and not messy.  That's a winning combination. :)

This product clearly says: 1 "Stella & Chewy's Freeze Dried Dog Food for Adult Dogs, Lamb Patties, 6 Ounce Bag (Pack of 12)"
A pack of 12 was not sent. Only one 6 ounce bag was received.

A friend of mine got a free bag of this of gave me a few patties that i crumbled to serve as treats, he loved them so much that i searched for a deal and bought him a couple of bags. He LOVES them. Firstly, if my dog was not a toy size dog I would not be feeding him this very often, it is EXPENSIVE. For my 8lb it would be 3 large bags a month, $80. So no way. I find a way to get discounts and it ends up being $60/mo for an 8lb pup.

The packaging says your dog should drink 1/4 cup water for every patty, so i make sure i serve them re-hydrated so that i don't have to worry that he's drinking enough water afterward. He gobbles it up without fail.

They are easy to measure, for my dog's size he eats about 3 1/4 patties a day, I break the patty into quarters and put them in water to rehydrate; they are ready to serve in less than 2 minutes. The ingredients are awesome and not only do they include all the meat products as the first ingredients but then vegetables that follow are organic. And to top it off they include probiotics for intestinal health.

I can't report any increase in energy or anything like that because my dog is only 2 years old so he's got all the energy in the world. But i love that raw-type foods, even if not the frozen kind, are very easy to digest compared to dry food, that's always better for the system.

Anyway, we've only tried this flavor so far, duck is next. : )

Ingredients:
Chicken Ground with Bone, Chicken Liver, Chicken Gizzard, Pumpkin Seed, Potassium Chloride, Organic Cranberries, Organic Spinach, Organic Broccoli, Organic Beets, Sodium Phosphate Monobasic, Organic Carrots, Organic Squash, Organic Apples, Organic Blueberries, Choline Chloride, Dried Pediococcus Acidilactici Fermentation Product, Dried Lactobacillus Acidophilus Fermentation Product, Dried Bifidobacterium Longum Fermentation Product, Dried Enterococcus Faecium Fermentation Product, Taurine, Tocopherols (Preservative), Calcium Carbonate, Zinc Proteinate, Zinc Sulfate, Iron Sulfate, Iron Proteinate, Vitamin E Supplement, Niacin, Copper Sulfate, Copper Proteinate, Manganese Sulfate, Sodium Selenite, Manganese Proteinate, Thiamine Monohydrate, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride, Vitamin D3 Supplement, Calcium Iodate, Vitamin B12 Supplement. (42% Protein, 25%)
We moved and were no longer able to buy the raw patties. We tried these "dry" patties and our dog can't tell the difference. Easy to prepare for our dog. You add water, microwave and that's it!

Summary: The end to my search for dog food!!
Text:
I have been trying all kinds of dog food to get my pick little chihuahua to eat something nutritious. Nothing was working. Then I discovered Stella & Chewy's Freeze Dried Chicken Patties and HE BLEW THROUGH THEM!!!

I think we have a winner here! I am going to order some of the other flavors to give him some variety. Hope he likes them as well.

The chicken dinner is one of several from Stella and Chew's that I tried after my dog rejected a long line of excellent dog foods. He is healthy and has an excellent appetite but prefers people food. He also likes the beef, lamb and other varieties of this dinner. He looks great and has lots of energy. I'm delighted.

It was hard to find a raw food that my yorkie would stick too and because we traveled it made it even more difficult! Thankfully stella & chewy was the only food that she ate and have continued to eat for months! Also its so easy to travel with because so it makes everything super convenient. Also her transition from her previous raw was smooth and she had no problems with her stools. Not only does she like chicken, but she likes the duck and surf & turf. I keep the beef and lamb around too but she mostly prefers the chicken. Overall great company and great product!

I have 2 older dogs that are so picky and one dog has no teeth and this product is wonderful..I mix it with canned food or as a treat and it doesn't upset their tummies! They love this and I plan on buying more! Our cat even likes it!
My dog eats the frozen Stella and Chewy's but I can't travel with them so I get the Freeze Dried. They don't need refrigeration, are easily re-hydrated and my dog loves them

This sugar-free Halva by Achva is absolutely delicious!  My husband and I both loved it and ate a little every day, while it lasted.  The texture is nice and the taste is mild and not too sweet. We found it in a little European market in Florida but now have to order it, since it's not sold in our area, at least not that I've found yet.  Definitely one of our favorite treats - and so much more healthful than most!

I bought the Kettle Corn variety Pop-Up Bowl. The first bag I tried to pop totally burned within 12 seconds (with smoke pouring out of the microwave), well before it was even fully popped, and the second bag, which I set on a lower temperature (even though it specifically says to use HIGH) actually caught on fire! Avoid this fire trap product at all costs. To avoid throwing all the rest of the bags out, I settled for cutting the bags open, scraping the contents into a heavy, lidded-skillet, and cooking it old-school. Those came out fine, as there's nothing the matter with the popcorn, just the packaging. So, unless you have a desire to destroy a perfectly good microwave, and possibly burn down your house in the process, avoid this packaging at all costs. Mark my words, this is going to come up in the future. The Orville Redenbacher brand is going to see lawsuits for this one! I wanted to give it ZERO STARS, but the program wouldn't let me! Be forewarned!

I'm a sucker for convenience, but with two kids and a job - do you really blame me? I'm the stereotypical busy mom, and I thought these would be great. I bought the popcorn in early August but quickly forgot about it as we moved into the fall months. While cleaning our pantry, I re-discovered them.

Today I thought it would make a great addition to my lunch. I went to the break room, popped it on and waited patiently.

It was still popping when I pulled out, but it just smelled burnt.

To my surprise, it was. Not only that, but the bag had sprung a leak. Unpopped kernels and butter leaked out. Had I let it go the full 2 minutes, we would have been facing a massive fire. Cleaning the microwave after that was bad enough, but having to deal with the possible problems it could have caused? Even worse.

I've only used one bag, but I'm throwing the rest of the box away. A fire hazard isn't worth it.

Summary: Orville is rolling in his grave
Text: So far, I've popped two bags (bowls) and both times, I've ended up with burnt popcorn, and many, many unpopped kernals.  These two things (burnt popcorn and large volumes of unpopped kernals) shouldn't occur together.  My guess is that this is the result of the grey heat reflector portion of the bag being smaller to accomodate the removable "bowl" lid.  So there is less surface area for the popcorn to be in contact with this reflector.  I will definitely not be purchasing any more boxes of these dumb "bowls" in the future.  It was a good idea, but very poorly executed.  Orville is surely rolling in his grave over the number of unpopped kernals with his name on them!

A few observations on this product:
- The pop-up bowl sells for a premium over the regular bag version yet it seems to be worse.
- Is this really a bowl or just a paper bag held sideways? There is big difference between the portrayal on the package and the product inside. The "bowl" end result will not look like the package illustration but more like a paper hat partially filled with popcorn.
- The product did not cook as well as the bag version and actually came out a bit scorched. It seems to make less popcorn than the bag version, and is definitely not like portrayal of the product on the box in which popcorn overflows from the "pop-up bowl."

Overall, this product seems like an interesting idea that was executed on the cheap. And the problem is compounded by charging a premium to the consumer. The company is degrading its image by putting out this product under the Orville Redenbacher brand name.

It should be illegal to sell this product. It's a fire hazard and lawsuit waiting to happen! The popcorn burns, the bag burns, the butter burns. And then how do you put it out. the top and bottom are made of plastic which gets terribly hot, put it under the faucet and you got wet paper and popcorn all over.

Redenbacher used to be a trusted brand, but with ConAgra taking over, it seems that the brand name is being used to shill inferior product.

This is a total disappointment of what could have been a good product.  I have tried this on two different microwaves both same result.  Burned in the middle and won't pop fully.  Don't bother, go back to the original style bag.

Summary: Sprayed orange grease all over the inside of the microwave
Text:
The pop-up bowl sounds like a great idea, but evidently they rushed it to market before all the bugs were out.

The first bag I cooked was fine, except the instructions for opening the bag are far from clear, and even after you figure out how to do it it's a lot of trouble and makes a big mess.

But the second bag evidently sprang a leak - it sprayed bright orange grease all over the inside of my microwave, even into the tiny vent holes inside the top and side. I always watch popcorn carefully while it pops, but I could not see the grease spray until after it was done and I opened the door. Cleaning it all out was a horrible ordeal, and I'm sure everything I cook in the microwave will come out smelling like popcorn grease for weeks.

They released this product too soon. It needs serious redesign. I will not buy it again.

When the popping sounds slow down, it's too late--the popcorn in the middle is burnt! The package is somewhat awkward to open. Some of the popcorn usually ends up on the counter. I love Orville's popcorn--no one does it better, but please don't keep this package design!

I loved the idea of popcorn that would pop in its own bowl. I gave it a try tonight as I settled in to watch a movie. The first thing I noticed as it popped was that the sides of the bag were a red see through type of material so you could see the popcorn popping. Not sure if that's needed but I liked it so it was a plus. The "bowl" was disappointing though. Essentially, its just a bag of popcorn that you place on it's side, rip the side off & you eat the popcorn this way so you have a wide opening to eat from. Problem is, where you tear the side off doesn't work well. I followed the directions and found the area that is supposed to rip off didn't go smoothly & part of it didn't tear where it should & I ended up having to go back & rip more areas off, etc. Perhaps with practice you can get it right but it was a little underwhelming. The popcorn was a little bland also. Great idea but poor design. Hopefully someone will improve on it.

Either the people who have reviewed this product are idiots, or they've greatly improved the product design by the time I bought it. Please take note. The 'popcorn button' on your microwave sucks. Stand there for the 2-3 minutes it takes and listen for the popping to slow. When there's 10-15 (if not less) delay in between, you have perfect popcorn.

The bowls were nice. The top ripped off easily all but one time. Don't know what happened there, but I'm willing to chalk it up to a human error on my part. The only part I didn't like was they left very little room to shake up the popcorn and equally distribute salt.

The bowl bag does not pop in the same amount of time as a normal bag so it makes your microwave's popcorn button useless. Additionally, about half of the bags are faulty and open when popping resulting in very little popped popcorn. Last, I have found it almost impossible to get the bag to pop completely even when watching it pop (since I can't use the popcorn button!). Overall, this new bowl design is terrible and I would recommend switching to another brand until they go bag to the old bags that work.

In all of the groceries that I've been to in my area, these new "Pop-Up Bowls" of popcorn are replacing the traditional bags.  But the price for the new bowls is always the same as the price for the old bags, and there was 13% more popcorn in the older bags (3.3 oz bags, vs. 2.9 oz bowls).  This seems to be another in a series of sly moves by food retailers to disguise significant price hikes by subtle quantity reductions, like Tropicana did when they reduced their cartons from 64 oz to 59 oz.  The old bags were fine, and I'd much rather have 13% more popcorn than the new bowl.  If Redenbacher had been honest about the price hike, and charged 13% more but kept the quantity the same; or if they offered a choice between the old larger bags and the new smaller bowls instead of outright replacing the bags with the bowls, then I could respect this change.  But given how they've made this change, I'm shopping for a new brand (Central Market, mabye?).

The popcorn was good and this was a great invention, except for the fact, there is red plastic on both the top and bottom of the bowl.  The red plastic dyed the countertop red.  This is not safe for furniture.  They should fix it or put a warning on the packaging.  Sent in a complaint to the company.  We'll see what I hear back.

My teenage daughters think this is the best-tasting microwave popcorn there is (although it's a bit buttery for my tastes as I'm used to the dry diet kind) and they love the bowl.

It felt awkward to pull the top off the first time, but now that we've done it about a dozen times, it's really easy. Hold the bag where indicated and pull the red plastic up from one corner. It's neatest if you pull it about halfway and then repeat from the other side, otherwise a few pieces inevitably end up on the counter. This takes a total of about 5 seconds, there's nothing to wash, and it's much easier to eat.

Summary: Better than the current formula in the grocery store
Text:
I've never purchased this via Amazon, but we used to live in Waco, TX and were able to buy this at the Dr. Pepper Museum there (Dr. Pepper was invented in Waco). Summary: Will gladly pay the extra price
Text: I'll gladly pay the extra $$$ for one last sip of America's greatest soda! R.I.P. Dublin Dr Pepper shame on you Dr Pepper Snapple!

After trying Dublin Dr. Pepper, even if I hadn't given up HFCS and wasn't allergic to Nutra-Sweet, I would never go back to drinking "regular" Dr. Pepper again. There's even a difference between the Dublin version and the "Heritage"/"throwback" versions that Dr. Pepper Snapple produce from time to time. The Imperial cane sugar makes a huge difference. This is so much better than what I've been used to.

Update 10/21/2011:
I just got my second shipment. I was going through withdrawals after the first one ran out about 2 weeks ago. This stuff is addictive. If you cannot afford to keep this habit, you probably shouldn't start it.

Update 4/25/2012:
Sadly, Dublin Dr. Pepper is no more. Dr. Pepper Snapple sued them and as part of the "settlement," Dublin no longer produces this soda. The bottler who was actually doing the work for Dublin Dr. Pepper also makes this soda with the same cane sugar but different packaging, but so far I've been unable to find any for sale on Amazon. I'll be kind to Amazon and not list their competitors name, but there is another site on the web that does sell the Dr. Pepper Imperial Cane Sugar version. Hopefully Amazon will do so soon.

So, I grew up in Houston, and was weaned to Coca-Cola, which like every other respectable soda, was made with real cane sugar, Imperial even, because of the cane fields and processing plant SW of Houston. Think late 40s, early 50s timeline. Howard Hughes was brewing Grand Prize beer and Golden Age soft drinks in orange, grape and strawberry (which was called "Big Red" by my name-unconscious younger brother). All soda came in 6 or 8 ounce bottles, except Royal Crown (RC) Cola, whose big marketing ploy was a 12 ounce bottle - "Twice as much for the same price!" In the summer, we would visit our grandparents in Erath County, only 14 miles from the golden hub - the Dublin Dr Pepper Company. The neighborhood grocery sold Dublin DP, and my grandfather was very fond of it. If we wanted a Coke, we had to cross the street and buy it ourselves. I drank DDP rather than blow my movie money on a difference of opinion. As we got older, we spent fewer summer weeks at our grandparents' house, playing dominoes and drinking DDP. That elusive flavor called to me, Mr. Pibb, various store brands that promised to taste the same, but they failed the test. For nearly 2 years I lived in the Dublin "territory" in the 70s. Then I moved to Austin. About 30 years ago, my father, looking for retirement, bought 3 farms in Hamilton County.
When we went to visit, we would bootleg Mr.Pibb into Dublin territory. Once I discovered Hamilton County was located in DDP territory,I gave up Mr. Pibb and began doing calculations on how many cases we had to take home each visit so we didn't run out before the next trip. I began to travel everywhere with the car half-filled with Dr Pepper and the rest with husband, self, a litte baggage and a few dogs. I actually flew to MA to attend a fellowship course at Tufts Vet Med School. Earlier ventures east of the Mississippi and north of
the Tennessee had blown it into my face that they didn't carry that pansy-assed tea party fare in those parts. A major fast food chain had never heard of it. But one of the doctors at Tufts actually drank DP! And he wouldn't share it at our box lunch socials. I one-upped him with Dublin DP, and while I wouldn't share either, I sent him a case from Texas. Next year, he came to a conference in Texas and looked for DDP everywhere. I finally told him the territorial secret and gave him Willie Kloster's Dublin factory address. I don't know if he could afford it on a vet/professor's salary (the shipping will kill you), but at least he had tasted Heaven. I gave up alcohol, inherited a farm in DDP territory,and changed my life, dedicating myself to good deeds. Is that a witness or not! Truly, I love Dublin Dr Pepper, and met Willie Kloster on a plant tour, complete with a cold bottle of his brew from the machine (he put up the dimes). On a side note, James Lee Burke's Dave Robicheaux likes Dr Pepper over crushed ice, but he doesn't have access to the good stuff. You don't water it down. Maybe he would have stopped drinking sooner if Willie could have sold his product in LA. Insert silly emoticon here. Dublin Dr Pepper has about a 1% share of Snapple Dr Pepper sales, but other distributors see Willie's original formula as a threat and are suing to restrict sales of Dublin Dr Pepper to the original 6 counties and to take Dublin out of the name. Never happen. It is the greatest stuff ever, and will persist in the environment as long as DDT, but it is better for you.
This is great stuff NOT to be shared.  It is very pricey but very good.  It makes the new stuff pale by comparison.

If you prefer Dr. Pepper, you need to try this cold and fresh at least once. Drink one of these a day for six days and good luck going back to regular without missing it.

I never realized this, but the salt and mineral concentration of seawater is different in each part of the world, and therefore the taste of sea salt varies based on where it comes from.

To me, "French gray" sea salt is delicious - the flavor is more gentile than regular salt and has a slightly tangy taste with just a hint of minerals. The price may seem high compared to table salt, but Amazon's price is low compared to other places I've bought it. Definitely worth it, in my opinion.

One thing to note is that this sea salt is very moist, so it doesn't work well in a grinder or shaker. Sometimes I'll serve it in a salt cellar, but generally I just keep it in a glass jar by the stove for cooking and use regular salt at the table.

Text: These sticks don't smell like peanut butter at all, so my dog didn't like them... though she goes absolutely gaga over real peanut butter. He goes for them first in his treat cupboard now so for me they were a good investment.  He likes them and they don't bother his digestion!

Text:
Very good value for the quantity, so I tried them. My chihuahua loves them, ... but as I watched, he goes through one in 2 minutes or LESS. Gone.

For people who dislike flavored coffee this might be a good choice (though why would those people be looking at this product I'm not sure...) The description has one thing right - "hint of caramel". With this subtle a hint, I don't think anyone would guess it was caramel flavored coffee without reading the label.

Summary: Caramel Flavor So Mild, It Barely Exists...
Text:
I love a cup of Starbucks coffee, and I love a good flavored coffee. When Starbucks announced Natural Fusions Ground Coffee, I really looked forward to purchasing and tasting it. Caramel-flavored coffee is one of my personal favorites - as long as it is not sickenly artificial, e.g. Ghirardelli Chocolate Caramel flavored coffee. Based on my experience with regular Starbucks ground coffees, I was sure Starbucks would be able to produce an excellent flavored coffee.

Unfortunately, I feel Starbucks missed the mark. The Caramel Flavored Natural Infusions Ground Coffee has almost no caramel odor and has even less caramel taste. Since the coffee I purchased was just being put onto the grocer's shelf, I know it was fresh and had not lost scent or flavor due to aging. In an attempt to be sure my dissatisfaction was not due to drinking my coffee black with sweetner only, I added cream to the cup. This did nothing to enhance or elevate the intensity of the caramel flavor. Because the coffee does have a mild caramel tone, it actually has a bit of a burnt taste.

I am less than pleased with Starbucks Natural Fusions Caramel Flavored coffee and have rated it as an average brew. If you are interested in trying this coffee, visit the manufacturer's and put the word "fusions" in the search box. You will be able to print two coupons for $1.50 off a bag of this coffee so that you can decide for yourself whether Starbucks has produced a brew that meets its usual quality standards.

Summary: Strange Color, Smells Weird, Bad Aftertaste
Text: To give a bit of credit the side of the bag explains that the coffee is a dark roast flavored with burnt sugar, licorice root, orange peel, cinnamon and nutmeg - not quite the delicious buttery caramel that they picture on the front. I feel it's deceiving though - the coffee looks unusually dark, has a strange chemical smell [perhaps from the licorice, but I love licorice and this smells like a solvent] and a noticeably bad aftertaste. Even with extra cream. For the eight bucks I paid in-store I'd rather have bought some Folgers and a bag of Werthers caramels to mix in - would have been a better value.

There is no Starbucks in my town, and this is the next best thing. It beats every other ground coffee on the shelf. Also, I save my empty bags so when I visit a town with a Starbucks, I can get a free cup of coffee! Rewarding responsibility is a great thing.

Summary: Don't be fooled by EntirelyPets $2.99 Price for these!
Text: I ordered three sets of these from EntirelyPets.  I even called them to confirm that the $2.99 price was in fact for 24 of these and was told YES.  When my order arrived, it had only one per set, not 24.  They keep changing their price here from $2.99 with $5.98 shipping to $66.00 with free shipping.  It seems like a bait and switch to get more orders because if you look at their reviews, you'll find that others also purchased these for $2.99 for 24 and received only one.  I even called to confirm and was told I'd get what is stated, yet I didn't.  When I followed up with them after receiving my order, I was told it was a "price mistake". When a vendor keeps making the same "pricing mistake" over and over, you have to start to wonder if it's a mistake or a bait and switch.  The item is fine, but not worth $2.99 plus $5.98 shipping for ONE, especially when the site specifically states that it is for 24 and even their own customer service stated I would receive 24 per set ordered.  I am submitting this review to warn others and to highlight to Amazon what EntirelyPets is doing.

Summary: Fine taste at an everyday price
Text:
I have tried every tea commercially available, at every price point. I have even received tea directly from China. But, for consistent quality and fine taste, every single day, nothing beats Taylors of Harrogate and my favorite of their many excellent teas is Pure Assam.

Taylors was founded in London in 1886 and today is the largest family-owned tea and coffee business in the UK. Not only do they get their leaves from original sources in Asia and Africa, but they run a model business that gives back through a variety of worthy charities and has been repeatedly named among the top 100 companies to work for. It is no wonder that their tea is so fine.

Best of all is its price. You can get more expensive and fancier tea (I've done it!) but you cannot get better tea.

"Once I had Assam, I have been spoiled to drink any other tea and once I had Taylors of Harrogate, I have been spoiled to any other brand of Assam".

Summary: Excellen black tea, plain no milk or surgar
Text: A good cup of tea in the afternoon to me is a bit of heaven.  My old standby for years has been Tetley's British Blend.  I then spent a month in Egypt, where they love their tea.  I came away craving Lipton Yellow Label loose tea, which seemed to be a favorite in Egypt.  The Yellow Label's a bit on the strong side so I usually add a bit of sugar.  Then one day,I found a unopened pouch of Taylor's Pure Assam Tea on the window sill.  My wife goes out with her girl friends to these decadent over priced tea houses where they have tea, sweets and plenty of gossip.  Well the pouch of Taylors had arrived via one of those tea houses.  Actually it had been on that window sill for at least a month before I somehow of other decided to try it.  Boy, talk about surprised, it was really good, no milk, no sugar, just tea.  It had all the qualities of a perfect tea, just strong enough, taste was of that magical flavor that has tea the choice of billions of people around the world.  This was one of the best teas I had ever tasted.

In another review, I chanted the quality of Taylor's Lapsang; well when I ordered my normal two boxes of Lapsang, I figured I would branch out and try something I had never tried before.

It was a good decision on my part.

I use no milk or sugar in my cuppa anything, so if it tastes like dishwater I'll notice.

This Assam tea is a full bodied tea that is just as enjoyable as all the other Taylor's teas I have had. They sell enough of it that I have never had a stale box of Taylor's tea delivered.

As I mentioned in the other review, their consistency is remarkable; the next box tastes just as I remembered the last box.

I keep my teas as fresh as possible; for me it really makes a difference.

Pricier than some, but worth the difference.

Taylors of Harrogate products are always excellent.  The best quality teas delivered promptly. Not cheap -but you haveto pay for quality and the teabags make plenty of tea ( a good pot size). Excellent.

Summary: Cleared my Dogs Eyes Right Up! No more RX's for Her!
Text:
My dog loves this....and so do we! Miki has been having problems for over a year with the skin just outside of her tear ducts getting red, then raw...poor thing. Each time I'd take her to the vet, (2 different vets just to see), they both prescribed the same eye drop medicine ($27.00) for a tiny bottle. But, it never cleared up entirely, and the minute I'd stop with the drops, after weeks of applying 2-3 x's a day, it would come right back. Looking at her made me feel terrible.

Then, I started thinking about maybe it was something she is eating, even though I've been feeding her Ceasar for a couple years and thought it to be a "good" dog food. But after researching what was in Wellness dog food compared to the store bought stuff, I couldn't believe I was feeding her that stuff!
So, after doing the math, a 3oz tub of Ceasar vs the 12 1/2 oz can of Wellness, I could get 3 bigger servings (4.1 oz each) out of a can of Wellness...for the same, or better price, and it was way healthier for her!

Our Miki looks so pretty again (Papillon) and seems she has a whole lot more energy too! I figure it must be the change in diet that helped clear up her eyes but wasn't sure because we moved at the same time (same town) and I thought it might have been some plants/allergies she was getting into in the back yard. But....I let myself run out of Wellness (not on purpose!) and had to feed her something else, so I went with the Ceasar and ordered her some more Wellness. By the time I placed and received my order, (not much more than a week), the skin below her eyes had already broken out again! Ummmm...CONFIRMATION! And guess what? Within 2 weeks after our Wellness shipment arrived, and she was back eating her favorite dog food, Miki's tear duct area was dried up, rawness gone, and hair was growing back!

I don't even remember how I stumbled across this dog food, and who would have ever thought I'd be ordering dog food from Amazon, but with the great price, and free super saver shipping, like I said earlier, it's the same price as that store bought "stuff", but she gets more than an ounce more per serving and look at the ingredients...it's real chicken, and sweet potatoes! (A lot of other good for her stuff!)

I'm sold on Wellness (so is Miki~she loves it!) I had just come back online to re-order some more Wellness Chicken and Sweet Potato food, when I thought that I should take a moment to RAVE about this great stuff.
So I did!

well I gave this product 4 stars because the purpose I used it for was not intended. I saw that it had 95% meat which was perfect (in my mind) for a cat diet, and the price point was nearly half of that which is for cats.

FTR: Cats and dogs have two completely and vastly varied nutritional needs, in my research I recall reading that a cat's diet is mainly 95% meat (from which they derive their moisture/water from as well) since cats hunt and eat small rodents and birds in nature this makes sense, since the 5% veggie content is likely from eating cat grasses and the contents of their prey's tummy at the time of death.

I decided to purchase this food since it was only 2.56 a can at Unleashed and I figured I would just add in a calcium supplement, and taurine, and cat vitamin supplement to make up for the missing bones which would provide the natural calcium source for cats, and taurine since I don't believe dogs require as much taurine in their diets as cats would and vitamins to make up for the possibility that there may not be enough vitamins in just meat alone.

My cats loved it. I have one very finicky girl kitty whom refuses to eat human foods (which is a good thing) and most junky cat foods (another good thing) and one male cat that eats whatever he can get his whiskers into. They both liked this. So I would consider feeding this to them in lieu of the more expensive cat foods (after I compare the ingredients of this to that of cat foods and make up the missing vitamins and minerals) however I am not happy with the fact that this cat food has the consistency of pate..

it is all ground up meats and looks like refried beans... I'm going to search for a similar product which has shredded meat rather than this consistency :)

Summary: Great food topper for my dogs
Text:

My wife and I bought a couple cans of this food for a few days when we were away from home with our dog. It is a little pricey, but then again this is definitely not meant as a daily meal - it even plainly says on the can to feed supplementally only!

PROS
- Our dog loves it!
- 95% chicken content, no fillers
- Perfect for road/camping trips
- No gastrointestinal discomfort that we could see

CONS
- Not human grade meat

It is important to understand the difference between quality in meats for dog (and cat) food. Much research has been done on the subject (easily found on Google), but my wife and I decided some months ago to only feed our dog human-grade meat, termed in the pet food industry as "inspected for human consumption". The chicken used in the wellness food is NOT inspected for human consumption, however since we have only fed our pup this twice, we aren't too worried. If Wellness switched to human-grade meat, I would happily give this the full five stars, and this is really the only criticism I could give for this product.

OVERALL
I would recommend this as an occasional food for your dog, with the one reservation noted above.
As a newly adopter of a one year old, I tried certain foods with not much success.  My dog loves this food, and I do too, as she eats well and healthy.

Summary: I Wasn't Sure About This One, but Wow!
Text:
Peanut Matcha. I was a little hesitant. I don't know what it is about the idea of peanut flavoring in a tea ... it just doesn't sound right to me. I am all for just about any other type of nut (yeah, I know that peanuts aren't technically nuts), but, peanuts just sounded too weird to me. Then I tried Peanut Taffy and this changed my whole idea of how good peanut flavor can taste.

So, I got the courage and I ordered this Matcha, and I'm pleasantly surprised. It's really quite good. Much better than I expected it to be. It is good prepared traditionally, with water and whisked well, but then after taking my first sip, I decided I wanted to find out what a pinch of salt might add to the flavor. And so I added a tiny pinch of sea salt and I LOVE this. It is really yummy!

Smooth, rich and creamy. Nice peanut flavor, balanced well with the fresh, leafy green taste of the Matcha. Really tasty - much tastier than I expected!

There are many claimants to the title of Best Kona Coffee. Like Lancelot searching for a king worthy enough to serve I have tried many Kona brands and found most to be wanting. When Starbucks was worth their reputation good Kona was available from them by phone order only. That was 15 years ago. It's been pretty disappointing but the good news is that Blue Horse Kona Coffee is making up for lost time. With a little imagination you can actually taste the black soil of Hawaii and feel the Trade Winds in this coffee. There is no other way to describe the smooth, delicious flavor and aroma that seems simple but has the complexity of a good wine wih several flavors one experiences during the beginning, middle and the wonderful finish.
This is a real find for anyone who loves coffee.  I just got turned on to it recently, and it's becoming my absolute favorite.  Smooth yet robust.  Something very special.

We are now on our third order and we have five people from my office ordering, as they too have become addicted to this special coffee. We share the cost of 5 pound orders (free shipping from Blue Horse directly), with our most resent order intended as an after dinner Thanksgiving treat for our family and friends. Then if the coffee wasn't good enough, I must add that the service from the folks at Blue Horse is fantastic, every order arrived with in days of its placement and each time the coffee was a fresh as it gets or at least tastes and smells that way. To say the least, IF you are truly a coffee frantic like I am, please do yourself and/or your family a favor and order some, you will not be disappointed and you will experience some of the best tasting coffee in the world. Then even if you don't like coffee, this would make an exceptional gift for someone who does. The medium roast is what we've ordered on our two prior orders but this time we've order 5 pounds of the dark roast, so we can compare and say we've had the best of both worlds. Once I've brewed a few pots of the dark, I will come back and update my posting, so everyone will have a review of both but as an FYI, you can order a pound of each and you do get free shipping with multi-pound orders. They also have a website and you can order directly from them, saving a little money over the Amazon price, plus the pictures and stories/history of the coffee alone is worth the visit to their site.

I have never dealt with a company that treats it customers as well as Blue Horse. They go above and beyond what is expected and have been a bright spot in my day. Thank you Blue Horse, you are exceptional!

Because the flavor of Blue Horse coffee is excellent, I can't justify reducing the number of stars in my rating. Just because the medium roast was too weak for my taste, doesn't mean it won't be perfect for someone else.

Text: This coffee is amazing!  It has a wonderful aroma that makes the whole room smell amazing.  The body has some earthy undertones but there is no bitterness to it at all.  It is one of the few coffees I can enjoy black.

I thought I'd give Blue Horse's 100% Kona Coffee a try since I had an Amazon gift certificate from Christmas. I was not disappointed! The aroma was fantastic and the flavor was incredible. The price was not out of line for such delicious coffee, but it's not something I could afford every day. And, just in case any of my family and friends are reading this review, yes - it IS the perfect gift for me :)
The coffee was flavorful yet not bitter as some darker roasts tend to be.  The aroma was great as well.  Great cup of coffee!
This is a top shelf coffee with a deep chocalate taste and a smooth aftertaste. I will buy it again when i can. I would recomend this product to anyone seeking a great gourmet bean.

This was some good Kona.

After tasting several cups of this brew, I made a pot of starbucks and decided to throw out over 1.5lb of starbucks in the trash.

This is a good bean from a good roaster.

Subtle flavor, easy sipping, good nose, and does not sit on the tongue.

enjoy.

The coffee is mild and fresh tasting.

I get subtle and mellow notes of netmeg, tamarind, and a banana-fruit finish.

This medium roast is very mellow and nutty. Low acidity, barely any bitterness.

I think this is a great deal, and I'm just as impressed by the fact that I actually know where my coffee is being planted, grown, raised, picked, and shipped from. I'm also very pleased that they roast to order, as the coffee comes to me fresh roasted and I get them in the 1st sniff as I opened the bag. Coffee arrived within a week of ordering, and I'm pleased with it.

I will continue ordering from this operation. My next order will probably be to try the dark roast and the peaberry Kona.

Summary: Best coffee to make at home
Text: I've had better coffee, but it was in Costa Rica or Hawaii. For making a fresh pot in the morning, absolutely NOTHING beats this stuff. It's well worth the price!

Aloha!
I like it. I recently visited Hawaii and some of the coffee plantations on Big Island. Maybe the Blue Horse coffee is not the best Kona coffee, but it's worth the money. I will definitely buy it again.

Delicious and balanced.  Not over-roasted.  Not too oily so it works well for super-automatic machines.  Arrived within three days.  This was my first order with them.  I'll review again if they show any inconsistencies in the future.
The product was receivede on time and meets my expectations. I tried the coffee this morning and enjoyed it very much.

Blue Horse medium roast is a five-star coffee if you compare it to the premium coffee beans you buy at the supermarket, but compared to its true peers the pricey Konas - it's a solid average in a world-class competition and would have gotten four stars from me. The price is reasonable and customer service is excellent: I raised my rating from four to five stars for that reason.

I just finished my first pound of this medium roast whole bean purchase. I found the aftertaste quite pleasing, much sweeter than bitter, and pleasantly unique. The balance for me was light and spirited and not overpowering. You do taste the coffee's unique flavors in a lighter roast like this so you need to enjoy that in your coffee - otherwise even a mellow coffee like this could seem a bit bitter due to unfamiliar tastes which are deliciously rich after you get used to them. If not, you always have the option of a darker roast since more roasting breaks down the unique coffee flavors gives it more of a Charbucks flavor... I believe "Blue Horse" has a dark roast also available if you want to try that instead.

For $25/pound Blue Horse medium roast is about the going rate for 100% Kona. I will be a repeat buyer because getting a dependable Kona at a reasonable price is not always as easy as it seems when dealing directly with small estates. And I like dealing directly with an estate coffee farm rather than a larger farm or coop since I know the exact origin of the coffee and it is more personal since most of the Kona farms are small and family run and in a tough economy with a premium product have their share of woes to deal with.

I have tasted better 100% Kona medium roasts, but usually they are $10 more per pound so I was pleased with my purchase. Being a dependable, decent quality Kona for the price is great, and the pesticide-free promise was worth something to me. The beans were nice, I didn't have a single broken one in the bag.

The claim that they roast basically weekly and immediately ship priority mail to get it to you fresh without jumping through hoops as I've had to do with others left me with a good impression overall. Mine was very fresh, definitely less than a week since roasting so I believe the claim. I put the half pound I was using in another one-way valve bag I reused from another quality coffee. To keep the rest fresh, I squeezed out all the air I could and then taped over the valve and put it in a second outer ziplock bag. The idea is to keep out water condensation which is how the flavor gets less than perfect. When I used the second half, I took it out of the freezer three weeks later, I let it come to room temperature before opening either bag. It isn't recommended to freeze coffee a second time so I didn't push it. The coffee I froze tasted almost as fresh as the first day though I actually could taste a minor difference. But I looked forward to this coffee right up to the last bean - was still great when using a coffee grinder each time just before making it.

I used 12.5 grams per cup to get the strength of the drip most to my liking (slightly under a half ounce). That makes 36 cups per pound, so it was currently generally between $0.70 to $0.86 per cup including shipping which is well worth it to me considering how much I'd pay at a place like Starbucks to get a cup in which the coffee was overroasted for my tastes and lucky to be as fresh on a good day for them.

Summary: It Pains Me to Write This Review
Text:
I held off writing this review until after I contacted Blue Horse and complained about these beans. I agree with the other one-star person that they are bland and rather tasteless beans. I contacted the farm and they replied immediately and they were very concerned. After answering a few questions they had about how I had prepared the coffee, etc., it became clear that there wasn't much they could do. They offered to send me a bag of the dark roast instead, but only if I returned the medium roast beans I had left.

I declined to do so--it isn't worth the trouble for me--but I will assume they simply wanted to check the beans to see if something was wrong.

As I told Blue Horse, coffee taste is subjective. So this review should be taken in that spirit. But I've had another brand of 100% Kona that I found to be the smoothest, toastiest, finest cup of coffee I've ever had. It's a shame that the label "100% Kona" coffee is not a guarantee that I'll be able to repeat that experience. I was truly looking forward to these beans.

I have to say that I was disappointed in this coffee.  The Kona coffee I remember was not at all bitter and had a unique taste.  This coffee was bitter and that unique Kona taste wasn't there.  As coffee goes, it wasn't bad, but not any better than I could get at Starbucks.

Summary: Nice aroma doesn't make up for acidic after-taste
Text: Having read the glowing reviews on Amazon, I ordered this coffee with great anticipation.  However, my wife and I found this coffee very disappointing.  The after-taste of this coffee is not just strong, but strangely acidic and off-putting. Based on the reviews, we expected a full and rounded taste on the pallet, but the coffee tasted almost bitter in the finish.  At $25 a pound, I cannot recommend this.

I have Blue Horse whole bean medium roast Kona on my wish list and received a pound as a gift. It's the first time I've had it, and I am not impressed. It had that papery, weak taste associated with under-roasted beans. I have experienced this phenomenon with other coffee beans as well.  I am disappointed in this product. Based on the high ratings given by other reviewers I must have received a bad batch, which doesn't speak well for such an expensive product. Packaging on the other hand was excellent.

Summary: totally bland, no aroma, should not have trusted high ratings
Text: My wife and I are Kona coffee lovers, Kona coffee with no cream no sugar, just that strong morning fresh coffee aroma and taste. I read some of the high ratings and ordered this coffee instead of Hawaii Roasters 100% Kona coffee, our normal Kona coffee. Did Blue Horse employees rate this coffee? My wife opened the new bag this morning and she said, unlike Hawaii Roasters, she could not smell that fresh smell of Kona cofee and worried it was not going to be very good. With Hawaii Roasters, whole house is filled with freshly brewed smell. Nontheless, I told her it received pretty good review in Amazon. She was right and I was wrong to order this product. First brew was so bland with no taste, pretty much like boiled water, no aroma of freshly brewed Kona coffee. I should have dismissed ratings and stayed with proven. I ordered Hawaii Roasters right away. I will have to throw away the rest of this 1 lb bag. Or maybe use as horse feedstock.

I discovered Vollrath dishers at Boxer-Northwest, a restaurant supply in Portland, Oregon. I had bought two similar looking dishers elsewhere for making Grand Marnier truffle, but on both of those the sweeps broke the first time I tried to scoop the cooled chocolate to form the cores. No such problems with this disher--I've done many batches of chocolates, and it keeps chugging along.

I own this model and the Vollrath #30. The size #50 is perfect for nice, big chocolates. I am sold on Vollrath durability. Many other brands look almost the same, but they are absolute junk. If you will be scooping something that is rough on the sweep of the disher, please try this brand.

Summary: My Favorite (not sure what can the other reviewers opened...)
Text: I'm a foodie and love this soup!  I avoid gluten, and had missed the comfort and taste of chicken noodle soup for years.  This is a real 'adult' chicken soup with nice-sized chunks of chicken, carrots and celery.  The picture on the label doesn't do justice to the rice -- the rice inside is a nice, textured, wild rice.  Sorry to see that the other reviewers had a bad experience, but I wonder if the cans they received were handled improperly because my experience doesn't resemble theirs at all.  I've eaten about 6 cans of this soup so far, and am now buying it by the case.

Summary: DO NOT PURCHASE with a dairy allergy!
Text:
I bought this ONLY because my grand daughter can not have any dairy at all and they said "no dairy" however, the can clearly says it uses dairy. I am ashamed that Amazon is allowing this to be sold and then refuses to accept a return.

Now I am stuck with 32.00 plus shipping for soup I could have bought at my local store, you have the chance to save yourself, so I suggest you do not buy this.....

This is just awful soup with so much black pepper, I nearly choked on it.  It had a burnt taste.  Very poor quality control on this item.  I was shocked because this brand's chicken broth is very good.

This is my first time trying Pacific Foods soups and maybe my last time.  I could not believe somebody would make this soup, package it and then sell it.  This soup is not consumable, and what makes it worse, it smells bad.  Honestly, I think dog food smells better.  I really do not think a dog would eat it either.  I put it in the fridge thinking I could come back to it and try it again - I could not do it.  I think the garbage disposer chocked on it also!  If I could give this soup a zero, I surely would.  Keep your money in your pocket.  Wolfgang Puck has much better organic soups.  I should have read the one review before I wasted [...] on this crap!  I am going to stick with their line of broths.

Matthew is a foodie; he is now 11 years old and has always been this way.  He would eat 24/7 if we let him, so we have to measure all his food.  As it is, he is pushing 20 pounds, although he is 19 inches from head to toe.  Purina is one of the brands I trust for food, having heard of no scandals like with some other brands.  The package says this food is good for the heart and immune system.  We feed Matt about half dry and half wet food because of concerns about male cats possibly having urinary tract problems if fed only dry food.  Matt will eat just about anything, so this chow is no exception.  I was surprised by how good this food smells, sort of like fresh wheat bread (okay, I am on a diet).  The price is good at $7.47 for a 7-pound bag with super saver shipping.  The expiration date is into 2013, but it will not last that long.

As well as most commercial dry cat food products, this is well tolerated by my 9 cats. (No, not 1 cat with 9 lives). This; however, contains grain products, so I also give them grain and gluten free dry and wet food, as well. Cats are "Carnivores" and do not, to my knowledge and experience, tolerate excessive amounts of grain.
There are more 'natural' products available, which are more costly, but you tend to get that, for which you have paid.

Summary: It's cat food. The cat ate it all. The dog did too.
Text: My cat ate it, so I'm happy. It was shipped free, (After I bought a few more things to make my total over $25, which is easy to do on Amazon). Not to shabby for 7 pounds of cat food. My picky cat won't eat "Store brand" food. She ate this just fine.
Cats love it and thats what important. Easy to select. Pleasant smell, also not strong. Convenient packaging and size. My cats have silky coats.

i not a cat person, i love dogs. but theres this alley cat that grown on me and i on him. i feed him, i bought him generic food he ate but no more than 1/2 cup a day not even that much (skinny cat). However i kid u not i got this bag out when generic ran out and the cat just ran to the bag sniffed and rubbed on it i put out for him to eat and he ate it like it wasnt nobodies business, he eats about 1 cup a day so thats good im trying to put wait on him. so next ill deworm him and flea him then see about vaccines, but for now hes a happy alley cat w/ his cat chow. i dunno why purina gets bad name. i used to feed puppy chow to my Pit Bull he loved it grew up on it and was very healthy muscular. now im getting a Staffy and deciding to feed him puppy chow or buffalo ill see. Good Luck Pet Lovers! Anybody want a cat? lol

A few years ago I made a huge lifestyle change. I used to eat everything in sight, loved processed food, never ate any fruits and few vegetables, was overweight and sluggish.
I started exercising and learned how to eat right, lost 90 lbs and never felt better in my entire life. I haven't had a single headache in the past 4 years, so I know how eating right is important.
So what does eating right mean? I don't eat red meat; use organic food whenever available; and stay away from processed foods.
Also, I have five meals a day (3 small main meals and 2 snacks), and I bag my lunch, usually a salad with a half chicken breast or fish, which I prepare the evening before.
Okay, sorry for the long intro, now I'm getting to the review of the product... sometimes I can't prepare my lunch, I don't have time or I don't have salad; so it's nice to have an alternative.
The gopicnic lunches are very convenient for that. Organic, calorie controlled, healthy, no trans fats, satisfying so they won't send you to the evil snack machine at the end of the hall.

Each package contains a little tub of salmon spread (quite tasty, a little sweet to my taste), Ritz-like crackers, a bag of dry-roasted edamame, a bag of trail-mix style fruit and nut mix, and a square of dark chocolate. There is also a plastic fork and even a puzzle at the bottom of the box, to keep you entertained after lunch!

Tastewise, it's not bad, although I wouldn't eat it too often; but I like keeping a few on the shelf as backup for the days when I don't have time to make lunch. Make sure to complement it with a piece of fruit though!

Summary: Easy nutritious meal for on the go
Text:
Eating nutritious meals on the go is difficult; eating "tasty" nutritious meals is even harder.
When I saw this product I was skeptical as to whether it would really taste good or be filling.
My thoughts about the product claims:
1) A balanced meal featuring chili lime salmon spread, organic crackers, fruit and nut mix etc - I really enjoy the different flavors and textures of the meal - no boring taste here!
2) All-natural; 22g protein, 11g fiber and only 410 calories - a good balance of nutrition and calories (much better than fast food!)
3) No trans fats; No artificial colors - I appreciate that it is all natural
4) Perfect for school lunch, field trips, sports games, road trips, lunch at work or after school - the Go Picnic is easy to tote along to anything you are doing away from home. It is shelf stable and does not need refrigeration which is a big plus!

Over all a great product with great taste that is good for you!

Summary: Go Picnic Not So Good For You
Text:
This ready to eat meal has a number of drawbacks, One the Sodium Level is 660mgs.

The Carbs are 48mgs. I would not call this a healthy snack or meal by any stretch of

the imagination. The taste of the salmon mixture is okay, the crackers taste good.

The snack mix and the little chocolate bar are the best of the lot here. Would I buy

this in a store? No I think not. First it is not really healthy, second it is too

expensive for what you get.

I do a lot of hiking and am preparing to walk in the 3-Day for the Cure so I thought I would give this product a try, besides, I like the turkey pepperoni GoPicnic product. Wow, was I disappointed in the salmon portion of the package. The salmon spread comes in a little carton like dipping sauces from a fast food restaurant - a plastic fork is provided to "spread" the product on to the crackers. The first thing I noticed was the strange color, sort of faded orange and unappealing looking. The next thing that surprised me was the consisteny - pretty much the same as cocktail sauce with tiny random flakes of salmon the were reminiscent of the horseradish in cocktail sauce. With so little actual salmon it seemed odd since the first ingredient listed is indeed "salmon." On to the flavor...if you LOVE Asian Fish Sauce you'll love this product as that is all I can taste. It feels "gummy" in the mouth and is all around unpleasant. Because everyone is mostly familiar with the other products in the box I won't comment on them but suffice it to say I won't be ordering this product again even though it arrived in a timely and pristine fashion. Pity.

This is another in a line of upscale on the go / "gourmet" box lunch. But there is really nothing too upscale or gourmet about this.

First you get a package of chili lime salmon spread. But it is not well mixed because you either get a bit of fishy salmon or the taste of chili lime sauce. Whatever they were trying, it did not work.

With the salmon spread, you get a package of six LAte July Organic Classic Rich Crackers. The crackers are fine but any health benefit from the organic is lost in the fat calories.

Next you have a package of Sweet Perry Orchards Ginger Zip & Nut Mix. This is a very standard dried fruit and nut mix.

You get a package of Seapoint Farms Dry Roasted Edamame. I know a lot of people who love edamame but I am not one of them and having dry roasted edamame is even worse. It tastes like dry soy beans without the flavour.

For desert you get Terra Nostra Organic Robust Dark Chocolate Square. This is the one thing that not only tasted good but had a great texture.

Overall, this is not a good meal replacement as the total calories of 410 and 16 grams of fat will not fill you up. All it will do is maybe be a sort of mid afternoon snack.

My advice is just to get a real meal.

Summary: The salmon is not what I hoped - Everything else is not bad
Text: The crackers, fruit and nut mix, the dry roasted edamame and the dark chocolate were OK. The salmon was oily yet it did not taste natural. It was also a relative small share of the entire box package. This is definitely a small snack even for one person. Like other reviewers, I would compare it to airline food.

This product is fine in a pinch - you want to go on an immediate picnic but are beyond throwing some PB&J in a basket.  Some portions of the meal work better than others -the crackers, trail mix, and desert were all good, but I wasn't a huge fan of the salmon spread.  It is nice to have the flexibility of not needing to refrigerate the meal, and it comes in a nice small box.

Summary: I really didn't like this at all
Text:
Do you remember when you were a child and you ate something that you instantly had to wipe off your tongue???? Well that's how I felt when I ate this GoPicnic meal. I had great hopes it was going to satisfy me. I was sadly mistaken. I am constantly on the go with dropping and picking up kids to and from school, practice, and whatever meeting either of us may have. I have been trying to avoid the drive thru and this was one attempt at that. Um, yeah. I won't be attempting this again. I will typically eat anything and when hungry will muscle on through even those meals most won't. So this was truly a disappointment for me.

Let's begin with the salmon spread. It was mushy, tasted fishy, and weird. This is when I was looking for an immediate tongue amputation. Now don't get me wrong I love fish. We eat it at least once a week either raw or cooked. This stuff however was awful! I couldn't get it out of my mouth fast enough and I only had the once cracker topped salmon deal. The crackers on the other hand were pretty good.

Next up the Edamame. I've had dry edamame before and I'll be honest I prefer the fresh version. I found what was included in the lunch to be too dry for my liking. Luckily I didn't feel like a tongue-ectomy was in order but I didn't finish the package either. On a positive side I did drink more water.

More for the positive, the dark chocolate piece and trail mix were a happy eat for me. I wanted to break up the chocolate and add it to the trail mix but for this review I decided to eat everything as it's individual intention. They didn't quite make up for the need to remove my tongue but they did their best so I will give honorable mention here.

So, yeah, this is a bad review. I definitely will not be eating one of these GoPicnics again. But if they do sell the trail mix or chocolate I would consider.

I received this product through the Amazon Vine program and had occasion to try it on my recent trip to San Diego from Seattle (1300 mile drive). I thought that this would be a great time to try it as there are long stretchs of I-5 that do not have places to eat. Crossing from Oregon into California, I stopped at a very scenic reststop and decided to try the Gopicnic meal that I had brought with me.

Here are the plus items:

Nothing needed refrigeration
The box is well designed so that you can close it back up easily
Every item is individually wrapped so that you can eat only a portion of it if you want without risking spoiling the remaining items.
There is no chemistry list in the food listings
There is trivia written in the box to help keep you amused as you eat.
The chocolate piece is dark chocolate and is very good.

Here is what I found a bit lacking:

The six Ritz like crackers are not very filling
The salmon spread was fishy tasting, smelling, and also had a very runny texture. The lime flavoring that it was supposed to have did not come through the fishy taste.
The salted edame were very bland and are apparently an acquired taste. I have had them before with spicy flavorings and there were fine. Just salt though does not do much for me.
The trail mix was supposed to be ginger flavored, but I could not really taste it.

Perhaps the other varieties of this product might be better, but I would not recommend this one.
