Food items are of ok quality, nothing special.  The salmon mixture has a strange texture, somewhat gel-like.  Not bad, but not cheap enough to buy again for the quality of the product, in my opinion.

Although I thought it was a somewhat odd combination of food, I actually enjoyed every part of the meal.  There were parts (like the edamame) that I thought I would not like but everything was tasty.  The fruit and nut mix was a little bit sweeter than I expected, which probably contributed to the rather high 21g sugar content.  The fat content (16g,5g saturated) is also rather high.  I found the chocolate a little bit bland but it was ok.  I thought the salmon spread was quite good.  I could taste the lime and the slightest hint of spiciness but it was fairly mild.  It didn't look like a whole lot of food but it was reasonably filling.  I like the convenience of a "meal in a box" that doesn't require refrigeration or heating.  It's a good option for a hike or anywhere that you just need to eat on-the-go.

Summary: Healthy, handy and tasty. Lunch for those on the go.
Text:
At 410 calories with no trans fat and 22 grams of protein you can feel better eating this than anything you'll eat from a drive-thru.

Chili Lime Salmon Spread: It smells a little fishy at first but the flavor is nicely balanced with lime juice and spices (onion, cumin, ginger, turmeric) against the red pepper paste. If the spices concern you, sweeten it up with some pieces of Romaine lettuce.

Organic Crackers: Dry and not as buttery as Ritz crackers (but much healthier), these crackers don't interfere with the spread.

Fruit & Nut Mix: The cranberries provide a pleasant tang between the peanuts and banana chips. Eat this mix along with the dark chocolate square for a sweet and savory experience.

Dry Roasted Edamame: The soybeans were roasted so much that they reminded me of Setsubun (the Japanese bean-throwing festival). That's not to say the edamame are too dry because they bring plenty of flavor to the lunch, however this treat can be overlooked next to the chocolate and fruit mix. I'd recommend saving the one ounce packet for an afternoon snack so you can appreciate the dark roasted flavor on its own.

Organic Dark Chocolate Square: Dark chocolate fans will rejoice, milk chocolate fans will find this too bitter by itself. If you fall into the latter category, try eating the square with the fruit and nut mix (my preference).

In summary, this is a handy and tasty lunch. You can store it in your desk drawer instead of the company refrigerator, which guarantees it will be waiting for you when lunchtime rolls around. GoPicnic even added a Sudoku puzzle in the bottom of the box!

Rating: Five stars.

I wasn't expecting a whole lot out of a "ready to eat" meal, but this GoPicnic combination was a pleasant surprise. There was enough stuff to actually fill me up for a quick lunch (though I have to admit, I added some carrot sticks and a nonfat 6 oz. yogurt) -- and I'm a 200+ pound male.

The salmon dip and Ritz-like crackers are the main course. The chili lime flavoring is mild at first, but builds on you. The edamame are crispy and salty and aren't objectionable at all, while the fruit and nut mix and (dark!) chocolate square round out the mix. Very pleasant.

For around $4 per meal, these aren't cheap, but aren't outrageous for quality, all-natural foods without trans fats or high fructose corn syrup. While the package itself is only 4.4 oz. (compared, to say, a Lean Cuisine at around 9 oz.) it still may be worth it for you especially if you don't want to have to worry about refrigeration or microwaving. I wouldn't hesitate to buy one again so I'm not stuck going out to eat at work and consuming more calories than I really need. But it's definitely not an every week thing, and don't expect anything real filling.

Summary: For those with "higher standard" tastes will find this satisfying.
Text: GoPicnic Ready-to-eat Meals (Salmon & Crackers) is a on-the-go meal for those with slightly deeper pockets and with a more "refined" taste than your average Joe lunch pail.  The Salmon & Crackers were okay, the Dark Chocolate treat with really delicious, the Edamames were okay and the Ginger Zip fruit & nut mix wasn't that bad.  This ready-to-eat meal is all organic and perfect for those who are health conscience.  But, if you're looking for a more traditional meal then keep on looking.  Only for those with "exquisite" tastes.

The essential attribute of GoPicnic's products is that they're self-contained meals. No refrigeration needed, no heating needed, all utensils included, and enough variety that it feels like you're having a little meal, rather than, say, just a bag of peanuts. They're also generally pretty healthy, though that will vary depending on the variety.

This salmon+crackers box is on the healthier side. 410 calories, 22g protein, 11g fiber, 16g fat, and 48g carbohydrates.

So how does it taste? It's not bad. The edamame are just roasted, salted soybeans, which are never very exciting, but they provide a lot of the nutritive value of this meal. The crackers are flaky, buttery, and quite nice. The salmon spread is a little surprising. It's whole-salmon, not salmon filet, so it doesn't look as tidy as something like canned tuna. Think of old-fashioned canned salmon, and you're closer. It's in a lightly spicy, glaze-like chili sauce. It smells pretty strongly of fish -- you might annoy people depending on where you're eating. Or attract cats. ;) I liked it, but I would not expect children to regard it with anything but suspicion. The fruit and nut mix was sweet and crunchy and very yummy. Good thing it's a small package. The dark chocolate was kind of meh, but hey, chocolate! Something minty or citrusy would have been better. I think.

The GoPicnic meals are a good choice (if you don't mind the high price) for car trips or long walks or other kinds of travel when you won't have access to refrigeration and microwave ovens. I enjoyed these.

This is a picnic lunch with 4 courses, including dessert, and even a sudoku puzzle to play while you digest. It seems like everything is very small and wouldn't be filling, but it truly filled me up! I was still hungry right after eating it, but just a few minutes later, I felt satisfied. (It's possible I eat too fast.) I stayed satisfied for several hours after, too.

As for taste - I really liked it. The salmon and crackers were good. The salmon was seasoned well, and the cracker flavor complimented it. I was worried that the ginger part of the "ginger zip fruit & nut mix" would be too strong, but it was subtle. I haven't actually tried the edamame yet. I did (of course) eat the dark chocolate square and loved it. It was small, but very good. I prefer dark chocolate to milk chocolate, and this was good.

As far as nutrition goes, it's not bad. At 410, the calories are in the OK range for lunch. Sodium is 660mg (28%), which isn't horrible, especially since there's 22g of protein and 11g of fiber, which keeps you full enough to not get another snack full of salt.

At the time of this writing, this is $30 for a package of 6. That makes these $5 each. That's a little pricey for something you take to work for lunch every day. But as far as a treat once in a while, it's a pretty good value.

I did really like this. It's tasty and filling, and won't bust your diet as long as you don't add too many snacks. I'd like the sodium to be a little less, but it's not really bad for what you get. I might have to get this again.

Summary: Not as good as some of their other options
Text:
I've tried GoPicnic brand snacks before, and found them fairly decent for a healthier option. This one was not as good as others we've had. My 4 year old son and I sat down to try this, and we both LOVE salmon. We eat it canned, baked, in dips, smoked, etc. Living in Alaska, we eat a lot of salmon. We both took a couple of bites of this dip, and didn't finish. It's okay in a pinch, but a little too hot (spicy) with an odd flavor that covers up the salmon. It's also a very strange almost gel-like consistency that we didn't like, most likely from the corn starch.

The crackers were good, although they are white flour instead of whole grain, and we very rarely eat white flour, even though they were organic.

We don't eat a lot of soy due to the health issues, especially GMO soy which this probably is, but we did taste the edamame for this review. They were dry without much flavor.

The Ginger Zip fruit and nut mix was a little odd. It tasted okay, but was an odd combination of dried banana chips, ginger peanuts, and dried cranberries. Not our favorite fruit & nut combo.

The chocolate was decent, although not as good as Endangered Species dark chocolate. It was organic, which is a plus.

The container & packaging was nice and included a fork and napkin, so you can take it with you on the run. There's even a Sudoku puzzle on the inside of the box for some post-picnic fun :-)

Bottom Line: I'd rather eat this than fast food or Snackables, but this wasn't my favorite flavor combination. Also if you are looking for organic snacks, the only organic items in this box are the crackers and the chocolate. Also, if you are allergic to corn, there's corn starch & maltodextrin in the salmon spread. Obviously this also contains soy, fish, wheat, and peanuts for allergy information.

Summary: An expensive snack for 4.48oz of food.
Text:
The box says this is a meal and @ $5.00 and 400 calories it should be a meal, it's not. Inside the box there are packages of crackers, a nut fruit mix, chili lime salmon, edamame and a square of chocolate. When I opened the box I was a little disappointed at the serving size of the chili lime salmon compared to the size of the edamame. For the price I would expect more salmon and less edamame to make up the 22gms of protein, my mistake. The salmon looks like baby food but it is tasty. There is a fork and not a knife in the box which makes it hard to get all of the salmon from the little container. The edamame is over dried with not much taste. It gets kind of powdery when you chew it and it made me cough from the texture getting caught in the back of my throat. You'll need a lot of water to wash them down with. I had to give up eating them because they kept choking me. I did enjoy the fruit and nut mix and the chocolate was really good so it wasn't a total loss.
I consider the the price to be the biggest negative in this review. At almost $5.00 a box this is an expensive snack. I won't be buying this.

Summary: Now you can have an airline meal at home
Text:
The GoPicnic ready-to-eat meal is pretty much the same thing you get in coach when the airline gives you a snack or meal. it contains some crackers, a chili lime salmon spread, some dry-roasted Edamame (a crunchy salty snack), some nuts, and a dark chocolate square. The salmon spread is very um...salmony. Not that good as far as my taste goes. The other stuff is typical dry snack food. Not bad. Not good.

I am surprised that this product is indistinguishable from one of my least favorite things: airline food. Flying coach is bad enough, but those boxed snacks, well if you have eaten them you know. According to the label, the product uses mostly organic, high quality ingredients. The nut mix does contain peanuts. If you have an allergy to them, stay away.

Summary: Great balanced meal for those on the go
Text:
I thought I was gettign a pack of 6 to review and share with family. I only received one box. The flavors are great and the portion is sized correctly to make most dieticians happy.

The negative side is the sodium content - too high.

Anyway, it's protein packed with good fats.

The food tastes good, I especially like the those dried edameme beans, everything seems to be USDA certified organic food, healthy and nutritious. I asked my 8-year-old one to take one to school for lunch once because she doesn't really enjoy eating whatever is on her school's lunch menu. She liked the crackers and the salmon paste, but not everything else, it was obvious too little food for her, she ended up coming home eating double the amount of snacks she usually eats. Also, $4 per pack is a little price too me.

A good and healthy snack. Very good porions and fresh taste. The Salmon is a little spicy for my taste; however, not overwhellming. Great snack pack for when you are on the go or need a qucik snack in between meals.

My honest opinion of this snack box is that the items in the pack were not good picks to fulfill a meal. I understand the intention of GoPicnic putting the pack together to offer a variety of interesting and nutritious snacks; however, as a meal, I do not rate this snack pack as great. Individual items in the box were great, such as two pieces of dark chocolate, crackers, and nut and dry fruit mix (which is a bit too sweet for my overall taste although the ginger made up for it), but altogether, each item is a snack, and essentially you are eating a meal consisting of snacks, which I do not feel is an ideal meal (maybe as a last resort meal, but not as a take-to-work meal). The least likeable item was the salmon spread. Perhaps others rated this spread as favorable, but in my opinion, the spread is a tad salty, and it did not leave a complimentary taste in my mouth. Overall, the pack is convenient, but I recommend a consumer eat each snack individually and not as a meal. Of course, if you generally eat snacks as a meal, then this pack is for you.
On a positive note, the snack pack is cute, includes a plenty of tasty healthful snacks, and is not too pricy, but I would not pay $4 for the pack. I might go for a wholesale buy if offered, but not as a single-time purchase. Therefore, the pack isn't too bad, but I wouldn't recommend it as a meal to anyone; I'd simply recommend it for what it is: a combination of decent snacks.

Summary: Pretty good, but could be improved...
Text:
The salmon was a little spicy, which was okay. It tasted pretty good. The chocolate was good as well.

It's wonderful that they're using organic, and so if you're looking for a packaged snack that's organic and has a variety of good nutrients, this could be a great little snack/picnic to take with you.

I like that the ingredients are listed on the product page so you can see what's in it before buying.

The drawback for me was the trailmix and dry roasted edamame, just didn't taste all that great.

I like that the salmon used is Alaskan salmon which is supposed to be fresher, cleaner, and better for you.

So, other than the drawbacks mentioned, it was an okay snack.

GoPicnic is a wonderful option for my college aged daughter.  She never really stops to eat, and when she does finally give into hunger it's usually not good food.  She loves the convenience of the packaging and the freshness of  GoPicnic.  I appreciate the nutrition in each package.  The new Salmon and Crackers is one of her favorites.

Summary: Somewhat Nutritious Snack, But Doesn't Taste Great.
Text:
I can't say I truly enjoyed these "meals". First, this is not really a meal, it's a snack at best. Sure, if you were trapped in the wilderness you may enjoy this, but for most regular people, this isn't the size of a meal.

The Good

The food is nutritious as far as fiber and protein.
The crackers were good.
The dried fruit wasn't too bad.

The Bad
The salmon doesn't taste good in my opinion.
The size is too small for a meal.
The package expires within months...I expected the shelf life to be longer I guess.

Bottom Line: I would pass on these, or at least buy one package and try it out first before buying this multiple pack.

That's right bleech, like you wanted to get it out of your mouth as fast as possible:

I do not like green eggs and spam
I do not like it sam-i-am
I'd rather eat my athletic sox
Than eat this Picnic-in-a box

Now:

Salmon, not bad if your starving on a desert island 1 star

Edamame, bad no matter where you eat it especially if your not near a water source 0 star

Crackers, good but how can you ruin crackers 4 star

Chocolate, actually pretty good (but you have to like hard, i mean hard chocolate) 4 star

Fruit&Nut Mix was the best of the bunch, truly enjoyable 5 star

So:

Why two overall, I'm being nice. Since the main part of the meal was the salmon and the edamame how else would you rate it.

Anyone want four free boxes?

Zeb Kantrowitz

I tried the Salmon and crackers meal and I'm not impressed. I normally love fish and am a sushi lover, but the entire time I was eating the salmon I felt like I was eating cat food. It smelled. Really bad. The texture of it was also reminiscent of cat food which made it go down all the worse. The salmon had a hint of spice which I generally like but the whole salmon + crackers bit did not work for me.

I did however enjoy the nuts. Those were yummy and gone in a flash. Without a doubt, that was the best part of the meal.

The roasted Edamame? I thought I would like them since I love boiled and salted Edamame, however these made me gag. They were so dry and the taste was bland. The chocolate, while good, also left a horrible after taste in my mouth.

Sigh.

It was not a good lunch. And it's a whopping 410 calories. That's more than the typical Lean Cuisine meals; even more than many of the Marie Callander meals! And it just wasn't satisfying. Even though I ate lots of calories I still didn't feel like I had a proper lunch, just a snack.

I won't be getting this again anytime soon.

As some others have noted, the GoPicnic salmon is like overpriced catfood. Heck, I've seen Fancy Feast cat food appetizers provide a higher quality of flaky salmon than you'll find in this GoPicnic snackbox.

First, the good. The edamame dried soybeans provide 30% of your daily protein intake, which was quite surprising to me. They were slightly on the bland side however, but I felt very nutritious when consuming then. The chocolate square and trail mix were ok (not great, but passable), and tasted fine. Also, the Sudoku game on the bottom of the packaging was a thoughtful touch, although I don't play Sudoku. Also, the crackers were pretty tasty; reminded me of a healthier version of Ritz crackers.

Now, the bad. The salmon, which is supposed to be the centerpiece of the meal, was nasty. Didn't taste like salmon at all, since it was overpowered by other spices, but it did have a slightly fishy odor. Had an odd consistency, probably better suited to coming out of a bottle of toothpaste.

I guess the GoPicnic isn't a terrible choice if you were starving and it were given to you for free. But even if I were starving, I probably wouldn't eat the salmon.

Summary: 1!/2, That's what I really wanted to give it
Text: This Meal is terrible. The meat products, the crackers, the nuts, all of them were nasty. The least nasty was the mixed nuts. They had a weird, palatable flavor. The rest was not at all digestible.

Okay, I like where they are going with this idea - prepackaging a healthy snack of unusual dishes for people with little time. Here is where it went wrong.

1) I read the box, and it tells me how healthy the meal is, including lots of fiber
2) I open the box
3) I notice that there are no utensils, and that the chocolate is missing.
4) I find a knife for spreading and open the salmon
5) I gag from the overwhelming odor of the fish and dispose of the salmon after a quick taste (not to my liking)
6) I discover peanuts in the granola mix - I like peanuts but didn't remember seeing any warnings on the box about peanuts
7) I liked the edemame but the bag was too small
8) I realized how much garbage was created from a little midget snack and feel bad for my planet. For real everything was individually wrapped in plastic and the portions were so small that odds are people will STILL go find more to eat.

In the end, my box was missing things, there didn't seem to be any way to spread the salmon included, I wouldn't advise eating this at your desk because of the pungent odor and there are better packaging choices for the environment.

Now if I could find a big bag of that edemame I would buy THAT, but there was too much trash for too little reward in this "snack" for me.

Summary: I didn't care too much for it :(
Text: For the price of it I would not buy it...you don't get very much and I did not like the taste of the salmon...I live where I get salmon quite a bit and this didn't taste like any kind of salmon I have ever tasted :(

The first thing I want to mention is that this package - consisting of a chili-lime-salmon spread, organic crackers (think Ritz-type crackers), dry-roasted and salted edamame, an organic dark chocolate square, and a fruit-nut mix - comes with a plastic fork, but no knife. Struck me as kind of weird - spreading the salmon mixture with a fork? One doesn't really need either utensil for the rest of it, unless one puts it all together in a bowl or something. One could also carp with GoPicnic's use of the word "meal" in the name - this is definitely a snack, not a meal, though it's a decent-sized snack.

Secondly, the fruit-nut mixture contains peanuts, as well as dried bananas and cranberries, with ginger flavoring. I am allergic to peanuts, so I didn't try this part of the product. While the fine print on the bottom of the box and the side (under the nutrition info) mentions this clearly, it's not stated on the front or back of the box. Just a minor caveat - it does say "nuts" and anyone with nut allergies of any kind will know to read the fine print.

That said, the rest of the product is quite nice. The salmon spread is quite salmon-y, and one can detect some hints of both the chili and lime, though I wouldn't say it's strongly spicy by any means. It's got a nice texture, not grainy but not too mushy either, and tastes fresh enough, and the crackers are light, buttery and crisp. The edamame are fine, also fresh and crunchy, and it's nice that they use sea salt instead of table salt. The chocolate is strong - maybe not intense enough for hardcore chocolate nuts, but it was fine for this chocolate liker (not lover).

The nutritional info on the package as a whole claims that it provides 44% of daily fiber, and 28% sodium, with 410 calories - so it's a good energy source without having a huge amount of salt, despite all the nuts and fish and crackers. The package is supposed to be shelf-safe for several months; I just got it so I can't vouch for that but I'll probably save one of the six boxes for a few months and update then, if there's any deterioration in quality before the expiration date.

This isn't typically the sort of product I buy; had I not gotten it through Vine I don't know that I would have ever tasted it. But it's a nice snack overall, and apart from not being able to eat the fruit/nut mixture I have no significant issues. I would definitely consider other products in this line, particularly if I can eat all the elements in the box!

Summary: Perfect For A Gourmet Fishing Trip
Text:
It is always a challenge to find reasonably healthy "fast food" - and this fits the bill. Several reviewers have compared it to "airplane food". I find it a little tastier then the typical airline offerings - but it would be a great option to take along and avoid the risk of what they might feed you (at a considerably better price).

For me - it provided the perfect gourmet fishing lunch. Paired with a nice Pinot Noir I felt like I was fly fishing in France. It is reasonably tasty and very convenient.

The GoPicnic Ready-to-Eat Meals, Salmon + Crackers, box contains an interesting collection of individual snacks. Almost all of them were good by themselves. with the exception perhaps of the edamame (soy beans) which I thought was too dry and without taste. The main course, the salmon spread was good, although it should have come with a better spreader than a fork. As soon as I opened the salmon, the cat became very interested. I gave her a bite. She liked it too.

The collection reminded me of the snack meals provided by airlines just before they stopped providing meals at all. To their credit, GoPicnic has worked to avoid including artificial colors and flavors. I think that this would be a good choice to bring with you on a flight. However, in the end, you are left with a very large pile of wrappers. This is probably not a good lesson in the use of resources.

Taken as a whole, the box was an interesting idea, and would work well if the fork is replaced with a better spreader.

Summary: Good for a quick bite or to keep at the office....
Text:
I usually try to keep a "ready to go" meal at work in case I forget my lunch and thought this item looked interesting. I was pretty happy with it....here are the pros/cons:

I like that it packs 11 grams of fiber (44% of your daily intake), 22 grams of protein, 10% iron and 10% vitamin c. The salmon spread is pretty tasty with a little bit of spice to it, but not too much, crackers, a generous serving of dry roasted edamame, Fruit & Nut mix and an organic dark chocolate square. I really liked the fruit/nut mix and the ginger was not overpowering. It was a tasty mix of dried fruit, bananas and ginger peanuts....very tasty.

The couple things we would like to change: you need more crackers-I think about 8 would be just about right, as you seem to have salmon spread left over unless you heap it on. Also, a knife would be helpful to spread it, along with the fork that is included OR ditch the round crackers and use square crackers that would be easier to just dip into the spread.

Overall, not a gigantic amount of food, it seemed to have proper food proportions and is perfect for one person who eats sensibly. As it has a lot of fiber I would keep in mind that drinking enough fluids would be important with a to-go meal like this one.
As far as the food, it was a nice little meal that I would keep for the office or in a backpack when I hike.

I would consider buying a couple of these to have on hand and would recommend them for those that need a quick meal.

Summary: Good for a Layover in an Airport
Text: I wish I'd had this the last time I was stuck walking around an airport looking for something nutritious and tasty to eat.  Seriously, this is a good alternative to Cinnabons' or Applebee's To Go.  The elements in the package were tasty on their own, and, together, made up a healthy little meal with a long shelf-life.  The salmon was a touch runny, but nicely flavored with lime and chili, not a whole lot of sodium.  Crackers were whole and tasty.  Edamame were dry-roasted and lightly salted:  the first time I ever actually enjoyed edamame.  The ginger-touched dried fruit and nut mix was WONDERFUL, and I will look for it separately in the future.  The little bite of chocolate was a touch too cacao-y and not very silky chocolate-y, but it was a nice sweet ending, none-the-less.  The packaging is nice, like a teeny-tiny picnic basket, and it had a little "keep you occupied" pencil puzzle printed on the inside.  I will look for these again.  Thanks for a great alternative to the nutritional bombs available in an airport.

I like the concept of the GoPicnic ready-to-eat meals. They're a more healthy alternative compared to some ready-to-eat meals I see in the grocery store; another plus is they don't need refrigeration. I've purchased their SunnyBreak & ExploreMunch: Turkey Stick & Cheese 6-Pack for long car trips. We never eat them as a whole meal but pass around the box & pick what we want to snack on.

GoPicnic meals are put together with a lot of thought, quality ingredients & quality products. The salmon & crackers balanced meal contains 410 calories and 11 gr. of fiber, 22gr of protein; sodium content is 660mg or 28% of your daily requirement.

Flavor & other info:
Chili Lime Salmon Spread: The taste of the salmon is not overpowered by the mild, spicy chili/lime spread. So, if you don't like the taste of fish, you won't want to purchase this. Getting back to the spicy flavor: it's not very spicy at all, which I prefer. If your taste buds prefer the 'crazy hot' spicy food that's so popular today, this will probably seem bland to you. Some of the ingredients in this spread: pink Alaskan salmon, red pepper paste, sugar, lime juice, vinegar, garlic powder & spices.

Dry Roasted Edamame: These lightly salted, dry roasted green soybeans are crunchy with good flavor. Containing 130 calories, 8gr fiber, 14gr protein & 150mg/6% sodium it's a healthy addition to this meal.

Late July Organic Classic Rich Crackers: These are very good, with a light, buttery taste. At 90 calories, 210mg/9% sodium they're on par with the average cracker...but these are organic and prepared with healthier ingredients & taste better than many other crackers.

Ginger Zip: Contains ginger peanuts, cranberries & banana chips; similar to a trail mix, it's good, fresh & crispy.

Terra Nostra Organic Robust Dark 60% Cacao: This dark chocolate doesn't taste as bitter to me as others. I'm not a fan of dark chocolate, but it's good for you...and this tastes better than some & it's organic.

All in all, this is a great meal to take with you on a long car trip, an outdoor outing or even something quick to pack for your lunch. It also has a fork and a Sudoku puzzle...so don't forget to bring a drink with you and a pencil with an eraser for the puzzle.

I am so tired of companies claiming their products are GF when they are not. Most of the items in this product are cross-contaminated, I have celiac ,this is not a diet fad for me.Believe me I miss all my gluten foods. The government needs to step up and regulate the products better. GLUTEN-FREE, should mean just that. NO *&%^ing Gluten !!!!!!!!
expensive and doesn't taste good at all.  i wish i could return them but amazon will not allow you to return food items.

Summary: You call that salmon?  Really?  Rancid dried fruit killed it as well!
Text: I read a really bad review of this but I'm trying all the GoPicnic meals so I tried it anyway.  There were more bad items than good in this, unfortunately.  The salmon was like a weird tasting, overly-fishy, lumpy soup. Gross! (And I love salmon in many shapes and forms!) I couldn't finish it and gave the majority to my dog.  Since that's the main value of the meal (protein) I found this GoPicnic meal to be of no value to me!  Anyway..The crackers were excellent (same ones as in a few other meals), the edamame was okay but bland (google the dangers of eating soybean for women...made me wary of eating this) and the dry fruit mix was rancid!  I double-checked the expiration date to make sure I didn't get a bad lot but it doesn't expire for several months.  I'm writing Amazon for a refund after my review.  It's too bad...I enjoyed the majority of the meals.

So after reading all the reviews I had really high hopes for this meal. To my shock and true disappointment this meal was terrible. The salmon tasted like vomit and the crackers were flavorless. The Edamame were very dry and tasted like raw black eyed peas. The only decent thing in the meal was the fruit and nut mix which I mixed with Edamame to make those edible. I'm in Afghan and was looking for a healthy quick lunch. What I got was an overpriced disappointment. The chocolate wasn't even very good.

Those who think I'm kidding obviously haven't flown Coach in a while, and while you can usually purchase a somewhat similar snack/meal from your airline during the flight, it will almost certainly cost a lot more.

Theoretically even cheaper would be assembling this snack/meal yourself because GoPicnic is for the most part simply repackaging food products manufactured by others, but of course in that case you will have to do all of the work!

The first item I tried was Seapoint Farms Dry Roasted Edamame, Lightly Salted, 1 oz., which I found palatable but extremely dry.

One of the two exclusively GoPicnic distributed items in the meal box was the Chili Lime Salmon Spread, 1.6 oz., which I found quite delicious. I ate it with the enclosed Late July Organic Classic Rich Crackers, 0.7 oz., but in fairness I think it would have tasted just as good on Ritz Crackers. (I'm unsure why a Dispoz-o Senate White Medium Weight Polypropylene Fork was included rather than the Dispoz-o Senate White Medium Weight Polypropylene Knife that would have been more useful.)

The other exclusively GoPicnic distributed item, the Ginger Zip all natural fruit & nut mix 0.75 oz bag, wasn't bad.

Finally, the Terra Nostra Organics Robust 60% Chocolate Mini Square, 0.43 oz. made a tasty little dessert.

Note: The meal box also has a Sudoku puzzle in the bottom.

Now it is up to you. You can buy this one, assemble your own, or try one of the other GoPicnic Care Packages or Ready-To-Eat Meals.

My relationship to food is very much a balance between cost and taste -- I'm willing to pay for pricey food that's amazing, but I have a very keen internal sense of what's "worth" it and what isn't. This box of snacks ain't worth it. First of all it's only a meal for folks who tend to eat smallish meals. Yes, it has 410 calories, but I would guess most of that is the chocolate and trail mix. There's not enough bulk here to constitute what I would call a meal, and unfortunately, the "main dish" is awful. The box contains:

A 1-oz. package of roasted and lightly salted edamame, which I actually liked, but I suspect most people will hate. It's got a very subtle flavor that most people I know hate.

A .75-oz. package of fruit/nut/ginger trail mix. I like trail mix, this struck me as a bit sweet and the two handfulls don't last long.

A 1.6-oz. packet of "chili lime salmon spread" to have with 6 small circular crackers. The crackers are totally fine (hard to screw up a cracker), but the salmon spread is awful. I love salmon, I love chili lime concotions, I love seafood spreads. This was nauseatingly bad, way too fishy and the red pepper base totally overwhelms the chili lime flavor. This part of the package needs a completely new recipe. (And why is this packaged with a plastic fork? It's a spread, it needs a knife!)

A .4-oz. square of dark chocolate. This was quite good and just the right size.

So, a pretty mediocre bundle of organic snacks at an outrageous price makes this a terrible value.

Summary: Go Picnic Snack Pack with Chili Lime Salmon Spread Main Course
Text:
GoPicnic's Ready to Eat Meals with Salmon and Crackers was an interesting array of mostly healthy foodstuffs. The whole shebang comes in a cardboard box that opens like a laptop and can presumably be closed again (I ate everything and so didn't close it). There's even a sudoku puzzle on the inside(of mine at least). Also inside are individually wrapped containers of Late July brand rich crackers, Seapoint Farms Dry Roasted Edamame with salt, Gopicnic's Chili Lime Salmon spread, Gopicnic's Ginger Zip fruit and nut mix, and a Terra Nostra's organic robust dark chocolate square. These items are all shelf stable for several months as long as kept in a cool dry place (meaning that you probably shouldn't store these in your car in the summertime for more than a few hours).

I have a love hate relationship with salmon. Either I love it (usually in the form of spreads and cakes) or I hate it (grilled, broiled, pan fried filets) so I expected to love this version. Surprisingly, I'm kind of on the fence about this very orange appearing spread. It has a nice salmon flavor (and large flakes of fish in the mix) that is just slightly fishy and you can taste the lime, but to me the chili was really lacking. I think with more of a chili note in the spread I would have enjoyed it much more. 3 Stars for this product.

Salmon Spread Ingredients:Alaskan pink salmon, water, red pepper paste, sugar, lime juice, modified cornstarch, salt, vinegar, garlic powder, chili powder, spices (no MSG), natural lime flavor, maltodextrin, and natural color. The salmon comes from a MSC certified fishery.

The Late July Crackers (which I have had before) are always delicious and remind me much of a flaky butter type cracker. The salmon spread went well on them and they weren't brittle enough to break when the spread was applied. The utensil given for this purpose was a fork. 6 Crackers come in a pack and I found that I had a little more salmon than cracker (although I didn't go crazy with the application. 5 Stars for this product.

Cracker Ingredients: Organic Wheat flour, organic evaporated cane juice, organic oleic safflower oil and/or organic oleic sunflower oil, organic palm oil, sea salt, leavening, soy lecithin, enzymes.

I didn't really like the Dry Roasted Edamame. The only taste at all that I got from them was the bare hint of salt added. I think with all the other flavor packed items in this picnic a seasoned variety could have better competed with everything. Otherwise it was somewhat bland and I had no desire to finish the small packet. 1 Star for this product

Edamame Ingredients:Soybeans, Sea Salt

I think my favorite item in this packet would be the Ginger Zip fruit mix. It was tasty, but not too sweet, with just the lightest touch of ginger that I thought was perfect and didn't overpower the natural flavors of the dried fruit and peanut mixture. Sadly, it was only a .75 oz packet and I ran out before I wanted to. I would gladly have traded the edamame for a bigger packet of this snack. 5 Stars for this product

Mix Ingredients:Ginger peanuts, (sugar, ground ginger, sea salt), cranberries, banana chips.

Last but not least is the dark chocolate square. I'm a big fan of dark chocolate and since this was 60% cacao it suited me just fine. It had just a hint of sweetness with that wonderful bitterness you can only get from darker chocolates. 4 Stars for this product.

Chocolate Ingredients:Organic dark chocolate, dry cocoa solids.

Allergies: On all items the packaging warns for Soy, Milk, Wheat, Peanuts, Fish, and Treenuts.

Overall I'd have to say that this was a pretty good snack that I could see myself taking to work or on a car trip with me. I'd prefer that a couple of the ingredients would change but it still filled me up despite my avoidance of some items, but didn't over fill me to the point where I felt sleepy after lunch.

Review by M. Reynard 2011

Summary: Tasty Gluten-Free Meal on the Go!
Text:
I have been searching for healthy, quick, pre-packaged gluten-free meals... I was so excited to find these! I tried the salmon meal today and really liked it all - it was SO EASY, and much less expensive than most gluten-free foods!

Since the packaging doesn't scream "gluten free" (and is more attractive than most store-bought packaged lunches), I plan to purchase some of the more kid-friendly flavors for the gluten-free elementary girl I sponsor. She will actually be able to eat a "fancy" packed lunch with her friends!

Now I'm off to order some other flavors...

I must say that this is quite good. I try to keep shelf stable food handy to grab if I want to have a picnic or to take to something like fireworks, or even a quick lunch. Normally that means something pretty boring and probably non-meat. In the past I have tried everything, including MRE peanut butter packets. Let me tell you, this surely beats MREs by a wide margin for taste.

When i say mini-feast, I perhaps should say micro I do have to admit that the portions aren't exactly large, but since I am on a diet this is a great option that brings some welcome variety to the table.

Summary: Satisfactory as a light meal or heavy snack
Text:
Sometimes I just want to be able to grab something to eat that doesn't require refrigeration or cooking and go. Unfortunately most things that fit these requirements are full of unpronounceable ingredients. This pack by GoPicnic is better than most options as the ingredients are recognizable. The calories are reasonable as well.

As for taste, I liked everything but the dry roasted edamame, which was bland. The crackers, chocolate, and trail mix were all delicious and the salmon complemented the crackers nicely.

Although I wouldn't eat these regularly for lunch, they would be great as meals while traveling.

It's a really good idea, I swear... Just not really for me. I didn't enjoy the taste of the salmon, nor did my mother or my brother. (in fact he kept asking me why I'm eating it and doing that to myself, ha). Some people seem to put great reviews and love this, its just ot for me. The edamame tasted kind of stale to me, but I'm sure thats the way dry edamame tastes. The Ginger fruit pack, My brother said tasted like perfume, I think it tasted fine, except the Ginger did resemble the taste of perfume. The crackers were good, As was the chocolate.
Over all, I wouldn't get this again, it's just ot for me. I would prefer to be healthy in different ways.

This was a fun little snack/working lunch. I loved that it had a variety of items - snack sized portions of five different things. For some reason I think that's more satisfying than just having a lot of one or two things. And the best part... there's a sudoku puzzle inside the box! Altogether a well-thought out package of goodies.

Every packet was easy to open and neatly arranged.
The salmon spread was less chunky than I expected but it was tasty and was a tiny bit spicy. Comes with a fork so it's spreadable. The crackers were good..I loved the snack mix which had bananas, cranberries and ginger-coated peanuts. Not too sweet and tasty..
I am sure I have had soy nuts before although not my usual fare...I couldn't eat these as there was no salt that I could taste on them..they were awful in my opinion, and maybe salt wouldn't have helped them. The dark chocolate was great and not bitter.

This would've been a good snack box for my teenage daughter without the soy nuts. She eats like a bird..and there is not much in this tiny box, but I feel the ingredients were good quality. Just depends on how much it takes to fill you up.

I ate this for dinner and am very surprised that I actually liked it. You get 22 grams of protein, 11 grams of fiber and 410 calories of energy in a box that converts into a very thin lunch box complete with a Sudoku puzzle.

The box contains:
- chili lime salmon spread the consistency of cat or baby food (my least liked food item) but still eatable
- organic crackers similar to Ritz crackers but not as buttery
- a nicely flavored Ginger Zip dried fruit and nut mix
- a package of dry roasted edamame that was very, very, dry but which I actually liked (you'll need a lot of water to wash this down)
- a tasty morsel of organic 60% dark chocolate - the chocolate was covered in a white haze (which means it was "blooming" but was still edible)
- a plastic fork for the salmon spread
- a Sudoku puzzle in the base of the box
- a fun food fact (similar to the trivia you find on a Snapple bottle cap)

The major element I didn't like was that this meal is very high in salt (660mg or 28% of your Daily Value). Also, since the edamame is very dry, you really need to bring lots of water to wash it down.

I think this is a good meal to grab if you are backpacking for a day or if you don't want to carry perishables on you during a long drive. However, I wouldn't consider this healthy fare for an everyday lunch. Overall, I really liked the taste and was pleasantly surprised that I ate every morsel in the box--I didn't even share my salmon spread with the cats and that was my least favorite item.

I never thought I'd say this since I usually called boxed food unnatural food-like substances, but GoPicnic gets 4 stars from me!

When I saw the size of this "picnic in a box" (only 4.4 ounces), I didn't expect much. Was surprised at how good everything tasted and how filling and satisfying it was.  For a child who doesn't eat much, this might be a perfect meal on a picnic.  While I wouldn't call it an adult meal, it's a great snack.  The dry roasted edamame was crunchy and delicious, but a bit on the dry side.  Not quite as tasty as peanuts, but a lot healthier.  The Ginger Zip fruit and nut mix was really good; wish there had been more of it.  The main course is crackers with Chili Lime Salmon Spread, which was adequate, but nothing special.  A child might not like it because of the slight spiciness.  For dessert, there is a nice and very good tasting dark chocolate square.  Except for the sodium, which was a little higher than I would have liked (660mg), this seems pretty healthy (no trans fats, no high fructose corn syrup, no MSG.)  The real beauty of these little picnics is that they are not perishable, are very compact to carry and come in a convenient box that you can re-close if you don't eat everything at one time.  I would stock a few of these up as emergency provisions, as they are nutritious and tasty, probably have a long shelf life and you won't go hungry in an emergency when you have no power to cook anything.  Great idea, but a slightly larger version might be better.  They are worth trying.  Seems like a good meal for diabetics who are supposed to eat frequently for their meal or snack in between the main meals of the day.

I wasn't completely sure what to expect from this product, but thought it would be good for a trip to the beach or quick snack at the park.  I was very pleasantly surprised by what is in these 6 really tiny looking boxes.  The salmon actually tasted like fresh fish, with a creamy texture, which was put on  "ritz" like, flavorful crackers. They were pretty filling.  Also included were a bag of edamame and one of dried fruit, both a nice treat, and a piece of yummy dark chocolate.  I think that if you really wanted a full picnic  meal, you might want to add some vegetable sticks or a piece of fruit.  But it occurs to me that a great use would be on an airplane flight that does not provide a meal, as is the case more and more often, and we plan to take a few on our next trip.  There are several GoPicnic varieties and based on this item, we are going to try a few more.

Summary: Mix-match of good and not so good
Text:
According to the packaging this product contains a balanced meal with 22g of protein, 11g of fiber and 410 calories. Inside you find a chili lime salmon spread, organic crackers, a fruit/nut mix, dry roasted edamame, and an organic piece of dark chocolate. Some of it was very good, while others are not-so-good. There's not a lot of food here, I'd consider it a meal if you're a person who eats multiple small meals 4-5 times daily rather than 2-3 larger meals; it's more along the line of a snack if you're a person with a hearty appetite.

I'd definitely buy the Late July organic classic rich crackers again, they were light and buttery while maintaining their crispness; much nicer than Ritz crackers. The Sweet Perry Orchards ginger zip fruit& nut mix was surprisingly good. I'm generally not a big fan of ginger, but there was a nice contrast between the flavors and textures - would probably buy separately. The Seapoint Farms dry roasted edamame was ok. Admittedly, it was my first time trying edamame, and the general consensus between my group was that it tasted 'green' or 'like sunflower seeds, only not as good'. I probably won't go out of my way to search for this product in the future, but it's all right. The Terra Nostra organic robust dark chocolate square got rave reviews, with people eagerly looking for more. It's a good sized piece, large enough for that chocolate rush, but not so big you'll regret it later. The chili lime salmon spread was a bit of a bust. It was definitely salmon, but I didn't enjoy the addition of the chili lime flavor. It was filling as a snack, but honestly, I'd probably pick a tuna option in the future.

Overall, I'd be more inclined to purchase the items I liked separately than purchase this kit again. I think I could make my own version at home for a more cost effective price, but if you're a person who enjoys convenience and variety, this may suit you fine.

There is a LOT of food in this little box. Each item is individually sealed to maintain freshness. For lunch I had 6 round crackers with a topping of Chili Lime Salmon Spread (1.6oz of spread) which was delicious. I followed this with a serving of lightly salted dry roasted edamame, Ginger Zip fruit and nut mix, and a square of dark chocolate. By the time I was done I felt comfortably full.

The Ginger Zip mix was delightfully flavored by ginger, however there was more sugar in it than I would prefer. The mix consists of ginger peanuts, cranberries and banana chips and each of the individual items had sugar added. (Ginger peanuts contain sugar, ground ginger, sea salt; cranberries consist of cranberries & sugar, and the banana chips contain coconut oil, sugar, natural flavors). The crackers are a Ritz-type white cracker made by a company called Late July, and which are described as Organic, classic rich, flaky buttery tasting crackers. Looking at the ingredients list they do contain all organic components and do NOT contain corn syrup, which is certainly a plus. And, I would have to say their description is accurate - they were flaky, buttery and quite delicious. They would be even better if they were whole wheat though. Just sayin'....

Overall though, these get a big thumbs up. My family spends a lot of time attending various sporting events for the kids and a box of food like this is awesome to throw in to provide an on-the-go meal so that we are not stuck buying bad food at exorbitant prices at concession stands, or snacking on a lot of junk.

Summary: The price is right, the taste is great!
Text:
This is a nice flat little portable snackbox that you can tuck into a purse or briefcase, knapsack, large fanny pack, luggage, picnic basket - desk drawer, whatever. It's convenient and there for you when you are on-the-go, a mid morning break, your lunch, a survival package, a camping/hiking energy booster or meal.

First, let's get this out of the way:
Two things it needs, and didn't have-
1- a plastic knife. The fork is not necessary -- at all. The knife - even one without serrations -- would be useful for spreading the salmon on the crackers, and scraping the inside of the plastic container to get all the tasty goodness left on the inner sides of the container.
2- a hand wipe. Most of this is finger food -- or slightly oily (the salmon) and a disposable moist wipe would be great.

The box is well-made and has a tab you can close if you don't eat everything at the same meal. It has a cool Soduko puzzle inside, and is a great place to put all the leftover empty packs to take with you until you are ready to dispose of them/recycle them.

Now, onto the comestibles.
First, the Chili-Lime salmon spread is great! Not too spicy -- nice and lime-tangy, and a good mouthful for the size of the package it comes in. I'm not much of a spice-eater but I thought this was a very good combination of flavors with just the right amount of spiciness. The crackers are organic, and even by themselves taste very good. Because there was no knife in the box, I used the crackers to shovel out the salmon spread -- they held up very well -- none of them broke. They were a good accompaniment for the spread - it tasted great on the crackers or by itself.

The Ginger Zip fruit and nut mix was Awesome! Ginger peanuts, banana chips (some of the banana chips were very hard-- not a good surprise for someone in-between dental work), cranberries -- enjoyably sweet and ginger-y. And ginger is also a great digestive aid.

The dry-roasted Edemame was surprisingly good-- at first I thought I was going to encounter hard Nuts -- but no -- they were nice and crunchy; tasty, with just the right amount of salt ("lightly salted"). The Edemame itself could qualify as a snack by itself -- a mini-meal.

The chocolate reminded my of my days of Survival Chocolate Bars, because it was pretty hard, but it was delicious.

Looking at the nutritional information on the side of the box, I see that this snack is low in calories (410) somewhat high in fat and sodium content, but it's also high in Protein and Carbs, which (to me) is great because these two are energy restorers and boosters.

(PS- The front of the package needs to carry a sentence or two about the Nuts in the ingredients. Not everyone knows that Edemame are Soybeans, a possible allergen to those who have nut sensitivities. Those who are allergic to nuts need to know what they are getting.)

There was a lot of food in a small package here, which was a pleasant surprise, honestly.

Now, as a disclaimer, I should mention I've eaten more than my bodyweight in MREs, so my standards for 'edible and delicious' in long-term-storage-food might be a bit low, but I actually really dug this.

The salmon spread was zippy and spicy without being too much, and just enough for the 6 crackers. The edamame are darker looking than you see in the boxart, and do have a bit of a beany aftertaste. I wish there was a bit less of those and way more of that fruit mix--unlike regular 'dried fruit' this had a nice gingery seasoning that made it really outstanding. I could eat just that and be a happy little camper.

And the chocolate square is nummy. :D

The downsides, as others have mentioned, is that for that price, you can probably go get something fresh-cooked to eat, and there is a good bit of waste--each individual plastic wrapper and the box itself. The plus sides are that it is portable, it's tasty and it's quite handy.

Will I buy it again? I think so, honestly. Sometimes I don't have time the night before to pack up a healthy lunch from home and in that case, this would be a great way to stave off the temptation of the dreaded vending machine or the temptation to call out for pizza. Not an every-day item for me, but as an occasional treat, definitely!

As a child, Lunchables held a great bit of wonder for me. Too expensive to afford very frequently, but oh so awesome when we could. I think it had something to do with the food being arranged in a certain way and the fun of putting it all together. As an adult, I no longer feel that way about them or would even want to eat one, but some of that magic feeling came back as I opened the gopicnic box for the first time. Everything is arranged in a snazzy way in little packages, and it comes with a plastic fork (I thought I would want a knife, but the fork worked better). The box is also printed with some fun facts and includes a Sudoku puzzle, though I chose to eat on it to keep from making a mess. Can I ditch work and go play?

Okay, with that out of my system, I will talk about the food. First, it was quickly apparent that this is geared toward health-conscious people. No corn syrup, MSG, or trans-fats (the opposite of Lunchables!). The salmon spread was my greatest fear, but it was actually yummy. Not too fishy, and the lime flavor is subtle and not grossly artificial like it often is in other products. The texture is typical spread -- thick enough to not make a mess at work when applying to the included 6 crackers. Speaking of work, I don't think the smell is strong enough to offend those around you.

Dry roasted edamame is included in a generous portion. I found this tasty and you may even want to keep some to snack on over time. The flavor is pretty neutral and not too salty.

My favorite part was the Ginger Zip mix, which is ginger peanuts, cranberries, and banana chips. The texture is not too hard or chewy and the amount of ginger is just right. My only complaint is that there is not much of it!

A block, which breaks into two pieces, of organic dark chocolate is included to finish the meal. It is just the right amount to end on a high note without being overbearing, since this is lunch/snack and a brownie or something like that might leave me feeling gross.

Overall, I love these! Like Lunchables, I am afraid they cost a bit much to eat on a daily basis, but they make a nice treat for here and there when I'm feeling a bit down. For me, a 410 calorie pack is a substantial lunch and I had trouble finishing it, but I also keep to a pretty strict diet in general. You could always add more crackers if you want to stretch it, because there is enough spread for more.

GoPicnic is a unique concept in portable foods. Each lunch box has a individually packaged items:

Ginger Zip Fruit and Nut Mix
Terra Nostra Organic Robust 60% Dark Chocolate bar
Seapoint Farms Lightly Salted Dry Roasted Edamame
Late July Organic Classic Rich Crackers
GoPicnic Chili Line Salmon Spread

THE BREAKDOWN

The Dry Roasted Edamme is dry roasted soybeans seasoned with sea salt. They are a light crunchy, tasty snack. The entire package is 130 calories with 4 grams of fat, 10 grams of carbohydrates (8 of which is dietary fiber) and 14 grams of protein. Sodium is only 150 mg.

Ginger zip is a trail mix of Ginger peanuts, cranberries and banana chips. The ginger undertones is subtle and not overpowering. The package is 90 calories with 40 mg of sodium, 2 grams of protein, 13 grams of carbohydrates, and 40 calories of fat (majority of which is unsaturated fat).

The crackers and salmon dip combination is very good. The dip tastes of mild chili with salmon and light citrus undertones. The crackers are cripsy and lightly salted. The combination of textures and flavors is just right. However, I also put a few Edamame on top of the combination that made the combination a lot more enjoyable.

The dark chocolate is aromatic, creamy and bittersweet. I usually favor higher percentage of cocoa but this is an excellent finish to the Salmon Dip.

The box is made of 100% recycled materials. Inside the box there is a Sudoku puzzle.

OVERALL

I don't consider this particular product a full meal, as I consider it a great item for grazing throughout the morning (or afternoon). The entire package has 410 calories so it is a sizable portion of your daily recommended dietary intake. Overall this is a great concept since it is a portable, non-perishable item. It makes a great energy source for travel and hiking. It is a product that I have never tried before. I would definitely buy this with some degree of regularity.

I highly recommend it.

I wanted to like this. I REALLY wanted to like this. It is, in a word- HORRIBLE.

The idea is a good one. Meals that you can throw in a backpack or messenger bag, eat on the go, eat in the office, or just have in case you need a quick snack. Each "meal" comes with several items that are differing in quality and texture- and appeal.

Included in this package:

Chili Lime Salmon Spread- nasty. It is a fishy paste of minced up yuck flavored like leftover salmon and a too-sweet chili imitation.

Organic Classic Rich Crackers- six crackers that taste as dry as the cardboard box the meal comes in. A bad imitation of a Ritz cracker that misses the mark entirely.

Ginger Zip Fruit & Nut Mix- its a sweet, very ginger infused, trail mix with sweet covered/candied peanuts, clusters of stuff, and craisins. Actually- the best part of the meal.

Dry Roasted Edamame- on the box front, you see a picture of a vibrant, green, plump dish of Edamame. Inside, you have a package of funky looking rejects of a food mumification project. They taste like dust, diry, and the back end of a yak...I would imagine. Horrible. Just horrible.

Robust Dark Chocolate Square- actually, this wasn't bad either, but reminded me of cheap chocolate. The dark chocolate flavor felt too "fake" and the texture was a bit too waxy for me- but all in all, not bad either.

So...great idea- but a terrible execution. The food was a total mixed bag- but I did find use for the box of 6 that I was sent. I ate two meals for review purposes...then to further cement my review I ate the remaining chocolate, the remaining trail mix, gave the fish paste posing as food to the cat, the crackers to the ducks in the pond and threw the dried edamame in the trash. A better pre-packaged meal option is a military grade MRE- seriously. And we all know the sterling reputation those lil' packages of awesome have.

Summary: OVER PRICED CAT FOOD FOR VERY LAZY PEOPLE!
Text: OK, I'm all for having some convenience here and there and a 8 point meal by weight watchers standards sounds intriguing, but this "meal" is really only a snack. Most of the items in this box, you would be better off buying in larger quantities and making your own servings from them. Dry roasted Edamame very tasty, trail mix good, crackers - check, but none of them are something you can't buy in a larger quantity, Chocolate same as the everything else in this over priced snack pack. Now, we get to the reason I was interested in trying this "meal"....the salmon spread! YUCK, I couldn't even finish it, it tasted like what I would think cat food taste like(probably worse)! Do yourself a favor and buy some similar items and buy some small reseal-able containers and make you own nutritious snacks or meals, they'll taste better and you'll save a lot of money.

Summary: Maybe if you were in the Donner party
Text: This is truly some nasty salmon.  The taste and mouth feel are awful.  I love fish prepared in a variety of ways - but not mashed up with some yucky seasoning and put in a can.  I have served more appealing cat food (to cats of course).  The trail mix was mostly dried bananas.  The dried soy beans were flavorless.  The chocolate was ordinary.  The crackers were just OK as well.  All in all, a very disappointing box of food and certainly no picnic.

The title for this product should not include 'Meal' but 'Snack' instead.  The combination of salmon and crackers, dried edamame, dried fruit, and chocolate toffee doesn't seem like much of a meal but several snacks put together.  Regardless, that makes for a great lunch/snack while on the go.  My kids did some taste testing with me and really enjoyed the edamame (we did live in Japan though, so this was familiar to them), dried fruit and nuts, the crackers without salmon, and of course the chocolate.  I was worried the salmon would be too strong but it just had a hint of lime and chili.  A knife would have been nice to have to spread the salmon.  Overall I thought this would make a good snack for the kids and I in between outings or at the park.  Lots of fiber and a healthier options that a lot of products out there.

Summary: Perfect savory snack while working late
Text: I live in California, and work closely with a team in southern India, which means that I spend most evenings on the phone or in video conferences. I tend to keep a stash of snack foods in my desk to bridge the 6-9pm gap until I can get home to eat. I've been trying to shift from sweet snacks to savory foods, preferably with a bit of flavor.  These GoPicnic products fit the bill perfectly.

Summary: Really nice gourmet-type lunch to go
Text: I really enjoyed this lovely little gourmet treat.  It is a little on the pricy side, but not as much as a trip to the fast food place, and you get so much more.  I have ordered some of the other combos.  This one is especially nice.  The fact that it is compact and doesn't have to be refrigerated is a plus for me.

Summary: Pretty tasty with a good variety
Text:
The GoPicnic Ready-to-Eat meal comes in a cardboard box packed with individually canned and wrapped treats. You get a pack of crackers, a small can of salmon, a square of dark chocolate, a bag of dried edamame and a bag of dried fruit and nut mix. You also get a fork.

I started off with the edamame, which was pretty good. They tasted just like the large packs of roasted edamame that I've had from Costco. They can be a little dry and this "meal" is a bit dry and salty overall so you should definitely pack something to drink a long with it.

The dried fruit and nuts had a ginger flavor to it, which I thought was really good. I think these could have been a great snack on their own.

The crackers are just regular crackers, kind of like Ritz. The salmon comes in a small, pop top can, but for some reason, they give you a fork instead of a knife. The salmon itself was a little fishy and had a mushy consistency. You could definitely taste the chile and lime flavoring though. This was probably my least favorite part of the package, but still palatable enough.

The dark chocolate square was an excellent dessert at the end.

Overall, I liked the variety that came in this GoPicnic, but I wouldn't really call this a meal, except maybe for little kids. However, I'm not sure if kids would like the edamame and the salmon. I think these could be a good snack for adults though. The price is actually pretty reasonable considering the variety and the fancy packaging.

The food is of real quality, not gourmet but still very good. The salmon was especially tasty. And at four bucks a pop when you buy six GoPics, this is a perfect alternative to crappy airline food, or crappy school lunches, or just prepackaged generally crappy food.

If you like to eat well but sometimes have to suddenly go somewhere without time to make something good to take, and you know that fast food scams like gmo-filled fake-"healthy" places such as Chubway are just selling you processed junk, then these GoPicnic meals will save you lots of time and money and give you better food as well. Win/win/win.

We keep a few tucked away in the cupboard and they've already saved us from eating worse and spending more a number of times.

This is a fine prodcut, of which I think we'll soon see more, from many of the agri-biz idiots.
If you can't buy local and organic, this is a good stopgap in the meantime.

This is a really nice ready to eat meal on the go. It has a little bit of everything. You get crackers, salmon, fruit, edemame and some dark chocolate. Everything int the box is really good. Each item is individually wrapped. All you really need is a drink and you are set. I like to take these with me when I go hiking or go to the park and relax on the hammock. All the stuff doesn't take much space up in my backpack. If you get the stuff out of the box then you can fit it better on smaller backpacks. No need for fuel or stove when I go for overnight backpacking trips. I take a couple of these and I am set. The edemame are my favorite. They are almost like peanuts but with an edemame twist.

What really brings down my rating is the below cat food grade "Chili Lime Salmon". I mean, how can you go wrong with Chili Lime Salmon? That sounds absolutely delicious. I guess it doesn't translate well into a non-refrigerated slush. It tastes very cheap and fishy. I was expecting something on the level of canned tuna but this stuff is inedible. I couldn't finish it, so I gave it to my mom who eats anything and she said no thank you. I gave it to my cats and they sniffed it, then backed away slowly. My only other option would be to give it to the homeless people near my house, but I genuinely think they would be angry at me if I gave them this stuff. In short, stay away from the seafood slurry included in this box.

For some reason, I don't care for the crackers that come with this either. I usually love multigrain crackers, but these taste like cardboard covered in a shiny egg wash.

The fruit and nut mix was okay, but not as good as the Baja Blend in other GoPicnic boxes. I also taste zero ginger even though it's called "Ginger Zip".

The Edamame wasn't bad either. I would eat more of it.

The Buttercrunch Toffee was the best thing in the box. I wish someone mispackaged my boxes and included nothing but the toffee. Me want more.

I wouldn't buy this box again. I'd just get the toffee...and some more of that Baja Blend nut mix.

I was very pleasantly surprised by this product! The salmon spread was extremely tasty, and I loved that it required no refrigeration and was completely portable. It was delicious on the crackers. Additionally, I was so pleased that there was healthy protein included in this: so frequently on the go it is only carbs, carbs, carbs available, which do not last energy-wise. I felt this was just enough to keep one going during a flight, and until the next meal on the ground, for instance.

My toddler really liked the roasted edamame, as well as portions of the fruit and nut mix. My version of this had a square of dark chocolate, which was of good quality; now it looks as though they've changed the dessert portion to buttercrunch toffee, upon which I cannot comment.

I would buy this again, and plan to for my next travel adventure.

Others have reported on the taste, and I'm with the consensus - for boxed food it's decent. Not spectacular.

I'm mainly writing this review as a cost analysis.

For the same price per box, here's what I was able to put together (all items from amazon):

Splendid Spreads Brand, All Natural Salmon Spreads, International Variety Set, 6 Oz. Jars, Pack of 4 Jars: 2 ounces

Crunchmaster Multi-Grain Crackers Gluten Free 20 oz.: 1 ounce

Emerald Harmony Deluxe Fruit N Nut Trail Mix, 10-Ounce Bags (Pack of 6): 2 ounces

Roland Feng Shui Edamame, 4.4-Ounce Bags (Pack of 12): 1 ounce

Walkers Treacle Toffee, 3.5-Ounce Packages (Pack of 10): 1 ounce

That's 7 ounces, compared to GoPicnic's 4.3 ounces, and the price is actually less at the time of this writing. Of course this doesn't all come neatly wrapped in a box, you'd have to use some Tupperware to split up the individual packages, but I'm willing to bet it tastes better.

Summary: The Salmon isn't like Pics, if u eat all items, it WILL FILL U UP, but...............................................
Text:
The Salmon isn't like Pics, if u eat all items, it WILL FILL U UP, but...

it's not good like the others, the Salmon dip is NASTY...it's runny, dark Orange colored,
with little bits of Salmon in it...not pink/fluffy like pic.
THERE IS PLENTY of the Salmon, cause it's SPICY, a little goes a long way...
you GLOB a LITTLE on a sumptuous cracker *those are good* so it is enough to eat w/all the crackers.
With this meal YOU DON'T WISH THERE WERE MORE Salmon, like you wish there were more
in the other meal-type containers...cause eating all what is given is ENOUGH.

IT'S THE OTHER SNACKS THAT WILL HELP FILL YOU UP...
something that tastes like SOY NUTS is also NASTY, doesn't go with the rest of the culinary attempts AT ALL.
IT'S A HORRID MIX OF TASTES...but it will fill you up....I did not eat only the Salmon/crackers and a little soy-tasting soy nuts cause Salmon left nasty taste in my MOUTH.
saved rest for later....WISH I DIDN'T BUY TWO 6-Packs.

I was pleasantly surprised about the healthfulness and portability of these little meals. It is more than enough food for me- I tend to eat bento lunches, so I like having little portions of a bunch of things. I didn't think that the edamame was too dry- what do you expect? Chewy dried edamame?? I would have given this five stars, except that the salmon dip was a little...odd. It was spicy for me, though my boyfriend didn't pick up on any spice at all. So if you're not like us, you'll probably find that it's just the right amount of spice. But the flavor of the salmon stuff is definitely unnatural and strange to me. I'll eat them all anyway- it's not that bad.

Summary: As advertised....the good and the not so good
Text:
I've tried several of the gopicnic meal boxes and I will be upfront and say that one box is not the "perfect" meal. Each has their pluses and negatives. That being said, if I had to choose the one I liked the better out of them, I would go with this one. The spice in the salmon spread is a nice touch giving it some flavor. The nuts and chocolate are also good. The dry roasted edamame I'm not so sure about. They are...odd...and tends to be crumbly.

I guess calling them "meals" is a bit of a misnomer since they are more snack-sized. I usually toss in a yogurt cup to add to the meal when I take one for my lunch. The big plus is that the gopicnic's do not need refrigeration and can stay on the shelf for a bit before they're outdated. I think ones you get on airplanes actually give you more, but if you can get this past the security checkpoint, then I'd recommend it traveling, or for a quick lunch at work. Some have complained about the taste, but it's fine for me.

Summary: Not as good as the other GoPicnics
Text: I've tried five or six of the GoPicnic lunches so far, and even though I usually love salmon, this lunch is my least favorite. I'd suggest GoPicnic Ready-to-Eat Meals, Turkey Pepperoni + Cheese, 3-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6), GoPicnic Ready-to-Eat Meals, Hummus + Crackers, 4.4-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6), or GoPicnic Ready-To-Eat Meals Sunbutter + Crackers, 3.5-Ounce (Pack of 6).

Summary: Flavor promise unrealized, and stingy portions.
Text:
The most satisfying part of this snack assortment was the excellent dark chocolate. Rest of the contents sounded so much better than they ended up tasting, and the quantities were small as well. I really like these kinds of foods, but what was presented in this pack was a disappointment:

- salmon spread, odd flavors. I didn't find it as bad as some of the 1 star reviewers did, but it also didn't taste good enough for me to ever want more, and certainly didn't remind me of what salmon usually tastes like. I was expecting to be knocked over by fishy odor, but detected only slight fishiness. It would have spread easier with a knife than the included fork. Odd texture and sort of on the wet side, not surprising because the second and third ingredients were water and red pepper paste, which probably helped reduce the salmon flavor by diluting it. Only about 3 tablespoons.

- crackers, six small imitation Ritz crackers

- fruit & nut mix, nice flavors, but too sugary. 3/4 ounce, would have liked more.

- edamame, a bit too dry to eat pleasurably, tasted mildly bad (but if you like edamame you might like the flavor) 1 ounce.

- chocolate, a really nice rich dark chocolate. 0.43 ounce, though small, it was satisfying.

Besides the odd flavors, the size could be too small for a workday lunch (depending on your appetite), but it would be a sufficient snack for an adult, or maybe an lunch for a child who likes these oddities. (410 calories, 22g protein, 16g fat, and a whopping 48g of carbs). What's with these micro portion sizes? There was almost more packaaging material than food.

If you absolutely have to have a shelf-stable snack on hand, consider this if the contents particularly appeal to you. But I feel it should have been better.

I love the idea. Not that I'd want to look forward to this ready-to-eat meal as my lunch, but it would be reassuring to know that I have a few of these in one of my desk drawers in case I'm too busy to deal with lunch.

So I love the idea.

I also think the price makes sense (currently $24 for 6).

I might even consider this meal as a convenient solution for traveling (since airlines don't really feed us anymore).

The one thing I wouldn't do, though, is consider this to be a really good idea for a good meal. It just isn't that good.

So why am I not more enthusiastic? It's the main course: it was pretty bad.

When I sampled mine, I was a little hurried and started with the odds and ends. First the fruit snack, then the edamame, and so on. Every one of these smaller snacks were really fantastic.

I repeat: Most of the stuff in this meal was REALLY FANTASTIC. The dried edamame were creative, the fruit snack was original, the crackers were good, the chocolate was great.

The problem was with the "main course", the salmon spread. I love salmon. I'll eat it in any way imaginable. I think it's pretty hard to wreck salmon. But somehow they found a way. The taste and texture of the salmon spread was just weird. Not that it was gross or sickening, it just wasn't appetizing. What a shame.

I'm a decent-sized guy who likes a decent meal. I have fairly discerning tastes and I like to enjoy my food. So this meal is merely a means to checking off a to-do item (fluids-check, grub-check, ...). It's a way to avoid a totally disastrous day ("I had to work long hours and didn't even have time for lunch...").

So all in all, I'd probably buy another set of these to keep around for emergencies, but I wouldn't consider this meal to be "Plan A". This meal would be a backup plan for when my day goes off track.

Nutritionally speaking this is a decent package, but it was in no way good enough to justify the price. The salmon spread was fishy, the chocolate was waxy and the crackers were flavorless. The only great thing in here was the roasted soy nuts, which I can get elsewhere. Not worth retail, that is for sure.

This was a cute little meal and I was excited to try it.  I personally didn't like the taste of the salmon.  It just wasn't to my liking.  The other items in the pack were good, but way too many soy beans.  I didn't think the taste was bad, but it wasn't pleasing.  I would probably buy this product if the salmon was a plain or a smoked flavor though.

For convenience, this is excellent. Everything comes individually wrapped with expiration dates beyond that printed on the box. It even includes a wrapped fork and a Sudoku puzzle on the box bottom. Some may complain about excessive packaging, but it does keep the contents dry. I stuck mine in with some fruit and the outer box soaked up some moisture and became damp, so I appreciate the individual packaging.

For taste, this falls a little short. The salmon spread did have a slight chili flavor but very little lime taste. The texture was strange--somewhat mushy and like a gritty jelly. There was a definite fishiness. The crackers were OK; they were similar to Ritz crackers. I have had the edamame before and they were as expected. To me, the best part was the fruit and nut mix. It has a nice flavor although I did not get many banana bits.

Overall, I thought the meal was underwhelming. It was not enough to fill me. I thought it was a little expensive for the amount of food.

This upscale pre-packed lunch is tasty, healthy, imaginative and handy. In this case the product description on Amazon does give the ingredients but not the Nutrition Facts a label-reading purchaser might want: Per box, 410 calories, Total Fat 16 grams - 25% Daily Value, Saturated Fat 5g - 25% DV, Cholesterol 10 milligrams - 3% DV, Sodium 660mg - 28% DV, Total Carbohydrates 48g - 16% DV, of which Dietary Fiber is 11g - 44% DV and sugars 21g, Protein 22g, Vit A 0%, Vit C 10%, Calcium 0%, Iron 10%.

Of supreme importance to some is the Allergen information which has been carefully noted on the box: the spread contains fish; the crackers contain wheat and soy; the fruit and nut mix contains peanuts, almonds, cashews, pecans, walnuts, Brazil nuts, hazelnuts, milk-containing products, wheat, soy; the edamame is manufactured in a plant that processes peanuts and other nuts; the dark chocolate is made on equipment that also produces soy, milk, wheat, peanut and tree nuts.

Other reviewers have discussed the various foods included so no need to go down the list again; just to say that I found everything included to be tasty. No complaints! ...Although I would say that I agree with the observations that the packaging adds significantly to the waste stream (but I can't suggest an alternative), and a plastic spreader would have worked better than a fork.

This is an excellent repast for those who can justify the expense. Others have pointed out that in certain circumstances, this lunch kit may actually be cost effective because decent food, if available, may be even more expensive - or far too inconvenient.

ProfileName: Scary Gertrude,  the Bad Sheriff for Life "Li...
Text:
This is a cute little packet and an easy way to find a simple lunch when you're on the move and don't like fast food. What's even nicer is that these are heart healthy and contain no MSG, HFCS, or trans fats. It's a definite treat to find them all in a one portion lunch kit.
