This has a good little selection of items in it, the salmon and crackers, a fruit and nut mix, dry roasted edamame, and a small piece of dark chocolate. Although I was a little suspicious of salmon in a plastic container, it is tasty. The salmon has a little kick to it that keeps it from tasting like tuna fish. The dried fruit and nut mix are surprisingly good. The edamame? It's alllll riiiiight if you like that sort of thing. Put enough salt on it and I'll eat it. A small piece of chocolate brings this lunch to a sweet and dark end.

I'm planning to get a six pack of these to keep in the car. So many times when I'm out running errands, I dig around the bottom of my purse and end up having a smushed protein bar for lunch. This is an awesome replacement.

Summary: didn't impress me but not bad
Text:
I liked the last go picnic product I tried but this one is only so-so. First, the salmon spread - squishy and not much flavor despite the chili. The Late July crackers are good but without something good to go on top, they're just crackers. The fruit and nut mix was really good but only a small taste. I ate the dried edamame peas didn't taste bad or good. Also, they were so dry that I got the hiccups! The chocolate was the best part and just about right; a very small square. However, if you took this with you on a hike, the chocolate would melt.

On the plus side, if you are burning a lot of calories, this pack provides plenty of healthy calories to replenish you - 410 calories in the pack. 16 grams of fat comes from edamame peas, peanuts and salmon (and a few from the crackers). You get 22g of protein. There are 48 grams of carbohydrates with 21 of those as sugar and 11 grams of FIBER! The products inside this little box are all top quality and generally organic. It's not bad, just didn't impress me with flavor and texture.

ProfileName: Miz Ellen "all the letters of my real name"
Summary: Crunchy and Fun but Pack a Drink Also
Text:
I found the GoPicnic Salmon & Crackers lunch to be a cut above most commercially packed lunches in flavor and nutritional value. With only 410 calories, it still made a satisfying meal with lots of "chew appeal". The dominant texture was crunchy: crackers, fruit and nut snack and the little bag of dry roasted soybeans each made a different crunchy noise in the mouth. The banana chips in the fruit snack were quite hard and the soybeans (called edamame on the package) needed lots of chewing. The latter were dry to the core and lightly salted so when chewed they gradually ground to powder in the mouth and provoked thirst. I remembered eating these (in a fresher version) in Japanese bars. The salmon spread is brightly colored, spicy hot and is a great foil for the soybeans which are neutral underneath the light salting. The crackers are delicate and make perfect platforms for the salmon. The dark chocolate is excellent--a very pure flavor, not too sweet.

Although salt is not laid in with a deliberately heavy hand, nearly everything here has salt in it. Because one box contains 660mg of sodium, this isn't designed for folks on a low salt diet. I'd definitely pack a drink of fruit juice if this was to be my lunch box for the day or/and add an apple or orange to counterbalance the dryness of this portable lunch. Beer would work also but might not be practical...

Summary: nice snack but not at that price
Text:
I enjoyed most of the snack but not the salmon spread. I love fish. But this spread was too rich and not salty enough. And it left a funny taste in my mouth. Still, the rest of the snack made up for that. The crackers were nice and tasty; the dry-roasted soybeans are as addictive as you'd expect and the fruit and nut mix was great. (The nut and fruit mix does have peanuts so if you're allergic you should know that.) And the chocolate candy was fantastic. So everything except the salmon was great so maybe the other products in that line are better.

The only other thing I'd add is that this is definitely a snack and not a meal. So, all told, I am not sure it's worth it for the kind of price they're asking.

Summary: Great concept, nice snacks, not quite a picnic...
Text:
Growing up on the free lunch program at school I wasn't exposed to the unhealthy treats and convinience foods of my peers until I was in my teens. Maybe that's part of why I prefer a warm soup with toast or a sandwich piled with veggies over peanut butter sandwiches and pudding cups. Keeping that in mind I thought this version of the Ready-to-Eat Meal would suit my palate and fill my tummy nicely.

I'll admit, I love novelty and there's just something about single-serving packaging that makes me all excited. Lime-chili Salmon Spread? Snack mix with Ginger Peanuts? It all sounded so fancy and grown-up. But then I looked at the outer package's nutritional info. At 400+ calories for this handful of snackage I was a little leary. Lots of fat (though I'd say with salmon some of it is the good kind) and lots of fiber. Read the nutrition info and you be the judge whether this would be for you.

Let me offer my assessment of the individual food items. The crackers were perfect, just the sort of thing I'd want to put a spread on, crisp and mild in flavor, solid enough to handle being topped. The salmon spread was nice in theory but had a (for lack of a better word) sludgey quality to it. I didn't taste lime and the chili was barely noticable, this felt like someone had tossed raw salmon in a blender and canned it. I was not impressed and I am a salmon LOVER. The Edamame were too dry but not overly salted as some can be. The portion on those was pretty big and since they aren't my favorite alone I was happy to move on. The mix of dried cranberries, banana chips and ginger peanuts was interesting and actually pretty yummy. The portion size looks like a lot on the box but was actually much smaller. My one complaint was that most of the ginger was rubbed off the peanuts and had settled into the bottom of the package. Lastly, the dark chocolate was a nice treat at the end, a decent quality and with a great texture.

Overall this was not quite my cup of tea. Aside from my comments regarding the individual items I must say I was still hungry after my GoPicnic. This would make a nice item to toss into your bag for a post-gym nosh if you're a lunch-time gym-goer or a good thing to pack when taking that dreaded family road trip so you could skip the fast food. I'd probably pick a different pack for myself but overall I really dig this idea and think the options in these being fruit, whole grains and healthy protiens are brilliant.

ProfileName: Chris Swanson "I'm just this guy, you know?"
Text:
So, here we go. The latest in picnic stuff for the Whole Foods crowd. It wasn't bad, really, but it wasn't anything special, and I don't really see the interest.

First, we have the salmon and chili lime paste. Now I like salmon, but I'm not used to it having a bit of a bite. It's not horribly spicy or anything like that, but you know it's there. It was fairly tasty, but nothing to write home about.

Next the crackers. They're crackers. Moving on.

The fruit and nut mix. This contained bananas, cranberries and peanuts. All were dried and apparently dusted with ginger, thus potentially addictive to any alien lizards out there. The taste on these wasn't bad, but again, nothing special.

Then we come to the horror of this package. The dried edamame. Why, oh, why, would anyone eat this? Not just lacking flavor, they actually seemed to suck out any flavor in my mouth from the previous food. Worse than that, while they didn't have any actual taste, they had an aftertaste that was truly something to behold, and not in a good way.

Then, finally, we have the organic dark chocolate. It's chocolate. Pretty hard to screw up. I would have preferred milk chocolate, but that's just me.

So there you go. Overall this pack wasn't bad, but that edamame really killed it hard. That stuff was really awful. Otherwise, it's largely inoffensive and tasty, but overpriced. You can do better elsewhere.

First let me say what is right about this product. It is a nice mix of items and textures, consisting of packages of spread, crackers, a slab of dark chocolate, toasted edamame nuts, and a mix of dried banana slices, cranberries, and dry honey roasted peanuts. There is sufficient food for a quick lunch or snack, with crunchies left for later. A plastic fork is included.

The spread is ample for the six buttery tasting crackers, and is neither too stiff to spread nor too runny. It is sweet with a bit of heat; too sweet for my taste, and I could barely taste the salmon. There could have been more of the fruit and nut mix, and less of the edamame, which my partner found undersalted and slightly musty tasting. The dark chocolate was OK.

For a grab-and-go product, it was better than many. Only 410 calories, which is great, but has over 600 mg. of salt, more than 1/4 the rda for an adult.

After reading the negative review that rated this kit below military MREs I was afraid that the food will be terrible, but I tried to keep an open mind when I was tasting it. In my opinion, this kit is not nearly as bad as that review portrayed it to be.

I liked the salmon spread and the crackers. Although, for my taste, the spread was a little on a liquid side the flavor was good and it combined well with crackers. I also liked the dried fruit and the chocolate.

The only item that I thought was not good at all is the Dry Roasted Edamame (I do like normal edamame that is served in Japanese restaurants). I thought the beans were too dry, the flavor was not good, and it was too much of it compared to other items. Also the look of it was not appetizing at all - dirty green color with a lot of peeled dry skin inside the package.

I had this kit for lunch and it filled me up. Considering that it contains 410 calories, I say it was not bad. I think that if the company reworked or replaced the edamame item, I would have liked the food more.

In my opinion, the current price of thirty bucks for six pack (five bucks per kit) is way too high. There is absolutely no way (banning food shortages) I would pay that much for this kit. In my view, this kit might work as a snack when taking kids out to a park, but I would not buy it to feed friends or take to a romantic picnic.

Having a neatly prepackaged lunch that doesn't need refrigeration is a good idea, but GoPicnic needs a lot more work on the items they are including in their "picnic in a box" before it's something I'll want to keep in the cupboard.
The packaging is cute - small and eaily portable - something you could throw in a bookbag or purse. Some of the items included were fairly tasty like the dry roasted edamame and the dried fruit and nut combo. I enjoyed both. The salmon spread, however, was completely disgusting. It looked and smelled worse than any cat food I've ever seen. Since I've never eaten cat food, I can't say which is better of the two. I cannot imagine, however, that cat food could taste much worse than this stuff did. Also included were a small square of dark chocolate and some crackers which, while not impressive, were not unpleasant. Overall, the box added up to more of a variety of snack items than a meal and at around $5 each, it's pricey for the amount of food you actually get. I wouldn't purchase this item again and, after the trauma that the salmon spread caused, I would be leary of trying other varieties of GoPicnic.

but the rest of it was not so great, actually.

1. Dry Roasted Edamame (soybeans). I couldn't eat them. Tasted like dust. I do like edamame generally and do eat soy products, but this incarnation was not edible. The good point of it the high protein, so if you like the taste, they do provide nutritional value.

2. Ginger Zip fruit and nut mix. OK, but too sweet. Dried fruits without sugar would be fine IMHO.

3. Crackers--not bad. They are billed as "organic", and the ingredients are pretty healthy, but they are made with "organic wheat flour" (ie, white flour) and not whole grain, so they could have more flavor and fiber if they had whole wheat or other whole grain. You get six small round crackers that look like Ritz, but not as sweet.

4. Salmon Spread for the crackers--mediocre. They have added a lot of water to this product, and the soupy consistency is unappealing.

5. Chocolate square--all's well that ends well?

In summary, this product while handy in terms of size, storage and shelf-life, does not live up to the purpose intended. Unlike some other Vine reviewers, I only got one package, which, in this case is OK. I would be willing to try other varieties of this product, but the "salmon and crackers" is not one I would buy or recommend.

Summary: Despite the organic labeling, not all that healthy a choice
Text:
"Salmon+crackers" is advertised as a "ready to eat meal." At just under four and a half ounces net weight it 's more of a snack than a meal, but leaving that aside, I found many other issues with this product.

It's further advertised as a balanced meal featuring a number of organic components. But a look at the side panel tells the tale: 410 calories, 150 of these from fat; 5g saturated fat; 660mg of sodium; and 48g of carbohydrates including 21g of sugar. Healthy? Not even close. The only redeeming feature is 22g of protein.

There are five components in the mix. There's a bag of dry roasted edamame. If you're not familiar with edamame, it's a popular Asian snack or appetizer. The dry roasted edamame in the GoPicnic package were very dry indeed and had suffered a huge loss of characteristic flavor.

Next is the Ginger Zip fruit and nut mix. I found this to be at once too salty and too sweet. I suspect a lot of the sodium and sugar was in this package.

Then we have the Late July Organic Classic Rich Crackers, which are quite similar to Ritz crackers. There were six of them; they were fresh and crispy with a nice crunch and bite, and not too salty or sweet.

The GoPicnic Chili Lime Salmon Spread is, obviously, made to spread on the crackers. More than enough spread is provided for the six crackers, though you'll need to have remembered your own knife or something to actually do the spreading. There was a nice chili taste, not too strong, and a clean lime taste. But the salmon spoiled it all. There were little shreds of salmon and one big chunk; the mix obviously wasn't mixed very well. And it tasted much more like sardine than salmon. The fish had an "old" taste and smell that was very unappealing.

The package was completed with a Terra Nostra Organic Robust Dark Chocolate Square, which had a nice bitterness and strong cocoa flavor; it was perhaps a bit strong on buttery mouth feel, but it was really quite good.

If you're thinking of getting these to serve to children, that may not be the best idea. They won't like the salmon spread and they likely won't like the edamame.

If you're thinking of serving these to adults, there are probably much better, healthier options. It wouldn't be all that hard to make up your own package with tastier, healthier, and more substantial contents.

I can't recommend the GoPicnic Salmon+Crackers. It's neither healthy nor particularly good.

Summary: Don't judge this meal by its cover...
Text:
Bottom line: I expected better. Better taste, better quality, etc. Two things really impacted my three star rating here: the salmon and the plastic fork...

Packaging:
The packaging is fun, but it's misleading. There are fewer crackers and far fewer bits of the fruit and nut mixed than shown own the actual packaging. In addition, my salmon certainly did NOT look like what you see on the box. I'll add this on packaging as well, but for a product going for the "all-natural" and certified organic route, I was a little surprised that the included fork was actually plastic and not a biodegradable product. The best part about this package was the Sudoku game at the bottom!

Salmon:
My chili lime salmon was mushy, and I didn't see any nice looking chunks as per the box. It was more of a puree than a mix of salmon. My wife tasted it with me and we definitely agree that it tasted a bit more fishy than we're used to with salmon. We also had to sort through a few boney parts. Additionally, the chili had a kick by the lime seemed to be hiding away somewhere.

Crackers:
The crackers were great! I can't get how they make something taste so buttery without butter!

Edamame:
There was a ton of edamame in comparison to the other portions. I thought the roasted edamame was pretty decent, but my wife said that it had a bad aftertaste.

Fruit & Nuts Mix:
This was probably the highlight of the whole box; the peanuts were sweet, salty and had a great taste of ginger. I will probably try to find where I can purchase this mix because it was so great; the dried cranberries and bananas were a nice compliment.

Chocolate:
Organic and tasty. At 60% Cacoa, I expected a little more bitterness from the chocolate, but didn't really taste it (I think this would have been better with a little bitterness) - but it was still good.

Last notes:
I'm not sure I would try this again. The Salmon really kind of ruined it for me; at the end of the day, the only way I can encapsulate my description of it is "slightly nasty." Everything else was fine, but the box wasn't defined by everything else, it was defined by the Salmon...

The chili lime salmon spread is a little on the fishy side and also a bit on the spicy side. If you like like a bit of spice then you might enjoy it. On a scale of 1-10, it's about a 6 in terms of spiciness. The salmon is smashed up into a paste, so don't expect salmon filets. The slight fishiness was a slight putoff.

The salmon comes with a small package of 6 "Late July" organic crackers (90 calories, vegan) which were very good, as crackers go. They are similar to Ritz crackers, only more of an oval shape.

A small package of "Sweet Perry Orchards" "Ginger Zip" fruit and nut mix was part of the meal. It includes peanuts with a crunchy ginger coating, banana chips and dried cranberries. It's a tiny little package, not even 1 ounce.

Also included is 1 ounce of "Seapoint Farms" "Dry Roasted Edamame". This product is very crunchy and healthy. While it contains 14 grams of protein, it's not very exciting but decent nonetheless. Still, 14 grams of soy protein in only 1 ounce of edamame is pretty good nutritionally-speaking. They are lightly salted.

If you'd like some chocolate with your fish paste, you'll receive 0.43 ounces of Terra Nostra Organic Dark 60% Cacao. This chocolate is darker than what I'm used to due to the 60% cacao content, but it's good. But again, it's just one little piece, so keep that in mind.

I don't believe this that this product represents a good value at it's current price as of this writing. I can't particularly recommend it, although some people might like it. But the price coupled with the small size of each serving (4.4 ounces) coupled with the fishiness of the salmon paste was not especially to my liking.

Summary: Delicious Snacks all in One Box
Text:
I think $4 a box is a great price for this GoPicnic box filled with tasty snacks. While I would have preferred the salmon to be smoked it was still good but a little spicy. The crackers were buttery and deliciously crunchy. The dry roasted edamame needed a little more salt but were still good. What I really liked most was the fruit and nut mix with dried bananas, ginger peanuts and cranberries. What a great combination. And to finish your snack meal there is some organic chocolate which is the best dark chocolate I've ever tasted. This box would be perfect for taking to work, for hiking and biking and for a spontaneous picnic at the park.

~The Rebecca Review

Summary: Not too big and not too tasty
Text:
If I had to sum up what I though of "GoPicnic Ready-to-Eat Meals, Salmon + Crackers," I would probably say that it is an adult form of the popular "lunchables" that were easy-to-make lunches for kids to take to school with them. This is about the same size as those kid's lunches, which means that it's probably not going to fill an adult up and is therefore not really to be considered a meal. It's a pretty in-depth snack to take on a hike or even to just eat at home if you need to nibble; and it contains 22g protein, 11g fiber, and 410 calories. However, it's not the tastiest food in the world, and I'm not sure that I actually liked it all that much.

The box has a tab that will pull in order to open the box, and inside you will find the following: a plastic fork, a plastic container of salmon spread, a package containing six crackers, a mini bag of a fruit/nut trail mix, a mini bad of dry roasted soy beans (edamame), and a square of chocolate. I personally didn't even use the fork since I found it better to use a knife to spread the salmon with. As for the salmon's taste...it was fishy with a hint of citrus. I appreciate good salmon, but this was not good, in my opinion. The crackers were delicious, though (how can you ruin those?). I didn't like the roasted soy beans either; they were like burnt sunflower seeds with a peanut texture. As for the fruit/nut trail mix, it contained very few banana chips, cranberries, and peanuts. They were all covered with a layer of sugar, which, of course, made them delicious. The chocolate was divine, as well, but the square was very, very small. Another thing to note is that on the inside of the box, there are some interesting facts and a sudoku puzzle.

Overall, I would just have to say that I personally like the layout of this product but not so much the ingredients. I would love to try another type such as the steak nuggets or turkey pepperoni, but I will not be buying this one again. I would definitely encourage you to try the other types of the GoPicnic series, but I just can't recommend this one.

This is really good. The salmon spread with crackers is tasteful and satisfying, the trail mix is good -- there is just not quite enough of it. The edamame is dry roasted and hearty. The chocolate was the only part of the meal that was less than satisfying -- it's
dark chocolate w/o much sweetness.

I would recommend this for a lunch or snack on the go. It would be also really good for trying to reduce the portion of food you eat. I admit that I had to raid the refrigerator following eating this for lunch to fill myself up.

There is something magical about a box lunch, the merger of opening a present and the anticipation of a good meal. The GoPicnic ready to eat meal is a box lunch for hiking, picnicking, and school field trips. It requires no refrigeration, but does have a limited shelf life.

The portion size is good for children, although teens and adults may still be hungry after eating one. The Salmon and Cracker meal includes a salmon spread, crackers, a ¾ oz. pack of fruit & nut mix, dry roasted edamame, and a chocolate square. The whole meal has 410 calories with 16 g of fat and 660 mg of sodium. The selections sound healthy, but more effort could have been made to cut down on fat and salt. No drink is included. A fork is included, but no napkin. The box is study and the crackers were undamaged.

The salmon spread is tasty enough to wish the portion were larger. The crackers are indistinguishable from Ritz crackers. The fruit & nut mix is mostly peanuts and banana chips, with a rare dried cranberry. The dry roasted edamame puts the emphasis on "dry." The highlight is the chocolate square. The salt content is evident in the taste and in the need to have a drink handy.

The cost, $5/meal, seems high for what you get.

In summary, the GoPicnic Salmon and Crackers meal is a good attempt at healthy food for on-the-go, but the attempt misses the mark. Like a Catskills comedian, I have to complain that the food was mediocre and the portions were small.

Summary: I thought I was eating baby food
Text:
I often times wonder who sits in on these food meetings to determine the nutritional value of a product like this. While it is no mean feat to design something visually appealing, with just the right number of calories to appear healthy, taste and consistency of flavor should be at the forefront of the mind. Upon arrival both my wife and I thought the product was great. Everything was packaged nice, it looked like the perfect little quick lunch or in between meals snack. The ginger coated peanuts were delicious, the edamame (soy nuts) were great, and even the bit of chocolate that was included was delightful.

As with all of these quick snacks though, e.g. lunchables or tuna packs from starkist, the assumption is that if they cannot put an entire sandwich in the box, they may as well go for a cracker and "meat" combo to make up for it. Lunchables pioneered the concept commercially and it seems as if everyone else is playing catch up. In this aspect and this aspect only has "go picnic" failed miserably. They have taken one of the most healthiest fish, salmon, and mascerated it beyond recognition. They should be embarrassed to call it salmon. The flavors of chile and lime should be great, instead it is just one big mess. It looks like baby food, has the texture of baby food, but is not fit for human consumption. Since this is the main course they desparately need to go back to the drawing board if they expect to not end up on the shelves at Big Lots or any other remainder item merchandiser.

Summary: Reminds me of Airline style food
Text:
When I first popped open the box, it sort of reminded me of past "Economy" flight meals. I got my peanuts, my crackers, the meat, and some chocolate. It has that feel, and taste. You really do eat with your eyes first.

The small box is really a snack in my opinion. It has the nutrition to be classified as a meal though. Each box contains 410 calories, with 16g of fat, 48g of carbs, and 22g of protein. The only thing it lacks is heft to make it a satisfying meal.

The entire meal is organic and contains no trans fats, high fructose corn syrup, or MSG. It doesn't need refrigeration as long as it is stored in room temperature. The shelf life seems to be about 6 months.

I enjoyed the crackers and salmon, and found the fruit and nut mix delightful. The dry roasted endamame was not too good though. I prefer mine steamed, and them being roasted made me very thirsty. Make sure you pack something to drink if you are eating this on the go.

The chocolate didn't have much taste, but was a nice touch to finish off the "meal".

All in all, it's a nice idea, and if you like to bring lunch to work and don't want to eat anything too heavy, this is a great alternative.

gopicnic is a more healthy version of the Lunchables that are so popular, and this variety is quite good.

For allergy sufferers, the warnings for all the internal packets are printed clearly on the side of the box under the nutrition information. Similarly, all the ingredients are on an end panel, and I can pronounce all of them. I like the lack of MSG, trans fats, or the dreaded HFCS.

Everything in the package was fresh tasting and flavorful. The light crispy crackers have a Ritz-like flavor. Salmon spread had a good flavor with nice spice bite, but not overpowering. A knife would have been a better implement, rather than the included plastic fork, for spreading the salmon. The ginger zip fruit & nut mix was also fresh crispy, but I didn't detect much ginger flavor, even in the bits of coating that had come off the nuts. The edamame was crispy and crunchy, lightly salty. The chocolate square is a nice dark chocolate, but not bitter.

With the addition of a beverage of your choice, this would make a healthier option for lunch than a trip to the burger joint or the vending machine.

The only down side to this type of meal is the amount of packaging. While the carton is made of 100% recycled fiber (at least 35% post-consumer) and can go into the recycling bin, everything else goes in the trash. Even that, though, is a minimum. The only plastic is the cup for the salmon and the fork. The rest is cellophane or foil wrap.

Though a homemade lunch may be cheaper this isn't a bad alternative.

When I ordered this GoPicnic set, I thought all I was getting was the crackers and salmon spread, but to my delight, it's a full lunch set. You get the crackers and spread, dried edamame, ginger nuts and dried fruit, and a little organic chocolate. For the most part, I thought this was really tasty. The salmon spread does taste like salmon, which is great, and the lime and chili complement it well. It's just a tad spicy, so mild that I didn't even notice it until I was well into eating it. I liked the slight kick, and it shouldn't bother people with sensative tongues. The crackers are organic, but you wouldn't know it. They're crunchy and buttery, kind of like Ritz crackers. My favorite item was the fruit and nut mix. They were salty and sweet, and the ginger went so well with the nuts peanuts and cranberries. It had a slight kick, no more than the salmon spread, and this was a great complement. The chocolate was ok. If you've had organic chocolate before, you know what to expect. It wasn't very sweet at 60% cacao, and it wasn't very smooth. Not really my thing, but eh. The only thing I didn't really like was the dried edamame. I generally like edamame, but dried... the first few bites were good. I liked the dry, almost flaky texture. But after a few bites, it tasted a bit weird.

This has 16g of fat (25% of your daily value), but only 5g of saturated fat (25% daily value), most of which come from the salmon spread. There are 410 calories and 150 calories from fat.There are only 10mg cholesterol (3% daily value). There are 48g of carbohydrates (16% daily value) and 11g dietary fiber (44% daily value). The sodium isn't bad at 660mg (28% daily value), and neither are the sugars at 21g. The biggest problem is that there's not a whole lot of nutritional value here. You get 22g protien, which is pretty good, but only 10% of your daily value for iron and vitamin C. Fish has plenty of omega-3s, though, and peanuts and cranberries are full of anti-oxidants, so that's something.

The packaging is very nice. I love the colors and design, especially the blue gingham pattern on the top. On the inside, there are fun facts and even a sudoku puzzle for you to complete. It's easy to open, and everything comes in its own easy to open packaging. There's a plastic fork for you to use, though I didn't need it. It doesn't all seem biodegradeable, though, and some might not like that.

Overall, this was a very tasty lunch set. It was pretty filling and not bad for you. A great alternative to things like Lunchables, which are just full of sodium. Recommended!

Summary: Useful for hiking and may be a good emergency item to have on hand
Text:
I like the concept here that GoPicnic has. The box is convenient although I would imagine that a flatter type of design of sorts would make it more 'carryable' for hiking or even camping.

I live in earthquake country and always look for things to have to store or have available for a possible disaster. If you live in EQ, hurricane or Tornado country, this may be a handy thing to add to your store of goods for such an event. Although the shelf life is somewhat short, you would have to cycle older product out more often.

Someone mentioned in another review that the salmon smelled rather 'fishy' which initially raised an eyebrow, but the taste of the salmon was rather good although some may find it spicy. I found the spicyness more of a zing and it faded quickly with the crackers, edamame and ginger zip trail mix. The chocolate mini bar in the pack it a dark chocolate that has a very rich taste and a great ending to a quick meal.

I want to try the other brands of GoPicnic for the possibility of kids at school using them once in a while for lunch. Maybe the salmon is too strong for them unless they have their tastes developed for it.

The edamame nuts were tasty and good addition. The crackers where nice for the meal and did not add flavor or take away flavor from the salmon and the trail mix was good.

Overall, a great little addition for a quick hike. The box says the total calories is about 410, pretty good for a snack that has so much variety. I would like to see the price come down some how, however, the way it is packaged probably requires the price that you see.

Try GoPicnic and have fun with it.

Summary: Good alternative to similar, less healthy products
Text:
I have to admit that I wasn't overwhelmed with adoration for this product, although it is a nice alternative to less healthy versions of this type of meal.

The food was all fresh and tasty. The salmon is in a little container similar to the dipping sauces you would get for chicken nuggets at McDonalds, already prepared with the sauce (I wasn't expecting that.. I though it would have to be mixed) It was nice that it wasn't mixed with mayonnaise. You peel off the top label and then use the fork to put small amounts on the crackers. I didn't think there would be enough, as it doesn't seem like much, but it turned out there was plenty. The crackers are "Late July" brand - a slightly healthier version of a Ritz. The trail mix was decent.. the ginger peanuts tasted neither like ginger or peanuts, but were good just the same. The dried edamame was fine, but I didn't finish it.. there was simply too much of that particular texture and flavor for me to want it all, even though it was a small bag. The chocolate, as you might expect was a nice treat!

My biggest problem with this item is that at the end of eating it (even had I finished the edamame), I just wasn't full. It is not substantial enough to be a meal. Also, not that expected differently, but the amount of trash at the end of the meal considering how little food there was is embarrassingly unsustainable. The plastic fork they included probably should have been compostable-style given the audience this is appealing to, but was not.

The box had a sudoku puzzle printed on the inside for those looking for entertainment on the go while they snack, but maybe they should have then included a little golf pencil or something like that.

It was good. But I don't think I'm going to order more.

Summary: A healthy meal-to-go option that is not too bad tasting
Text:
Specifically marketed towards the health conscious, the all-organic "GoPicnic Ready-to-Eat Meals, Salmon + Crackers" is a pretty good meal-to-go alternative. The cracker and salmon combo is quite tasty, fairly rich tasting, while not being too salty, while the fruit and nut mix and the organic chocolate bar both provide a nice sweet treat. About the only thing I didn't really enjoy was the dry roasted edamame; it wasn't awful tasting (and was particularly filling), but the taste was bland and dry to my palate.

A few caveats: "GoPicnic Ready-to-Eat Meals, Salmon + Crackers" is not for everyone, to be sure. Those weaned on Kraft "lunchables" will probably miss the heavily processed and salty taste they have become accustomed to with those types of meals-to-go.

Also, as is the case with so many healthy food alternatives, this is clearly priced towards an upscale market. While the cost of $5.00 per box is competitive with (or if you live in the NYC area, actually cheaper than) other health-oriented meal-to-go alternatives, it is certainly priced higher than mainstream meal-to-go products, such as the aforementioned Kraft "Lunchables" (priced at around $3.60 a box here on Amazon.com). This means that those on a tight budget are once again left out in the cold when it comes to choosing healthy foods alternatives. When is that inequity ever going to be truly addressed?

All things aside, "GoPicnic Ready-to-Eat Meals, Salmon + Crackers" is a good meal-to-go alternative and worth picking up for those so inclined.

Summary: Good but not for picky eaters
Text:
The convenience of this to-go meal was quite handy for me this morning, as I was running extremely late.

However, I'm a selective eater and the only thing that appealed to me in this box was the salmon and crackers, and the chocolate! The salmon was nice, a little spicy but good. The crackers and chocolate were excellent.

For the price, I can't recommend this unless you think you will enjoy all of the items in the box.

Summary: Quality Food For People On The Go
Text:
GoPicnic is a great organic alternative to fast food on the go.

The meal in each package consists of four parts:

The chili-lime salmon spread and crackers, a fruit & nut mix containing ginger peanuts, cranberries, and banana chips (though ours only contained one chip), dry roasted edamame, and a dark chocolate square.

This was surprisingly filling, quality food. My body even felt good after eating, so I know it wasn't cleverly-disguised junk. My children enjoyed the chocolate, salmon spread and crackers (Ritz-like, but organic). We all agreed that the dark chocolate didn't have the strong, bitter after taste we've found with other dark chocolate varieties. I preferred the dry roasted edamame & dried fruit & nut mix. I found the salmon to be too watered-down (I'm more of a chunky spread person). I couldn't taste the salmon enough over the chili-lime, but the children disagreed (they don't like chunks).

This ready-to-eat meal is nutritious, well packaged (brightly-colored wrapping, includes Sudoku grid in each box) and tasty. This is great for traveling in the car with my children, who usually want to stop off for fast food (it has the Lunchable-type appeal to kids). It is a bonus that we can eat out of the same box-less waste and I don't go hungry (also curbs my ravenous sugar cravings)!

As a health conscious mom, I am satisfied.

Summary: Tasty, but not enough food for the price
Text:
I pack a lunch every single day, because if I don't, I wind up begging someone to cover for me while I do the Burger King drive-thru. That's not good for my wallet or my arteries, so I was excited about this product. Wholesome and healthy? With a delicious sounding menu? Yum!

It really is made from natural ingredients, and it is as good as it sounds. I was a little worried that the salmon "spread" might be gross, but it wasn't, and it wasn't boring, either. The assortment of sides is nice, and they're all tasty, too, although I think the edamame could have used a little more salt.

However, it's not enough food for me for lunch, and I'm not a big eater. When I do the Burger King thing, I get a Whopper Jr and a value fry, and I never finish the fries. This is 410 calories if you eat every bite, and I think my optimum lunch intake is ~500 calories. Maybe if I paired it with soda or juice it would do the job, but I try hard to drink only water, so...I'd rather supplement it with other food. That kind of defeats the purpose though.

The other thing that will likely keep me from buying these after my Vine-supply runs out is just the price. $4 each isn't horrendous for a lunch, and it's worth the extra to me over a Whopper/fry meal, but it's a lot more than packing leftovers. I *might* buy a box to keep in my desk for emergencies -- and for that purpose, the size would probably be fine -- but it's unlikely that I'll start eating them every day.

i know they call these meals on the go and I think these are great snack items to have around or keep when you are going to need a quick and easy meal.  I've tried these before and liked but this is my first time with the salmon.  I love salmon and cook it frequently or eat canned salmon when I want a quick snack.  However, the salmon was the one thing I just didn't like so much.  It is very tangy and very fishy at the same time.  I make orange and lemon salmon all the time but this was just nothing like that in its flavor.  It's hard to describe but I think you would like if you like a spicy fishy tangy combination.  Everything else in there was very tasty.  Even the edamame wasn't so bad.  If you remember you are eating a healthier replacement for peanuts, they really start to taste like them.  The chocolate, crackers and fruit and nut mix were all good.  I just didn't like the chili lime salmon so much.

I wasn't surprised that the dry roasted edamame tasted like salty dust. That's what a handful of dry roasted edamame tastes like.

The ginger flavored peanuts completely overwhelmed what would otherwise have been a nice blend of dried fruit. The best that can be said is that it was edible.

Onward, and hopfully upward, to the "main dish:"

I could not finish the 1.6 ounces (I repeat: 1.6 ounces) of chili-lime salmon. It all tasted, in the immortal words of Elaine Benes, "Fake! Fake! Fake!"

The LateJuly Organic Classic Rich crackers were excellent. Really.

The Terra Nostra Organic Robust Dark 60% Cacao was rock hard and resisted melting in the mouth. I adore dark chocolate, but not this.

"Just add a drink and chow down," reads the back of the box. Better make that the strongest you have around.

I suppose if you need something for an emergency kit or are going for a long hike and need supplies you could toss a couple of these in.  But for me it would have to be a long hike.  Like to another country,

Summary: The Salmon is mushy and FISHY
Text: I'm not a fan of the salmon in this box.  I almost gagged.  Super fishy and no chunks of meat here, just soupy gruel.  The ginger /lime flavoring was nice but not enough to cover that seriously awful salmon.  Gross.  If you like fishy, it's all yours.  A matter of taste I guess.

I liked the idea of a "grab and go" type lunch or snack, so decided to give this a try. However, it sat on the shelf for over a month before actually giving it a go - I was nervous that I wouldn't like it, so kept putting it off (it was the only flavor available when I decided to give it a try). Well, my worry was founded, as I did not care for it at all.

The Salmon spread was SUPER FISHY. I love Salmon, and the fresher it is the lighter, more delicate the taste. This hits you over the head with fishiness. The crackers were your basic ritz type crackers and were as expected. There was a granola-ish mix of fruits and nuts that was okay, but seemed sugar sweetened. The dried edamame were indeed dry and not very flavorful. All in all the best item was the little chocolate squares for dessert, but even that wasn't anything I'd purposely seek out when shopping.

Perhaps the other GoPicnic meals are better and I was just turned off by the fishiness of this one. I would consider trying a different flavor before completely writing off these little meal packs, and suggest that anyone else considering these meals does so as well (unless you like a strong, fishy taste...)

Summary: Great idea, Salmon is super-fishy - try a different flavor meal pack if considering GoPicnic, or just pass it up all together.

I brought this ready-to-eat meal to work with me yesterday for lunch. I'm not sure what I was expecting, but this wasn't it. Nothing was really terrible, rotten, or all that off-putting. It just wasn't good. My friend and I had joked while waiting for this to arrive that it was an "adult lunchable". If you've never had a lunchable, the idea is a little packet of ingredients the kid can put together in his own way, e.g. pizza or cracker sandwiches. They were always very bland and the idea sounded better than it actually tasted. These ended up being exactly the same way.
The Late July crackers are tasty (similar to a Ritz), and the salmon spread is alright. I did eat most of it, so it must have been somewhat appealing, though I couldn't tell you how. It was VERY fishy, which I don't mind, though others might.
The dry roasted edamame beans are so bland, I can't imagine eating them in any other capacity. Just pure salt and not much other flavor. A bit like eating those styrofoam packing peanuts.
The fruit and nut mixture was pretty good, though the number of banana chips was disappointingly low (two in the whole bag). The ginger peanuts were a strange new taste that I couldn't quite get into, but they were tasty.
By the time I got to the chocolate I was tired of trying these strangely bland foods. It's dark chocolate. Not much you can screw up there.
If you're in a hurry or if you're trying to get your kid to eat better (whole box is 410 calories), these are decent in a pinch. But I'd rather take the extra time to prep my own lunch, or hell, have a lean cuisine.

Summary: Airplane food for half the price
Text:
I was pleasantly surprised by this little meal in a box. It reminds me of the snack boxes the airlines are selling in place of complimentary frozen entrees these days. Every items comes individually wrapped with a little fork, but surprisingly no napkins for messy eaters. However, the airlines would charge $8 or more for this selection.

The chili lime salmon spread was surprisingly good. The appearance is initially off-putting (it looks just like the picture on the box) and there is a fishy odor, which your airplane seat mates might not appreciate. (Though last time I flew United they were offering a tuna box which was also stinky). The chili does give the salmon a little kick. The crackers were good, though I wish they had provided 8 instead of 6 as 5 as not sufficient for the size of the salmon spread serving.

The dried roasted edamame was so-so. Edible, but it won't replace Cheetos as my favorite crunchy snack.

The ginger fruit and nut mix was very gingery. It has bananas in it and I accidently ate one - I don't like bananas. Other than the bananas the seasoning was good - I nice blend of sweet and salty, with emphasis on the sweet.

Also included is a chocolate square. You can't go wrong with chocolate!

Grab one of these things before you head to the airport next time. Hopefully since everything is sealed TSA will let it through - there are no plastic knives in this package.

Summary: Healthy meal, but a little lacking in taste
Text:
The GoPicnic salmon and crackers, a reasonably-priced meal, is the perfect choice for those looking to watch their calorie intake while eating healthy as well. The salmon was a bit salty, but that was likely due to the preservatives. The dried beans were a little bland as well, but would, by themselves, be a perfect snack. The fruit and nut trail mix was very tasty and among the best pre-packaged trail mix I've had. The cocoa bar wasn't my favorite, but I'm not generally a fan of chocolate-type snacks. However, my wife who does like chocolate really enjoyed the bar.

Overall, this ready-to-eat meal is a healthy meal for the cost-conscious consumer.

GOPICNIC is a complete picnic in a box, great for lunches on the go, at a lecture or in the park, during those hot summer afternoons when you dont feel like a big meal, and want to get some sun before lunch hour ends. Also, these wouldnt be bad for camping, or throwing a few in the car for those long vacation trips, when you dont know WHERE you might find a healthy meal on the road. So, whats in the BOX? Chemically, 410 calories (16g fat, 48g carb, 22g protein, with 660mg sodium)that gives you a nice size meal. Add grape juice, or green ice tea, and you're good to go. The CENTERPIECE of the culinary experience is the SALMON SPREAD in a chili lime sauce. ITs not hot, but there is just enough of a bite, in that hot/sour S.E.Asian way, to give the salmon a unusual, complex taste. The GOPICNIC box includes a small plastic fork, to get all the salmon spread out of the container. Also included are buttery wheat "organic" crackers, that dont clash with the salmon taste. (That sauce is remarkable, and literally changes the overtone of the salmon, into elegant seafood cruisine.) Also, you get 1 oz of dry roasted Edamame, which are soybeans. But dont think of those little dried soybeans found in many "trail" mixes, that are so hard you can break a tooth on them. No, the Edamame has the soya protein content, but they're green, fingernail sized, providing a crunchy, but not hard texture. They're very lightly salted. Also, there is this "GINGER ZIP" fruit and nut mix, that compliments the "asian" taste of the salmon sauce, and the Edamame. ALSO, you get a little sweet for desert--a square of dark chocolate, the kind that has all the health benefits. Not a bad picnic lunch at all.

Summary: An adult, Foodie-worthy step up from the tuna lunch kits out there!
Text:
I'm a regular consumer of Starkist's Chunk Light Tuna Lunch Kits. There's always at least one to three of them sitting in my desk drawer at work. I love the crackers that are packaged with those kits, as well as the individual pouches of condiments that can either be added or omitted from your chosen mixture. But those kits, while about half of the price of these, pale in comparison to this kit, if you're looking for something more adult, more elegant, and more Foodie-friendly.

GoPicnic's Salmon + Crackers ready to eat meal comes very smartly packaged, with a small, eco-friendly cardboard box that can be closed securely, with a tab that actually, really stays in place and keeps it closed. The box is rife with information and entertainment, from food product blurbs to fun games meant for adults, as opposed to kids.

Also highly adult-friendly are the extra little snacks and treats enclosed with the main dish of salmon "salad" and Ritz-type crackers. The snack mix containing the ginger-glazed peanuts, dried cranberries, and banana chips is sweet, crunchy, and chewy all at once. It's a small pouch of snack mix, and the peanuts ARE rather sweet, but being a BIG fan of ginger, I loved the spicy bite of ginger, and how well they paired with the banana chips and dried cranberries. Definitely a step up from other trail mixes, and delicious. The dry-roasted Edamame are DEFINITELY dry (be sure to keep some sort of drink on hand if you plan to eat these in one sitting - you'll NEED some liquid to choke these all down!), but very tasty, and pretty filling. They hit the spot if you're craving a lightly salted, crunchy, nutty treat, but just remember that they ARE dry!

As for the salmon spread itself, don't expect yours to look like what's pictured on the box. At least, mine didn't. It was more of a salmon salad puree' with a few cursory chunks of salmon thrown in to remind you that it really did come from an actual fish. Taste-wise, it was very tasty to me, but DID need the crackers to cut the strong flavor. Salmon DOES have a stronger flavor than tuna salad, which I was aware of already, but I enjoy canned and fresh salmon both, so it wasn't terribly off-putting to me. There was a subtle hint of lime, and the spice of the chili perked it up just enough for me, so overall, the flavors combined well, but I felt compelled to eat the salmon mixture on the Ritz-type crackers, whose buttery, flaky taste were a perfect complement. As for the crackers themselves, they were as good as I'd hoped they'd be, and even better than the ones I've come to enjoy so much from the Starkist tuna lunch kits (an unrelated product, but similar). There were enough of them to get me through the small tray of salmon salad from start to finish, and they smoothed out the more distinctive taste of the salmon salad. For me, it really didn't matter whether they were organic or not, but it's a thoughtful consideration for GoPicnic to have made for their potential customers that WOULD have taken issue with it. The one thing that I think GoPicnic SHOULD swap out here, though, is the plastic fork that came enclosed in my kit - a plastic knife would've been much more helpful, but its omission wasn't a deal-breaker for me.

Not being a huge chocolate fan on average, and one who avoids dark chocolate in general, I was very pleasantly surprised by the smooth taste of the dark chocolate square included in this kit. I've grown to expect dark chocolate to be bitter, and this square was not. It had a great snap and crunchy bite, was just sweet enough, and was deliciously smooth and creamy, so I was very, very pleased with it. I can see why the chocolate square enclosed in this kit got rated as the best-tasting organic dark chocolate out there. It was really very, very good.

Overall, I found this lunch kit to be more than adequate for me as a lunch option, as opposed to simply a snack. With all of the different components in it, all of the small- to medium-sized portions of items added up to, for me, a very filling lunch. The price is a little higher than I'm used to for my fish salad lunch kits, but the product that you get is definitely worth it. It's a step up all around from what I'd grown accustomed to, and had everything in that small box that I believe most people would want.

A delicious product for a good price. High quality ingredients, and plenty of sweet and salty treats to satisfy all around! Good stuff!

These little snack boxes are cool -- the treats inside are tasty and healthier than many common snack foods and, at around four bucks per box, they're not TOO much more expensive.

I previously reviewed a GoPicnic 'care package' which was a much larger box full of a variety of delicious snacks... so I expected the snacks in this little meal box to be similarly tasty --

- Chili Lime Salmon Spread: this was pretty good... fairly light-textured and easy to spread. There was enough to cover my...

- Organic Crackers: honestly, these tasted like generic Ritz. I like Ritz crackers, so this is a good thing.

- Fruit & nut mis: this was good... wish it was larger.

- Dry Roasted edamame: this was my personal favorite in the snack box. Sometimes, with dry roasted edamame, I've experienced dryness and/or hardening of the skin-like outer layer of the edamame beans which makes them tough to eat. The edamame in this package didn't have this problem. I'd actually say they were the best dry-roasted edamame I've had.

- Chocolate Square -- this was good... not outstanding, just a nice little square of dark (pretty dark!) chocolate.

Bottom line -- I think this is a fun and tasty snack box. At 4 bucks, it's not that cheap... but for the quality of components and the supposed healthiness/'all-natural' variety within, I think it's a good choice for health-conscious parents or office workers.

Summary: A tasty and protein filled treat
Text: This is something that you can eat on the run that frees you from eating protein bars or shakes when you can't sit down for a meal. I was happily surprised by the taste and will be buying more in the future.

Wow, this is a delicious light meal or a heavy snack. The products are all high quality and tend toward organic healthier products. The ginger nut/fruit snack was the best mix of that type I've had. The salmon spread was delicious and not too fishy, and I appreciated the fact it had no mayo or icky products added. The crackers are like a ritz cracker but an organic version. Paradise again has come to my rescue. This product saves time and is of very good quality, I have used their products for many years and have never been dissapointed with the fruit cakes made with them

This product met and exceeded my expectations! It contained an outstanding mix of fruit and  wonderful looking cherries. Upon opening, the aroma was fragrant and the mix was extremely fresh. The cookies baked using the product were moist and flavorful. Will I purchase this again - without a doubt! Outstanding!!

Summary: Good price and taste, healthy snack with fiber
Text:
I enjoy one of these bars per day as a mid-morning snack. The chocolate satisfies any sweet cravings and the extra fiber makes up for breakfast which often doesn't provide enough. As the box warns, do not consume in excess to avoid consuming too much fiber.

Subscribe and save makes the price very reasonable and convenient.

Summary: Good tasting source of fiber Best place to purchase
Text:
I want to preface this review by saying these are not "health food" however they are still the best commercial bar of their type.

These are the best tasting fiber bars I have tried. Better than the Fiber One bars. Perhaps because these use real chocolate instead of Chikory Root. These bars are also a bit less chewy than Fiber One, something I prefer. If one really needs to increase their fiber 35% of the daily value in each bar is a good amount for the size of the bar. Tasting as good as they do also make it an easy way to do so especially with all the chocolate they are much like a candy bar with fiber. These are my favorite bars of their type. Amazon has had the best consistent pricing on these vs local stores. If you subscribed to have them delivered every month or two or three, it is your choice, you get an additional 15% discount which is obviously the way to go. Do watch though as prices may fluctuate and you may find that the deal on the 5 pack version is priced lower or vice versa the 10 pack may be priced lower as is currently the case, however it is for exactly the same number of bars. I simply add the seeds to a healthy smoothie or oatmeal which are a major part of my daily diet.

Being from Ny the onions in red sauce were iwelcomed in NC I love them and will definetly order more in the future

Summary: Even at cheap, you don't get what you expect.
Text:

It works well, I don't sweat as much, but the dispenser it comes in "leaks". How to I describe this... I can't even find a link on Dove's website to ask if I am doing something wrong.

It is in my bathroom, not exposed to sun, or extreme heat or cold. If it didn't leak, I would give it 4 stars, but because of it, only 3 stars. I would give it 5 starts if it wasn't so pricey compared to regular, scented sticks.

The good thing about this is that it works as a really good moisturizer and the smell is weak and pleasant.

Summary: NOT worth the money..make your own!
Text:
We were given this product as a gift. OK, I can forgive the fact that I'm a pastry chef and I was given a MIX for a gift :-0 but I have always made my own frosting from scratch and have for years. It's one of the EASIEST things to make!!! Make your cake from a mix if you want but....I looked at the back of this box to see what was in it and...SERIOUSLY it's just powdered sugar (.80 cents worth), salt (.05 cents worth) and vanilla (maybe 20 cents worth). I mean, I 'm glad that this small company is making themselves some money but really you should spend your money on other more difficult to make items. (Or all the medical bills that come along with the issues of gluten allergy.)

Honestly folks here is all you do for AWESOME frosting:
1 box (16 oz) of powdered sugar (put it in a bowl)
1 pinch salt (put it in the bowl
1 teaspoon vanilla (in the bowl)
1 Cup margarine (at room temp,in the bowl)
4 TBL soy milk or other milk (in the bowl)
Mix it all up with a mixer till it is light and fluffy (about 5 minutes)
...if you want chocolate add 4 tbl of cocoa powder and another tbl of milk

Summary: Kashi Heart to Heart pack of 12
Text: This is a great product.  The cereal tastes great, and has good nutritional value.  I used to order the "crunch" cereal also by Kashi, until I noticed the amount of sugar in each serving.  It was way too high.  But the Heart to Heart cereal does not have way too much sugar, and it does still have fiber and even protein.  I like the fact that I can pour milk directly into the package.  I paid somewhere around $12 for a package of 12, and received free shipping with my Prime membership.

This tastes about the same as Quaker oats cereal. You get 12 cups for $11.90 which is just about a $1 a cup. It's a decent portion. Each cup is a little smaller than the size of a coffee cup (1.4 ounces). If you're watching your weight, it has 140 calories in each cup. The sodium content is 100 mg which is not bad. It also has some (not all) essential nutrients such as calcium and vitamin A. It can also be used as a snack at any time or as a breakfast cereal.

The only problem with this cereal is the dull taste. To me it's bitter. Oats to me does not have a pleasant taste. To fix this I add cinnamon, a few slices of a banana and a packet of stevia (a low calorie sweetener). Sometimes I even add a little honey and mix it in with a small amount of skim milk. If this had been done already I would have given this a higher rating. For the price Kashi should have considered making their cereal more tasty. Summary: Ok, it works, but the important thing is WHY it works
Text:
SUMMARY:
Ok so this is a long review, but the short summary is that although i regularly consume 5-Hour energy i do so with the knowledge that the effect i am feeling is mostly from the caffeine, and this effect is the same as caffeine consumption in coffee form, this also includes the "crash" later. The vitamin-B's added have as far as i have been able to find very little evidence supporting any effect, and at large doses some are toxic. I buy it in general because of the convenience of the concentrated form, and the fact that it is not calorie laden to the extreme (a la Starbucks). That said i could not find any evidence suggesting that 5-hour energy has any effects which makes it preferable to coffee
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Let me start out by saying that i am an avid 5 hour energy drinker. As a university student i go through at least a few every time a major exam week is coming up. Being a Psychology student with a focus on Neuroscience i decided to actually have a look at the contents of 5-Hr and and the scientific basis which merits its inclusion in the energy drink. Drugs that affect the body are intrinsically very complicated with many different effects on different parts of the body, so this is not a complete picture and will often be a very simplified one, but i think it will do for our purposes here.

Caffeine:
5 hour energy contains caffeine, this i am sure comes as no surprise to anyone. What might be a surprise is that caffeine is a drug, this only means that it has a physiological effect on the body, but it is important for several reasons. One is that there is quite a lot of evidence for the buildup of both addiction and tolerance to caffeine, most people that regularly consume caffeine do build up tolerance, requiring larger consumption for the same effect .Without getting too technical caffeine works by effecting receptors on cells called "neurons", caffeine is what is called a "direct antagonist" to adenosine receptors. That means caffeine inhibits neurons from reacting to adenosine (it sort of works like a "cap" on top of the receptors stopping adenosine from attaching there). this inhibitory effect "increases" cerebral (brain) blood flow, as well as decrease the effects of adenosine on the brain, adenosine builds up in the body over an entire day, and seems to play an important part in promoting sleepiness. By blocking these receptors caffeine temporarily reduces the feeling of being tired. It does however in no way reduce the need to sleep overall, as adenosine is still building up in the body even when you have consumed the caffeine. It is like being under water, caffeine can act as a "air bubble" isolating us from the water for while, but once the air is used up you still need to deal with the water, in the case of adenosine, this means sleeping.

The "crash" after caffeine consumption is simply the neurons again being affected by adenosine, so you are now feeling how tired the body really is, as caffeine has built up while you have been under the influence, the subjective experience is from a higher high then you were before to a lower low. The importance of this is that as far as i know there is NO WAY to remove this effect, unless more caffeine is consumed. As such the claim that there is "no crash later" sounds very disingenuous to me. There is also conflicting evidence as to whether or not caffeine improves mental alertness or just increases cognition in addicts back to a non-addict baseline, however as far as i know there is no consensus in either direction, and i am not willing to spend hours interpreting the papers dealing with this issue.

Various vitamin B:
There is a lot of misconceptions out there as to what vitamins actually are. Vitamins are defined as any organic compound needed in tiny amounts that the body needs, but does not produce. So by definition we need Vitamin B, however that does not mean taking lots of them is good for you. Its a bit like saying "well the body needs carbohydrates to survive, so the more i eat the healthier i will get". So the question is not if vitamin B are effective (they are) but if they have an effect in large doses. Virtually everyone gets all the vitamin B the body needs, the one exception is usually pregnant women and vitamin B9.In general there is little to no evidence of positive effects on cognition or attention after consumption of any vitamin B, vitamin B is liquid soluble so most of it simply passes right through the body. The one *possible* exception is that there are some exploratory studies finding that vitamin B6 consumption in children with ADHD leads to better attentiveness and cognition. However these studies (at least the ones i was able to find) are generally small (30-50 participants) and thus unreliable. Even if there was a link this would most likely be linked to a specific deficit in people with ADHD, not the population as a whole. I also found several meta-analyses (papers reviewing other papers) that suggested no link between vitamin B6 (or B12) and increased cognition or attention.

There is however a danger associated with some vitamin B's if consumed inappropriately. Overdosing on vitamin B6 and B3 is toxic to the body, so don't consume more than 2/day (recommended max from 5-hr themselves) for extended periods of time, it is well documented that vitamin B3 overdosing is associated liver damage in large quantities, while vitamin B6 is associated with nerve damage at high quantities the FDA sets their upper daily limit at 100mg which is roughly 70 times their recommended dosage, a bottle has 40mg B6 so you can do the math from there.

Energy Blend:
So this is the shortest section because there is not really a lot to say, Glucuronic acid is sometimes used for more effective delivery of drugs, but doubtful that that is effective here. The much touted Taurine is also a non-story with the EFSA (think european FDA) stating that there is no effect positive or negative from the levels presented in energy drinks. at least one study suggests Citicoline might have some positive effect on memory in people with dementia, but i was unable to find a study which dealt with a healthy population.

So why do i continue to consume 5-Hour? even though the vitamin B has little proven effect, the caffeine does, in the sense that it acts the way one would expect it to. I consume it because it is more convenient to bring around then coffee, is consumed faster, and tastes quite good (in my opinion), and at $1.70 a bottle, its cheaper than Starbucks and far less unhealthy.

I seldom review products here but I am sufficiently impressed with this product that I felt it deserved a little promotion. Normally I do not tend to lend much credence to and am skeptical of most natural supplements' claims, magic elixirs, and other products that I tend to lump into the classification of "snake oil" type products. For me, this product lives up to nearly all of its claims. I began taking these infrequently after a colleague at work recommended it. I'm in law enforcement and now keep a stock of these in my office and in my car. When you have to push through a really long day (or night) at work, these are wonderful to fall back on.
A lot of people who have reviewed this product attribute its effect mostly or completely to its caffeine content. No way... That may be true for people who have a high sensitivity to caffeine, but I drink coffee like water and have a substantial resistance to the effects of caffeine as a result. The caffeine content in one bottle of Five Hour Energy supposedly equates to one small cup of coffee. I can tell you that its effect on me is much more substantial than the effect of a small cup of coffee and arrives with far fewer negative effects (ahem... like a trip to the restroom that often follows morning coffee..). Within 4-5 minutes of drinking a bottle, I always feel noticeably energized, alert, mentally sharper, and physically stronger (endurance wise). I have only felt "overly stimulated" on one occasion and this was early one morning after having already drank a LOT of coffee. On that occasion, I think the caffeine in the FHE simply pushed me over the limit. Other than this one occasion, I have never felt "jittery" after having taken one. For me it is normally only really effective for 3-4 hours, not a full five hours.
I have experienced Niacin "flush" on one occasion after having taken one, however, I also take a large dose of Niacin every morning (the only other natural supplement I take regularly) and I again think the Niacin in the FHE simply took me over the limit in combination with my daily Niacin dose. For those of you unfamiliar with the sensation of "Niacin flush" it can be a little intense the first time but is completely harmless and will pass after 5-6 minutes. Kind of a combination of an intense all over hot-flash/sunburn. Don't panic, even though the sensation can be somewhat intense, and it will pass quickly if you happen to experience one from the Niacin in an FHE dose.
Since there is a bit of a history of low B-12 levels in my family, I have always suspected FHE's rather large B-12 content may be one reason it works so well for me. I have no objective evidence that this is the case, however, I know the minimal caffeine content present would simply not have much effect on me. All in all, I love this product, see no risky or questionable ingredients in it that concern me, and find it a very nice and effective alternative to swilling down coffee to push through a long day or night. Give it a try sometime when you are dragging. I think you'll be pleasantly pleased unless you are unusually sensitive to caffeine.
