Since I have been using Blue Buffalo Wilderness I have noticed a reduced amount of waste and smell in the litter box from my cats.  They seem to be much happier.  Plus, my Siamese mix was showing signs of the onset of kidney failure which he no longer has.  Thanks BLUE BUFFALO, WE LOVE YOU.

I have had cats all my life and currently have five plus a feral cat I feed. This is the best dry cat food I have found. But there was a significant problem ordering it from Amazon. I have Amazon prime and always use it whenever possible. This time, a few days after I ordered it, I was told I couldn't get it.

Summary: NOT 100% GRAIN FREE. Much cheaper at Petsmart
Text:
I originally accidently wrote the following review for the Wilderness INDOOR chicken formula as opposed to the regular version of this Amazon listing. Upon further inspection I realize that this particular product IS NOT grain free as it contains oatmeal. I actually use their Wilderness Indoor formula and it is indeed 100% grain free.

I am therefore demoting my rating to 3 stars as, while this is still a good food, the claim that it is grain free is just plain false.

"I'm not sure why this is listed as $60 on Amazon. The MSRP is around $35, a price you can fetch at Petsmart or Petco.

Anyway, this food is great! My two cats love it. They have excellent coats and have maintained a healthy weight for years with this food.

I switch back and forth between this and Blue Buffalo Freedom depending on sale prices as they are the same thing except that Wilderness has added salmon."

I love this food. I was so happy to find a food that was 40% protein. The grain-free food I had been using was 50% protein. I was concerned that might be a little high for my less active cats. I am  totally comfortable with Wilderness. My next concern, though, was that one of my cats was sometimes constipated. No grains ~ no oats ... I was told it is better to deal with feline constipation using food over laxatives or petroleum-based products. I was at a loss, but now Blue Buffalo has come out with a Wilderness grain-free formula that has added dried cellulose, which is a natural fiber. It has 5% fiber content. It also has slightly lower caloric content than the regular Wilderness. I can't wait to try it!! My cats absolutely love Wilderness!

Summary: Tasty but a little TOO tasty
Text:
I bought this because PetSmart were out of Innova at the time. Normally I buy Innova for senior cats and for weight control and mix them together. I have a 9 year old skinny kitty and a 6 year old chubby kitty. I've noticed as soon as I switched to Buffalo Wilderness (mixing Chicken and Weight Control now) their bowls empty significantly faster. That means they're packing away more calories, which is NOT good for the chubby kitty. I definitely plan to go back to Innova. My chubby cat was eating much less (getting fuller faster).

Nevertheless, they both do love it. Must be delicious to little cat taste buds!

I recently switched my cat Charlie (a little under a year) to this stuff from another type of Blue Buffalo dry food. He is not clawing his way to the food, but he took to it just fine. His coat is soft and shiny and he rarely gets gas. I can't say his business smells any more pleasant, but I doubt there is any food to take care of that bit. I feel better feeding him this stuff, knowing that it is much better for him. He has a ton of energy (sometimes a bit too much) and seems to be a happy and healthy little fellow.

Summary: Blue Buffalo Wilderness is the best for cats
Text: My cat changed completely when he started eating wilderness--he is more relaxed and contented and his fur is beautiful,,,,  I like this product because it is mostly meat which is what cats need to eat....

I switched to no grain food several years ago when I realized my cat has a grain allergy. I have tried many brands and this one stands amongst the best. The added perks are it shipping for free for Amazon Prime members, this saves me a trip to the nearest pet food store that carries this type of food an hour and half away. I also use an automatic feeder and the kibble size is perfect. My cat is always excited for meal time!

This is the second bag of Blue Buffalo Grain Free Chicken Dry Cat Food I have purchased.  My cats all seem to like it just fine.  I really like the ingredient listing and believe it is one of the best I have found so far.

Summary: Yes, it's pricey, but WHAT a difference in my cats!
Text:
My 10-yr-old cats have had problems off and on all their lives with allergies. My female has had it the worst: she gets a rash on her tummy or inside her legs, then proceeds to lick it, causing terrible irritation/scabs. I was told by a vet that it was probably the cat litter I was using, so over the years, I've tried virtually EVERY unscented, natural, "organic" cat litter on the market with virtually no change. Hers cleared up a bit, then my male started getting the same thing. He also started losing weight and vomiting. Not good for a little (7-lb) kitty. Their food has always been a "premium" adult-formula cat food, which they seemed to like.

Finally, a breeder suggested I get them off grain-based cat food. I chose this Blue Buffalo variety because of the high protein content and what seemed to be a balance of the other ingredients.

Oh. my. The difference has been nothing short of miraculous. After three weeks on the new food, both seem to be rid of their allergies. Fred has gained some weight, and no longer upchucks every day. Both are full of energy and chase each other all over the house (remember, these are 10-yr-old cats!). Their coats are looking good, too.

I'm totally sold on this stuff. It costs a lot more than my previous food, but my kitties are so much healthier and happier that it's TOTALLY worth it.

I have two cats that both eat this food. I adopted each of them and switched them to grain-free food as soon as possible. My little one had very soft stools until he was put on a 100% grain-free diet. Both of their coats are incredibly soft, they aren't overweight and they are full of energy.  It is more expensive than other brands out there, but my cats' health is worth it to me, especially if it will help with possible health issues in the future. The vet is very happy with their health and my boys are very happy with their human.

Summary: Turns older cats into healthy, vibrant kittens!
Text:
I've been feeding my 2 cats cheap (whatever what was on sale at the supermarket) food for years. They were vomiting hairball-food mixtures all the time, and had dry, flaky skin. I didn't really take notice until the older cat had to have teeth pulled because of stomatitis. He was sluggish and had trouble chewing even after surgery. After searching, I learned that poor diet could be a factor. So, I decided to quit putting their health on the line and buy some quality food.

I had tried a few other brands, but they didn't want to eat any of them. This, however, they LOVED. Now ages 13 and 8, they are friskier than ever! They're coats are soft and shiny, their gums healthy, and they stopped vomiting (there's still an occasional hairball once in a while but very rarely).

The change in behavior and health is very noticeable, and I'm sure because of this food they will live a long healthy life. This is the only brand (and flavor) of dry food they eat now!

Summary: Blue Buffalo Wilderness Grain Free Dry Cat Food, Chicken Recipe
Text: My 6 month old male Tuxedo cat likes Blue Buffalo Wilderness Grain Free Dry Cat Food, Chicken Recipe, which is a round pellet shaped kibble.  Based on the stated ingredients and nutritional information, I award Blue Buffalo Wilderness Grain Free Dry Cat Food, Chicken Recipe "5 Stars."  The bag does not feature a resealable strip, which is a nice feature that some other kibble cat food bags have.

Summary: Cat liked it ok, but quality control issues
Text: I ordered this to help my cat's digestive issues and he seemed to like it.  However, I immediately stopped using it when I found pieces of string sticking out of several of the pellets.  Like the other reviewer who found rubber inside, it could just be a fluke, but I don't like taking chances and switched to the Organix (which my cat loves).

Summary: magic bullet for cat with digestive issues
Text: After 8 years and many vet consultations, diets, and lifestyle changes I finally found a food that my cat can digest -- I wish I'd found this product years ago. My cat has had diarrhea/soft stool, blood in stool, and elimination behavior issues for all 8 years that have made me think she is in serious discomfort -- kitty colitis or the like. The stink this cat used to create was also the foulest odor ever to waft past my nostrils. Vets have largely dismissed my concerns about this (small animal vets have earned about as much of my respect as dentists or auto mechanics -- good luck finding a decent one among the lazy, greedy, or just plain incompetent). I've fed Royal Canin products at vet recommendation (cat hated it and no digestive benefit), as well as Taste of the Wild and Chicken Soup for the Cat Lover's Soul on friends' recommendations, all with zero improvement. Then I moved cross country and could not find these brands at the local store. Picked up the pricey Blue Buffalo wildernes food on a whim and voila -- cat is producing truly solid waste, seems to be able to use the litterbox without discomfort, and has reduced the poop odor by ~90%. She also simply seems to like the taste. The price is outrageous, but it's worth it to have her comfortable and to have a house that doesn't smell like the putrid waste of the devil himself whenever the cat takes a crap. Not being awakened in the middle of the night by eye-wateringly fetid odors wafting from the bathroom, demanding immediate litter scooping, is truly priceless.

Summary: waaaait a minute: OATmeal is GRAIN!
Text: I have a diabetic cat, and I really need to feed him low low or no carbs. He likes this and his sugar's good and he's as healthy as can be expected on insulin, but I feel a bit deceived they are calling it "grain free" then listing oatmeal as an ingredient.

We first bought Blue Buffalo when trying to find an alternative to prescription cat food that has fillers in it. Our older cat has had a lot of problems with weight gain and UTI issues. After Science Diet, and Rx, we wanted to give a more natural cat food a chance. This worked wonders!

Our 7 year old cat, Isabel, eats some of the Blue Buffalo chicken mixed in with her wet food every day. Her coat is starting to look healthy again with her dandruff going away, her chronic UTI has cleared up, she is beginning to lose a little weight, and she is more active than she has been in the last two years. For the last 12 months, she was becoming more and more lethargic, to the point that we were worried she had a serious illness. Now she chases our younger cat, plays with balls, and is generally in a much happier mood. She is even starting to jump on top of the washing machine to steal her 'sister's' food, whereas a few months ago she could only jump on the couch after a few starter jumps. She also eats less without begging for more food, I think the higher protein is doing a good job of keeping her feeling full.

Our younger cat is much pickier than Isabel, and she LOVES this food! I love having a cat food that both of my cats can enjoy and that does not contain corn, wheat, or soy. I take away one star for price, Amazon is not always the cheapest place to buy it.

I noticed the description on Amazon does not have the Nutrition information. From the side of my bag:

3,682 Kcals/kg, 391 Kcals/cup

I have to agree with most of the other reviews - this cat food is amazing. I have one cat who had digestive issues her whole life, and I figured that was just the way she was. I was feeding her Natural Balance. Ever since I switched to this food a couple years ago, all her issues completely disappeared. It's quite amazing, and definitely worth the price premium.

Summary: Best cat food on the market!
Text:
I have a 14 yr old, 2 yr old and a 7 yr old cats and we were feeding them Iams, Purina... one of those big name cat food brands. However, when we moved to a new location we came across this brand and I instantly fell in love. All you really need to do it read the ingredients in the back. Practically, everything that you would see a cat eat in the wild is in the food. There is real meat and fish in there, blueberries, cranberries and vegetables as well. I noticed a HUGE change in my cats. My oldest used to be real lethargic, always laying around sleeping, taking a few practice jumps before jumping up on the couch. Not to mention she had very bad dandruff. She's a tortoise shell and you could clearly see the dandruff without being right on top of her. Once I switched to Blue Buffalo, she got a little pep in her step. Now I find her running around the house like a bat out of hell and neither of my other two cats know what the heck is going on. Her coat is also nice, shiny and dandruff free. I never knew how much of a difference the change in food could be for her. Now she jumps up on the couch and bed (which is higher up) with ease and is even initiating play with my other two cats. She was the one cat that I'd noticed a dramatic change in. I highly recommend this brand to everyone. It gave me my childhood friend back.

It may be more expensive than your average cat food but it is well worth it in the end. I have found no problem with my cats not liking this food. All three of them gobble up the food in their bowls as if they were rottweilers.

*I recently had to switch to a low protein diet due to my eldest developing kidney disease. Within a month of switching foods she reverted back to having horrible dandruff. Aside from switching away from Blue Buffalo nothing in her diet/environment has changed. So this food really does help with dandruff.

It's true what they say about the super high protein food.  Without all the grain fillers, the cats don't need to eat as much to be satiated and to get the energy they need.  This food is more expensive, but it lasts a lot longer than the junk they sell in most stores.  And I've definitely noticed an increase in energy level in one of my cats.  I'm convinced this is a better quality nutrition and worth the extra money.  We've been feeding them this for the last year and I don't expect I'll ever switch to anything else.

Quality product as one of the best.  The 2012 price increase is not too welcome as I have been ordering also from petfood.com for $38.98 with tax/shipping.  I recommend this cat food to anyone who wants one of the best products on the market.

Summary: Works well for Sensitive Stomach Cats
Text: I have tried many brands of grain-free food for my Abyssinian and so far this is the best for her sensitive stomach. She is supposed to eat grain-free and fish-free, and the first time I received this item I noted that fish meal was the fifth ingredient, but had not been cited in the Amazon description. I tried it anyway, and it has proven to be the best food so far. Both of my cats like it.

Summary: This stuff didn't work for our cat
Text: I have no doubt this product contains quality ingredients, and for many cats it might be a key to good health and nutrition. We were looking for a high-quality grain-free food, and our cat wasn't able to digest this well at all. She seemed to like the taste of it just fine, certainly never ate less of it than other foods, but it gave her diarrhea which persisted even when we cut the food down to a 50/50 mix with her old food. As soon as we switched her to a different food, a more conventional healthy weight loss formula, the problem went away immediately. I don't mean to imply this will happen with every cat, and I can see there are many good reviews here (which is why we tried it, despite the price being quite a bit higher than our usual cat food), but I thought I should mention our cat's strong reaction. If your cat is sometime "iffy" with new foods, you might consider purchasing a smaller quantity of this first to make sure they can digest it OK.

Blue Buffalo has a long standing reputation for making top quality dog and cat food, and this product is no exception. While it is pricey, it is worth every penny. I noticed a much improved coat, among other things, on my cat after switching her to this food. One very important thing to note on this food, is that is grain free. Grain free is much higher quality food as grains for dogs and cats are not in their "normal" diet. The different flavors also make a big difference, so try different ones and see what your cat likes best!

Summary: Blue Buffalo Wilderness Grain Free Dry Cat Food, Chicken recipe
Text: My cat had been scratching herself constantly.  She doesn't have fleas or mites, just constant scratching.  Then I thought she might have allergies to her food.  I tried this product and have seen a dramatic reduction in the scratching and her course greasy looking coat is now so soft and fluffy.  It's only been three weeks but I can see a lot of difference.  It's a little pricey but the benefits to my cat are worth it.

My two cats just started their second bag of Blue Buffalo Wilderness Chicken dry food.  In the twenty years that I have owned cats, I have never seen cats so excited about dry food.  With other dry food they would eat a few bites and then walk away.  I would end up throwing away what they didn't eat after several hours.  With this food, they don't waste anything!  They usually eat their entire serving as soon as I feed them.  It must really taste good to them!  I'm very pleased with the ingredients and I've noticed how silky their coats are after starting this food.  This dry food and the Weruva canned food are definitely their favorites.  It's worth spending the extra money because nothing is going to waste.

Summary: No more throwing up or hairballs!
Text: What a relief! After almost a full bag between 2 cats, neither has thrown up since starting them on this food. I had started feeding them wet food around January because one of my cats had crystals in his UT. The vet recommended very expensive dry food (which was meant to make the cats very thirsty therefore would drink a lot of water which helps dissolve the crystals) Anyway, I "googled" the whole crystal thing and found that wet food can also help with crystals in the UT. For about 6 months they had nothing but wet food, and never drank a drop of water from their dish! I was amazed, and the crystals in the UT cleared up. Then, about 2 months ago they both started to throw up. I thought of a few different reasons, but could never come up with a conclusion. I had originally been feeding them Blue Buffalo dry food for many years, but not the Wilderness kind. I thought I'd check it out, read the reviews and found others had some success with this food and helped with not throwing up and hairballs. I AGREE!! The cats love this food, but they aren't that picky either. I'm ordering my 2nd bag today!
After we switched to blue, my cat's belly is gone. She is more energic! Blue is the only brand we buy now!

I love Blue Buffalo products, but my cats are not fond of it.

After reading articles about the awful ingredients and recalls on Fancy Feast products, I decided to make the switch to a healthier brand. We were already buying Blue Buffalo for dogs, and I know it is a very reputable brand so I thought my cats would love the Chicken flavored Cat Food. They don't. I even bought the wet food and they still will not eat it.

I think my cats were so used to eating unhealthy junk food that they don't realize good food when it's in front of them. Hopefully I can transition them slowly into liking it.

I gave the product 3 stars because I know this food is great, but my cats don't like eating it.

I felt that my 13 yr. old Siamese (Lester) with a sensitive stomach, sometimes overeating and throw-up problem would benefit from a new "Grain Free" kibble. After doing some research, I choose Blue Buffalo Wilderness over the Evo that I had been feeding for a few months (the Evo had major dust and I had to sift it before feeding..maybe 15-20% by volume). Towards the end of the second BBW bag I noticed that Lester (and my other cat) were not eating their normal amount and their litter box wasn't as full. Lester then was not cleaning up well after a #2, then in a couple of days stopped eating everything (even his daily wet food snack), we took him to a vet; blood work good, but x-rays show that he had large air bubbles in his stomach and upper GI. He couldn't eat anything without throwing it up..nothing. The vet made no suggestions other than keep trying to feed him; and it was only after going to Petco and talking with their staff did we take action with a syringe, baby food (beef), electrolyte, and a high protein cat paste all slurred and injected every hour that we got him recovering after a few days.

I can not be sure it was the BBW cat food that deteriorated Lester's health to very close to euthanizing, but I had not changed his wet food only his free choice kibble to Hill's Age Defying and he is back to normal now. The Hills has grain, but the kibbles are smaller and easier to digest and I am suspisious of Blue Buffalo Wilderness and/or maybe that an older cat's system can not handle very high protein dry kibbles. He was OK on Evo so makes me think that BBW was the problem.
Awesome, cats love it. :) Kinda high in potato though, but for the availability, it can't be beat. High protein and fat content, all three cats love it as part of their rotation.

Summary: Great variety means no picky eaters!
Text:
We discovered Earth's Best when my oldest started solids years ago. They had a more limited selection then, but offered more variety than the "regular" brands. For him, we only bought a few jars each trip, those flavors that we couldn't get in another brand. For our second child, we added a few more. With the 3rd baby, we started out on the larger brands, but he wouldn't eat them. Who can blame him!? They're runny and lacking any flavor. Not to mention, no matter how good sweet potatoes are, how many jars can you eat? He gobbles up every jar of Earth's Best without any problems. When we introduce a new flavor, he's all for it.

Text:

The Center for Science in the Public Interest evaluated popular brands of baby foods, including Gerbers, Heinz, Earth's Best and Beech-Nut. According to the Center's report, Earth's Best did not use starchy fillers or "replace real food with water and thickening agents in many of their products for children over six months of age. The brand offers single-ingredient, smooth foods for infants over four months; fruit, vegetable, grain and meat blends for babies over six months; and a variety of chunky soups, dinners and vegetable medleys for children over nine months old. They use quinoa and kamut flours. It is excellent all around.

I believe that the apricot puree that other's talked about in the sweet potato and chicken dinner is there to maintain the color of the food. I make my own sweet potato and chicken dinner for my little one and it turns brown. Summer vegetable: Water, organic corn, organic zucchini, organic green beans, organic brown rice, organic carrots, organic garbanzo beans, organic canola oil.

Rice and Lentil: Water, organic apples, organic carrots, organic brown rice, organic lentils, organic canola oil

The ingredient lists are all directly from the Earth Best's website, earthsbest.com, as I do not have the products in front of my right now.

Summary: Not a fan of BPA in baby food jar lids
Text:
As I have with all other Earth's Best jarred baby food, I won't be purchasing these Dinners for my baby because the jar lids contain BPA. I contacted Earth's Best's consumer relations dept. personally, and the representative read me a prepared statement saying that the epoxy resin that lines Earth's Best baby food jar lids contains "trace amounts" of BPA, but it "doesn't come into direct contact with the food." That kind of lukewarm response wasn't enough to put my concerns about BPA to rest ... after all, packaged food is jostled-around so much during shipping that these jars could spend days upside down, with the food resting directly on the jar lids. So I guess I'll have to pass on these jarred Dinners for now. (The Earth's Best rep did say that they were doing "accelerated testing" of BPA-free alternatives for lining their baby food jars).

This is such a shame, because Earth's Best is the only company that makes organic, pre-packaged Stage 2 complete meals (e.g., with meat/protein, veggies & carbs/starch) in PUREE form. All the other organic baby food manufacturers, such as Plum, Sprout, Ella's Kitchen, etc., only make Stage 3 meals, in chunky form. Earth's Best does make some baby food in BPA-free squeeze pouches, but that doesn't include its Dinner line. I was hoping to be able to expose my little-one to a wider variety of flavors and well-balanced meals while still at the puree stage. But I guess I'll have to wait until she's old enough for Stage 3 chunky meals, or make her baby food myself. (Virtually impossible for this super-busy and domestically-challenged mom, LOL!)

Text: Amy's Organic Soup is quite delicious. My husband & I are cutting back on sodium (extra salt) and so we tried this product, and we are very pleased with this soup. It has a rich tomato creamy flavor, and is great to have on had for a quick meal.

It would serve as a lovely base for chili or even pasta sauces.  But, I eat it "as is" at work for an affordable and low caloried lunch that fills me up!  I am on subscription for this because it is so good. I like it best of all the canned soups at any calorie or sodium level, so it is great that it is almost healthy!

Summary: A rare exception to canned food hell
Text:

This "light in sodium" version is already ridiculously tasty, so I'm not sure what more I'd get out of the regular version, other than excess salt. :)

Taste so fresh! The cream adds a nice base supporting a sweet and non-acidic flavor, yet this soup is not heavy!  Very light and works well with many dishes. I absolutely do not miss any extra salt, the flavor is perfect! Truly this soup stands up to anything in a can, only fresh tomatoes from your own garden could ever hope to compete.

This will be the best cream of tomato soup you'll ever have.

At one point he starved himself for over 3 days and would only eat grass or treats.

I told a local pet store clerk about how I had to start making homemade dog food because he would only eat "real" meat and none of the products we tried looked real. He asked if I had tried giving him WeRuVa because the meat looks like real human quality meat. He popped open a can and my dog inhaled all of it, licking the can totally clean. Summary: Get the original while it lasts
Text:
After the popularity of the Slim Jim waned in the years following revelations that the alleged "macho" of its celebrity endorser was merely spray-on tan, we endured a series of tasteless and unsnappable tinkerings to the original recipe.

Sadly, by the early days of this century, the original recipie had been lost. Even a team of scientists hired to reconstruct the glory of Slim Jims past failed in their efforts. We feared we would never see the likes of the "skinny james" of our youth.

Happily, a warehouse cellar of the original was located near Hoboken, NJ. How the store had gone missing more than 30 years ago is not known. But, like fine wine, these Slim Jims have only improved with age. Get yours before they're gone!

I found they were easier to eat if I took tiny bites.

That said, they were very tasty. But I don't like to fight my food, so I won't be buying this little stick any more.

Order these for me and the guys over here in Afghanistan. Got them quickly, and enjoyed them just as quick. Slim Jims are an essential for deployed soldiers. Thanks for the quick service and delicious treats.

My grandson ate just about all of them, I should have hid them.
They go great with beer. It's a good thing grandson is to young
to drink.

Summary: If you like Slim Jims and/or Tabasco, then these babies are fantastic. Hot, but delicious. A+!!!
Text:
This review is in reference to the 18 count pack of Tabasco flavored Monster Slim Jim's, although any size of the Tabasco Slim Jims are GREAT. (Slim Jim Giant Smoked Snacks, Tabasco, 0.97-Ounce Sticks (Pack of 24))

I love Tabasco sauce, and love the amazing synergy products they have made with other companies. So when I saw Tabasco Slim Jims, being a fan of Slim Jims anyway, I had to try them. The smaller sized ones, which I have been unable to find here on Amazon, taste great, but they are somewhat tougher than the larger versions, though not in a bad way. The medium sized and large ones, which this review is about, are much softer. Regardless, they are ALL delicious. They have the same spicy flavor that we Tabasco lovers have come to crave, but at the same time, since it was mixed in with other ingredients, it isn't so hot that you are forced to stop eating no matter how good it tastes. My friends and I all agree that it does have a high heat factor to it, and people who don't like spicy stuff might find it too much. But if you like spicy foods, these are an AMAZING snack. If you haven't tried them, then I highly recommend you get one from your grocery or convenient store. If you like them, buy them here since they are cheaper in bulk. Fans of Tabasco will not be disappointed. That's my $.02 on the matter folks.

Thanks you so much for your time folks.
Sincerely, R.A. McDowell
I use these sticks for people treats and dog rewards.  I show my dogs and have found that they love these jerky sticks.  The added benefit is that I can eat them, too while working with the dogs.

Summary: First batch was great, second batch was stale and old
Text:
this is the second time I have ordered these from the same seller (Amazon as it gives free shipping). The first time the slim jims were moist and plump and oily and you could tell they were fresh. This second batch was hard and dried out and not oily at all. For those who like slim jims you know what I mean about them being plump and oily as opposed to hard and dried out without much oil.

This is the ONLY place I can get the HOT ones so I was dissappointed with the second batch, while the first batch was perfect! I will continue to buy these but may see baout buying from a different seller to get fresher ones.
My husband love monster slim jims. Alot cheaper to buy it by packs then pieces. He ate 2 packs in a month, he is something but anyways I do recommend this to everyone. Great price for great products.
I have ordered this item several times and for once one of the boxes came opened and several items were missing before they were packaged for shipment.

Great product here, perfect combination of tabasco with the meat product.  For the size and quality this item cannot be beat, highly recommend this!  Ive bought a lot of Slim Jim and Jack products here, this was one of the best deals around!

I brought these a few times honestly and I even saw the Jax  on sale cheaper. Yes Jaxs are bigger and look tempting but thats all they are. This has the old school taste, the jacks taste more artificial then this. Even though Jax is cheaper. This tastes so much better.
Way beyond the tolerance level of people with "room temperature" palates, but if you like HOT!!!, then this flavor is the one to buy. I WILL be ordering more in the near future.

Well, it's as advertised, tabasco flavored double sized slim jim.

It's just not as great as some of the other flavors like sweet/hot, nacho, and so on. It's not even really that hot. They captured 80% of the flavor of tabasco, and none of the heat.
Generally, Slim Jims are great.  I love the taste of them and a little heat is good with them (Tabasco).  But these are all heat - and little of the Slim Jim taste.

Not very fresh....Experation date less than 2 months?
The experation is on each individual SlimJim so you can't check that until you open the box.
Each individual seemed different from the other. Some were tough and hard to chew and some were ok.
I'll probably buy at the store from now on.

Well, the 1 star reviews are from people who never liked Slim Jims and would never like Slim Jims so why they buy a whole package instead of spending a quarter for one at a gas station I'll never know... regardless, these are good and tasty.  Greasy?  Yes.  Bad for you?  Of course.  But you shouldn't expect anything but a fatty treat.  For some reason they seem tougher then they were a few years back when I had them last.  Not something I would eat daily, but a "good" treat if you like them.  With the sales lately amazon has had on them, the price is right as well.

These individually wrapped Slim Jims make great snacks for hungry kids.  Toss a few in your purse and you have a portable, filling treat while you're out with the kids.  My kids love them and ask for them over fruit snacks or candy.

I've loved Slim Jims since I was a kid in the 70s, and these are just the way I remember them - a little greasy, chewy, a little spicy. This box of 100 contains the small sized sticks - about 4 inches long, individually wrapped, and stored in a dispenser box. They don't have to be refrigerated, which makes them easy to tuck into a purse or lunch box.

These aren't the "spicy" flavor - I think you have to order the jalapeno or tabasco flavor to get those. But these are *slightly* spicy, chewy and delicious. Nobody eats Slim Jims because they're health food - they contain preservatives and low grade meats. But for a quick snack or if you just want something spicy, these are the same yummy snacks you'll remember from your childhood. They are also high protein and zero carbs, which is good for those who are dieting.

I've ordered this box three times and have been happy with it every time. Free shipping with Amazon's Supersaver Shipping makes it a good deal. And if you sign up for automatic delivery (no obligation to keep getting it past the first shipment) you will save an additional 15%, making each stick about 20 cents apiece.
I just got these items. They were as hard as the leather. And I could not return these items. Don't waste your money. They are trash.

The cost was no more than buying at a brick and mortar store and the product arrived with excellent freshness. The handy box they come in make for neat storage in the pantry. Not a downside to be had! I would definitely buy again.

Summary: This Will Put You In A COMA!
Text:
This hot sauce is not hot sauce... it is heat incarnate. I didn't even use a "bullet-spoon" serving, I just dipped the tip of a toothpick in the sauce and stirred it around in a plate of beans thinking it wouldn't really do anything. I was freaking wrong. This junk is by far the hottest sauce I've EVER tasted and I am a hot sauce junkie. Here are a few tips if you're going to use this stuff: 1) ALWAYS WASH YOUR HANDS AFTER HANDLING THIS PRODUCT!!! I learned the hard way. 2) Don't try to be a hero. There are serious health risks if you attempt to consume this product in large quantities. 3) If you are going to prank someone... make sure you don't go too far with it because this stuff is seriously painful even in small quantities.

If you think you can handle it... prepare for tears and a very abrupt halt to your ego-trip. This is the god of sauces and it commands you to respect it.

My dog has been eating California Natural dog food for the almost 6 years she has been with us and she seems to like it. It's easy on her stomach. She doesn't seem to get bored of the different flavors.

These are soo good!  I ordered them for my son's birthday party and the whole 5 pound bag was gone within a few days after the party--so good and you cannot just eat one!  I love the theme of them, too--you cannot find too many good dinosaur themed gummies out there.  These are THE BEST!

I have the most sensitive dogs. Both my Shepherds, Belgium and German, are quick to have diarrhea. I've tried Iams, Science Diet, Bill Jack, you name it we have tried it.
Finally, my breeder suggested the Nature's Variety dried dog food which left my dogs still a little inconsistent. Then, I found a store in town that carried the freeze-dried small bits. Wow! what a difference it has made. I add 5 nuggets, which are the size of a large cookie dough ball, to some Royal Canine German Shepherd dried dog food and Voila. We have not had ONE incident of diarrhea since. Venison and lamb are their favorites. They are also the perfect size to hide a pill. I highly recommend this product.

I have a pyranese and a pyr/wolf mix about 270 lbs of dog between the two and they get picky about their food.  I've tried to save money and feed them science diet or iams but especially my pyr she lost hair by the handfuls and her stool got runny. So I bit the bullet and went back to instinct. What a difference their hair is gorgeous, when we go out (my pyr is my service dog) she gets so much attention and people can't help but pet her she's so soft.  What I do is feed her the chicken instinct dry dog food and I sprinkle the freeze dried raw food on top in various flavors to keep them interested, and It's very handy to take with me when we are out and about as a snack, treat or a meal if we can't get home in time (I don't feed them "people" food at all because of their training) ...since both are large breeds there is the concern of bloat if they eat cheap or the wrong food, with instinct I don't worry about it at all, my vet says both are perfect weight and very healthy.  And another thing with instinct is that you need to feed your dog a lot less food because of the high quality, so this is not the food you want to free feed your dog or they will put on weight rather quickly....I love this stuff and more importantly my dogs (my right and left hand) love it too.

It also provides a great deep color for your sauces, chili, tacos, fajitas, etc. This is not an all-in-one chili seasoning as the other confused reviewer seemed to think. Add some onion, garlic, cumin and salt and it will cover that job very nicely. It is somewhere between mild and medium, heat wise and again, has a very nice flavor.

Be prepared to use it all in a year because the expiration date isn't more than that.

A peanut is a peanut, but hey, whatcha gonna do . . . eat more of these peanuts, of course.

This was one of those "oops" situations that can happen occasionally.

The package of three jars arrived, and seemed to have stains on the outer box. When I opened the box and saw the inner, bubble-wrapped package, I understood.

Two of the three jars had popped their lids, and the contents had leaked out. That had, apparently, happened long before the package was shipped, as there was mold growing all over the interior, on the leaking sauce, and on the jars. It was a mess.

This couldn't have happened just during shipping, so my assumption is that the package had sat for quite a while in a hot warehouse. Whatever the cause, there was no way I was going to use the product, and it wasn't practical to repackage it to return it.

As usual, Amazon came to the rescue. I called and described the problem , offering to send photos of the opened box and interior package. The Amazon rep agreed with me that it would be pointless to try returning the disaster to them, so he offered a simple, full refund.

If uncorrupted, the Con Queso is probably good stuff; I just didn't have the chance to find out.

Summary: Wonderful Sugar Free Flavoring! Highly Recommended!
Text:
The Kahlua Flavor is one of my favorite DaVinci Sugar Free Flavored Syrup types. This was a great find for me since I am a Type 2 diabetic and really have an overpowering sweet tooth.

We have tried quite a few of the different brands on the market, but have settled back to DaVinci since the flavors are good and they are sweetened with Splenda. Several of the other brands use Sorbitol (which my wife is slightly allergic to) or Maltitol (which causes me "gastric distress" in large quantities).

The real test for anything sugar free is if my kids will use it, and they all like the flavor enough to go out of their way for it. We have used this in coffee and in baking with great results.

Highly recommended!

My favorite coffee creamer years ago was a Kahlua flavored product, but it disappeared off the market refridgerator shelves, never to return!  So not only was I was thrilled to discover this Kahlua syrup, but it is sugar free as well.  That first cup of coffee in the morning has just gotten better at coaxing me out of bed.

Had purchased this years ago and didn't care for it, but thought now w/Splenda and the good reviews, it had to be good.  Wrong.  They get you to bite  w/the Kahlua on the label, but there is no comparison to Kahlua, doesn't taste at all like Kahlua.  Actually it doesn't really even taste like coffee.  It has just a sweet artificial flavor, but not a coffee flavor.  Very disappointing.

Recently I used this syrup in homemade ice cream. I put 1/2 cup of the Sugar-Free Kahlua, 1 cup heavy cream, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, and 1/4 cup sugar-free sweetener (you can use Splenda, Stevia, whatever you like) into a bowl, stirred well, and then poured the ice cream batter into ice cube trays. I froze them for four hours, let thaw for about half an hour, and then blended them in my food processor (a blender works) for a short time. Amazing results! The ice cream has a great coffee flavor without any kind of aftertaste. You would have thought that I added real coffee. I am so pleased that I am making two more batches of this stuff. This sweetener also works well in coffee and protein shakes.

My husband's  first cup of coffee in the morning has just gotten better thanks to Davinci. If you love the taste of Kahlua liquor, you are going to love Kahlua Sugar-Free Syrup. I have been using it in my coffee and I can not get over how much it tastes like Kahlua liquor. Of course without the liquor. This sweetener also works well in iced coffee.

Use for making lower calorie White Russians to replace the sugar content in real Kahlua. Also use fat free half and half. Not quite as good as the real thing, but close for the amount of calories saved. Downside is product is fairly expensive when having to add shipping. Not a bad price for the occasional drink, but would be too expensive if using regularly.

Summary: Da Vinci Sugar-Free Kahlua Syrup Smells Funny

Better to toss it out than find out later on that there is something wrong with my particular bottle. I won't buy this flavor again.

Sue

Stash's Lemon Ginger Caffeine Free Herbal Tea is a basic lemon ginger tea, tasting strongly of ginger, full of flavorings, and oddly, even contains soy. If you like your tea more subtle, with true pure tastes, and can discern complex differences between natural and commercial teas, then this definitely is not for you, and I would recommend any Numi tea, Yogi Tea, Traditional Medicinals, or even Stash's organic line of teas (which comes in a wonderful Lemon Ginger Organic Tea!)

Stash Lemon Ginger Tea contains ginger root, lemongrass, lemon flavor, safflower, hibiscus, citric acid, and soy.

Summary: Misnomer, but great noodles all the same!
Text:
These are NOT soba noodles.

But they are good! As the earlier reviewer correctly indicated, they're the same type as ramen noodles. Think of this as essentially a double-pack of plain ramen noodles, without the extra packaging and without the flavor packet.

I use them for a quick sukiyaki-type of meal for 2-3 people (with apologies to true Japanese food-lovers, who won't be impressed by the shortcuts):

1) Cook a package of these noodles separately according to package instructions, drain, and keep warm (can be done almost at the end of the remaining steps, so that both noodles and meat/veggie topping are done at the same time).
2) Brown 1/2 pound of hamburger, breaking it into smaller and smaller pieces as it cooks.
3) About midway through the browning, add 1 very large chopped Spanish onion (or two smaller chopped onions) and 1-3 ribs of chopped celery to the pan, and keep stirring to soften those as well by the time the hamburger is fully browned.
4) Remove the meat, onion and celery to a large bowl, keeping them warm, while draining all (or most of) the fat from the pan. In the same pan, quickly saute a package of sliced mushrooms (small or large package, your choice), using fat from the beef if desired or just a little tap water to keep the mushrooms from burning if, like me, you want to eliminate the fat.
5) Toward the end of the sauteeing of the mushrooms, add a bold amount of minced fresh garlic and minced fresh ginger (optional) to the pan, stirring frequently to keep them from burning as they soften with the mushrooms.
6) Once mushrooms are just about cooked through, add one package of fresh mung bean sprouts, and stir for a minute or so until they're warmed.
7) Add 2 small cans of beef broth or consomme or 1 larger can or carton to the pan; add ground garlic or ground ginger if desired in place of fresh if you had omitted either of them back in step 5, add soy sauce to taste, mix with the reserved beef, onion and celery while the broth warms, and serve over noodles. Yum! Great for leftovers, too.

Which brings me to the dill flavored Triscuits...

It's a combination of that wonderful Triscuit crunch, texture and flavor we have all grown to love combined with a perfect dill flavor. It is very yummy.

The caloric value yields 120 calories per serving and only 4 grams of fat.. but this is with a serving size of 6 crackers. You might be tempted to eat half of the box in one sitting as I almost have.. but be warned as a full box is 1080 calories and 36 grams of fat. yikes!

Summary: Beware of this product--one of our dogs died.
Text: You should monitor your dog very carefully if you give him/her these chews. One of our dogs died as a result of eating these chews, and the other three were very ill for two days. This product is very difficult for dogs to digest and can result in blocked intestines and infection. Since the package did not contain any warnings, we thought they were harmless. Be very careful if you buy these for your dog.

Summary: Great cat food.  It's a keeper!
Text:
All 3 of my cats love this food. They were previously on Wellness Turkey and when the cans were recalled I tried this on the suggestion of a family friend since their one cat has the same crystal issues our oldest does. He eats his prescription dry in the morning and this at night. Normally he's content to let the other two cats get to their food first and hold back with patience for his own, but with this it is the first time I have seen him muscle away the other two cats to eat. I'll be sticking with this and the turkey flavor.

Also there is no fish in this or the turkey flavor wet or dry foods which is excellent! My cats don't tend to enjoy food that has fish in it and this is one of the few foods I can find that is both good for them and has no fish. One of them does not like the peas in the food, he will eat around them, but one of the others eats them when he's done. So if your cat hates bits of veggies they may not really enjoy it as much.

Oh and one more point, it doesn't have that funky wet food smell a lot of other foods (even good ones) have. I really can't smell it once I stand up after putting it in the bowl.

Summary: Excellent choice for my finicky feline!
Text: Since my elderly cat has started eating a wet food diet, she's become extremely finicky. She used to eat anything I'd put in front of her, until about a year ago when she decided nothing was good enough.  I'd been through every brand in the store...she doesn't like fish, plain chicken or lamb so my choices were limited.  When I found this, I gave it a try since she primarily likes beef. The ingredients were excellent and I read great reviews from Vets about it online.  She has been scarfing this food down from day 1 and still loves it. There are peas and carrots in it and the  consistency of it is very mushy. She likes it that way, so she doesn't have to chew much. I also noticed it doesn't dry out if there's any left in her bowl for several hours, like other brands have.  I definitely plan to continue giving this to her. I've been ordering on Amazon since it's been difficult to find it in my local pet stores lately.

my cat is going to be morbidly obese. she loves this food so much it's almost dangerous to her health and my wallet. it looks and smells delicious. i would feel fine eating it myself. that's how wholesome and REAL it is. we get the dry food too- my cat is KING OF THE CASTLE. sigh..

Whole peas may seem appetizing to a human but to cats, they're junk food. Cats get all their nutrition by eating the whole animal. Cats have hard time digesting plant matter. This is closer to dog food than cat food since dog's physiology will allow digestion of many plant based food itms. My cats ate about half of the yellow goo around the peas and carrots. If you want a true holistic approach for cats, veggies gotta go.

Called a stew, but it's really a soft pate, and with big chunks of green beans and carrots.  Overall my cat seems to like it okay -- not a difficult task for him to work around the vegetables and leave them in the plate.

After my cat was diagnosed with renal failure, he refused to eat any of the canned versions of his vet prescribed food for kidney disease although he would eat Hill's Science Diet k/d dry food, but he was vomiting it up regularily. Since his diet requires low protein after searching online I finally found Spot's Stew. My cat really likes it and readily eats the chicken, turkey and salmon varieties. Granted sometimes he eats around the carrots, peas and green beans, but he does eat them. I really like that Spot's Stew is an all natural cat food with no by-products or fillers, and especially that it is an alternative for my cat that he really enjoys.

Summary: Dog Food Masquerading as Cat Food
Text:
My cat loved the dry version of spot's stew. When she was sick with a UTI, I purchased this in hopes of adding some additional fluid to her diet. When I dumped it in her bowel, she looked up at me as if I were mad, and I couldn't blame her. It is literally "stew," with whole chunks of peas, carrots, etc. in it. Cats are carnivores. I have owned several, and I have never seen one of them willingly eat a piece of fruit or vegetable, grain products excluded, that hadn't been completely ground up and disguised in something else.

She took one sniff and walked away. Of course, cats are unpredictable creatures and YMMV. But there are loads of good quality pate-style wet foods and all-meat wet foods that most cats are more likely to prefer.

Oh, this is some good cat food!
Have you ever opened a can of Friskies and gagged at the awful smell? How can your cat eat that?
This cat food smells pretty good, and it simply looks and smells like good food. My kittens made so much noise when I opened that can! They gobbled it right up, and I have to admit that it smelled pretty good.

This stuff looks disgusting, it really does. It's like meat soup that has been pureed. My cat goes nuts for it. She chirps her tiny cat meow at me whenever I get up in the morning and when I come home from work. I put her dry food in, that she used to love (will definitely switch to Spot's Stew dry next time I buy) and she looks at me like I'm evil. All she wants now is her succulent salmon.

I purchased this for my 15 year old cat who has health issues. Unfortunately, this cat decided after about 2 cans that she was not going to eat any more health food. She didn't eat the first cans very well even though I tried giving it in the morning when she's the hungriest and she licked a couple times and then followed me around meowing for something else. I finally gave up and gave it to the other cats. Two of the seven other cats will eat it but they leave the peas and anything else that is not mashed. So as far as I'm concerned it is great food, but the cats weren't impressed.

Summary: Wow! Cat Food That Seems Yummy!
Text: Wow! I have the pickiest cats in the whole universe.  The only wet food they eat is Spot's Stew Chicken.  I can get them to eat the Chicken/Beef flavor if I add some shaved Bonito but with three cats Slinky, Jester and Regal, only Slinky and Jester scarf the food down.  They will eat the chicken without the Bonito but Regal is another story.  She won't eat it at first but might come back later and eat some.  She will ONLY eat the Chicken and does not like Bonito so with her, it gets a little more tough.  However, this food is a wonderful consistency, smells good (to me the human) and I assume to the kitties as well because they LOVE this stuff.  For the vegetables, I don't know if cats really need them however, I mush them up with the meat and they don't notice.  If I miss mushing some, then yes they try to eat around the peas/carrots.  All I can say is thank goodness for this food.  I spent lots of money and time trying to find something they would like.  I also feed them a mix of Halo dry Sensitive Formula Turkey and Purina Dental Health.  In order to prevent urinary symptoms, I give my cats only fresh bottled water every day that I put in bowls all over the house.  With the good water, the good food and lots of petting, I have the happiest cats in Arizona!  Thank you Halo!!

I've been buying this for years and have no intention of switching to something else.  If you read the labels you'll see how good this stuff is.

My furry little friend, who happens not to enjoy eating and who has turned down many cat food brands, LOVES Spots Stew chicken.

The consistency and texture are soft and fluffy, much like mousse. I am gathering by the clean plate that the flavor is just the thing to get any picky little eater to ask for seconds.

I like all halo products but this canned cat food is just a little too soupy. My cats look at me with "What's this?" .
They like a little something to chew on.

I was surprised to find that the canned Halo cat food is low in protein - even lower than Science Diet wet KD for cats.  And my cat refuses to eat the Science Diet food anyway.  She loves this (turkey) and also the chicken and salmon.
This even smells good!!  Not like any other cat food I have ever purchased.  My cat dove into this and didn't look back.  She loved it.  I AM REORDERING because she is my little sweetie.
Our 2 fussy kitties hate any seafood but love beef with gravy, so we gave this a try & they licked the dish clean!
It's the best food my cat has loved for a long time, there's nothing left after I put it down and she craves it, I've a very happy cat!

Summary: Picky felines love this canned food
Text: My two cats somehow never figured out how to use their teeth to bite into their food--given dry food, they'll just use their tongues to lick it up and swallow the kernels whole, with an occasional bite with the teeth to crunch on food that's already been delivered into their mouths.  For a while I despaired of getting them to eat wet food, as they would just sit there and lick up all the juices, without getting much of the meat.  Typical canned food is just packed too tight, and the texture is not amenable for breaking off little bits with just their tongues.  Finally, I tried out Spot's Stew, which solved the problem.  This food is much looser, I think due to the inclusion of peas and other veggies, and the meat part is just the right consistency where they can lick it up successfully.  At first the cats would eat around the veggies, but they now lick up every morsel, and even prefer the Spot's Stew over the Wellness pouches.  I also like that the food doesn't contain any fish, as one of my cats is allergic to something or other (his back legs are always itchy, and he'll pull out the hair), and the vet suggested it might be fish.  Anyways, thank goodness for Spot's Stew, otherwise my teeth-challenged cats would never have been able to enjoy wet food!

I bought this dog food because the bag showed pictured of veggies and chunks of meat, and with a name like "Beneful" I thought I was purchasing a nutritious brand of dog food. My dogs did eat this food, but after reading the ingredients I completely regret purchasing it and feel just awful for feeding it to my dogs. The first three ingredients are Ground yellow corn, chicken by-product meal, and corn gluten meal. How disgusting is that?! The main ingredient is a corn filler. One thing my vet told me a while back that I never forgot: "When you eat corn, what comes out of the other end? The same thing happens with dogs." Basically, dogs cannot fully digest corn as they are carnivores. Corn it is just a cheap filler that can cause dogs to actually eat more to feel full, poop out more, and retain less nutrients. The only meat in Beneful at all is a by-product, its not even a real meat! By-products are the stuff leftover once all the actual meat is harvested. We're talking beaks, chicken feet, eyeballs, even chicken poop! I would not recommend this product to anyone, for any reason, ever. It is an absolutely awful dog food. I can't believe the pictures of veggies and full chunks of meat on the bag can be allowed to be on the packaging if the product does not contain the pictured items; it is very misleading and should be considered false advertising.

I recommend to stay far away from Beneful, and most Purina products. When purchasing a dog (or cat) food, the most important thing to consider is the first 3 ingredients; just make sure those first three are decent ingredients that you would eat yourself. Now that I know what to look for, I usually buy my pets all natural, foods such as Natural Balance, Blue Buffalo, Halo, or Wellness.

Text:
I have a small mixed-breed dog, about the size of a large chihuahua. She has always loved Beneful (just like my last dog who lived to a ripe old age), but she tended to only eat dry food when she became impatient for me to give her a little canned dog food. I would only give her small amounts of other food, wanting her to make her dry Beneful her main meal. I realized that the large dry food bites were probably too much work for her.

When I found out about the IncrediBites, I couldn't wait to give them a try. I have to admit that I was disappointed to only be able to find the 15.5 lb bags at the grocery store, because I have heard that dry dog food actually contains some moisture and large bags tend to get dry and stale if it takes you too long to use them. The good news is that the bag has a zip-loc closure, so that should help retain some moisture. If you have several dogs, 15.5 lbs may be fine for you, but I plan to order some smaller bags here on Amazon.

Anyway, my little dog now LOVES this new just-her-size kibble, and I probably fill her bowl about four times as often as I did with the larger pieces.

I gave this product 4 stars instead of 5 because I can't say for sure that this dog food is the healthiest dry dog food. My last dog was overweight, and I eventually had to switch her to the Healthy Weight flavor which she definitely did not like as well. That told me that the "regular" flavor has something really GOOD tasting in it. My daughter has three large dogs, and they too love Beneful. But two out of the three are overweight as well. So since I haven't done the research to determine how healthy Beneful is, I can't really make a judgment on that.

I tried feeding my dog something "healthy" and expensive from the pet store, but she wouldn't touch it. I suppose it's the same principle as when I choose a juicy hamburger over a turkey burger. All I know is that she gobbles the Beneful up. So for now, I will stick with what she loves, and she loves Beneful IncrediBites.

Summary: First Herbal Tea I've ever liked
Text:
I kept hearing great things about Rooibos tea, but couldn't find it ANYWHERE. I went to Nature's Market in a local Kroger and the only two teas they had with Rooibos was Red Lavender and Fireside. There was no straight Rooibos and this particular tea was on sale. I picked up one tin, thinking I wouldn't waste much money if I didn't like it. I brewed the first cup and thought it smelled more like perfume than tea. Moderately turned off by this, I bravely took a sip of the stuff - no sweetener or cream (as I usually add to my teas). I was amazed. I fell in love with the stuff and chugged it - despite it being moderately warm. I've also let it sit and drank it when it was cooler and still loved it. Then, I added sweetener and cream and suddenly it was a tasty dessert tea. I threw in half a pack of sweet n low one morning and made a replacement for my coffee.

I'm not sure what it is about this stuff, but I love it. It has a very unique flavor that's difficult to describe. It's a very smooth, slightly bold flavor with a somewhat sweet aftertaste.

I plan on trying their fireside, next - but not before I try adding some cinnamon directly to my Red Lavender tea, first.

Bread "Soldiers" with Marmite when you're ill, and Marmite and Peanut Butter sandwiches are the foods an empire was built on!

If you're trying to get an American to appreciate it, make sure they know it is savory and salty before they try it. My wife nearly threw up when trying it because she was expecting something like Nutella! I was so impressed when my local Safeway stocked it in the tiny English section of the "Foreign Foods" aisle, only to find it had gone again two months later. Obviously not enough demand in California, although I hear it has become a sought-after delicacy in New York. Now we just need a few New Yorkers to spread the word (and the Marmite!).

As the ad campaign in the UK said, you either love it or you hate it......

how could one improve on marmite? only by turning it upside down! now i can doodle elaborate designs on my toast before playing the cromwell and smooshing them into oblivion. or i can simply devour my creations as is, savoring that familiar marmite tang that is such a helpful alternative to honey or jam when one is trying to lose weight.
and true, i agree that winnie the pooh would simply hate marmite, but that's okay - all the more for me.

Summary: At last, great packaging that really works.
Text:
You either love Marmite or you don't. If you are reading this then you probably love it. There has always been the problem of what to do with the spoon that was used to remove some product from the jar. These squeezable bottles with the valve in the cap allow you to dispense the exact quantity desired without dribbles or long strings of Marmite. They are a great solution to an age old problem.

When the bottle is almost empty air blows out the cap valve. Loosen the cap and put the bottle in a microwave cap up for 7 seconds. That warms the contents enough to reduce it's viscosity and you can squirt the last drops of warm liquid out. I will be buying these jars from now on.

Summary: Good Product at a Good Price
Text:
After a lot of trial and error I have decided that Stevia is the best substitute sugar product for me. SweetLeaf is a good product because the Stevia is still in the powder form, not changed to a granulated form. Reading about stevia I found out that the basic powder or liquid form is better for your health and I find the taste just as good.
In our house we use SweetLeaf for coffee and tea, of course, but also cereal, oatmeal, fruit desserts and plain yogurt. We have not missed regular table sugar.
I've tried them all and this is the best.  I typically use this to sweeten berries,greek yogurt, oatmeal.  I've also used it in recipes.  It's very good.

I've been using Sweetleaf Sweetener for more years than I care to mention. They've perfected Stevia a great deal since the early days when I would dip a toothpick into the bottle and still use too much. It's still easy to use too much, and I've gotten pretty good at judging when a whole packet is called for or whether to sprinkle out less into my drink or whatever.

I grow Stevia, just because I grow herbs, and it's a nice plant to have, but I've not been successful at drying the leaves for my own use. Even when I grind them in the coffee grinder, the powder just floats on top of my drink.

There are controversies over the use of Stevia, just as there are over everything from eggs to green tea. I just know I can't use the artificial sweeteners like aspartame as they immediately give me migraines, as does anything sweetened with corn syrup. I sweeten with Agave Nectar, Stevia, local honey, and occasionally organic raw cane sugar. These work for me. Mostly it's just a matter of trial and error to find what works for each individual, but I would vouch for Sweetleaf Sweetener, and I try never to run out of it.
